explanation: Each different kind of plant, animal or organism represents a species, and the number of species known and described ranges between 1.7 and 1.8 million. This figure keeps changing because new organisms are continuously being identified.

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct

correct_answer: The number and kinds of organisms recorded increase as the area of observation increases
explanation: Increasing the area of observation increases the range and variety of organisms seen, and a dense forest shows a much greater number and kinds of organisms. Many organisms not visible to the naked eye are present everywhere, and new organisms keep being identified.

correct_answer: local names vary from place to place, even within a country
explanation: We know plants and animals of our own area by local names, and these vary from place to place even within a country. To avoid confusion, naming is standardised so that a particular organism is known by the same name all over the world; this process is nomenclature.

explanation: Organisms occupy extraordinary habitats from cold mountains to hot springs, about 1.7-1.8 million species are known and described, and many organisms around us are invisible to the naked eye. Statement III is wrong because new organisms keep being identified as new and old areas are explored.

source_page: NCERT section: Diversity in the Living World
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Biodiversity is the number and types of organisms on earth; each different kind represents a species; ICBN provides principles for naming plants; binomial nomenclature gives a name with a generic name and a specific epithet.

correct_answer: Increase in mass and increase in number of individuals
explanation: Increase in mass and increase in number of individuals are twin characteristics of growth. A multicellular organism grows by cell division.

correct_answer: Plants grow by cell division throughout their life span, whereas animals show growth only up to a certain age

correct_answer: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
explanation: Non-living objects such as mountains, boulders and sand mounds also increase in mass, so growth is not a defining property. However, it is the non-living objects that grow by accumulation of material on the surface; living organisms grow from inside. The reason is therefore false.

explanation: Yeast shows budding; Planaria (a flatworm) shows true regeneration of a lost part to form a new organism; the protonema of mosses multiplies by fragmentation; in unicellular organisms such as Amoeba, reproduction is synonymous with growth, that is, increase in number of cells.

source_page: NCERT section: What is living (characteristics of living organisms)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
explanation: In unicellular organisms such as bacteria, unicellular algae or Amoeba, growth by cell division is itself reproduction, so the two are synonymous. correct_answer: not a living thing, but surely a living reaction
explanation: Metabolism, the sum total of all chemical reactions in the body, is a defining feature of all living organisms. Isolated metabolic reactions in vitro are neither living nor non-living organisms; they are not living things but are surely living reactions.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: All organisms sense and respond to environmental cues, but the human being is the only organism that is aware of himself, that is, has self-consciousness.

source_page: NCERT section: What is living (characteristics of living organisms)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion

correct_answer: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
explanation: Living organisms are described as self-replicating, evolving and self-regulating interactive systems capable of responding to external stimuli. Isolated in vitro metabolic reactions are not living things, though they are living reactions, so the reason is false.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: They are not present in the constituent cells but arise from interactions among the constituent cells
explanation: Properties of tissues are not present in the constituent cells but arise as a result of interactions among them. correct_answer: R shows growth synonymous with reproduction, and P shows an increase in mass that is not growth from inside
explanation: A boulder increases in mass by accumulation on the surface, not from inside. A sterile worker bee is living though it does not reproduce. In Amoeba, increase in number of cells by division is both growth and reproduction.

source_page: NCERT section: What is living (characteristics of living organisms)

source_page: NCERT section: What is living (characteristics of living organisms)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Homo is the genus and sapiens is the specific epithet

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
explanation: Animal names follow ICZN. Scientific names ensure each organism has only one name and that such a name has not been used for any other known organism.

correct_answer: the two-word format was found convenient
explanation: The binomial system, with a generic name and a specific epithet, is practised worldwide; the two-word format was found convenient.

correct_answer: It must be correctly described, and named under ICBN with a name not used for any other known organism
explanation: Naming is possible only after correct description (identification). Plant names follow ICBN, and a scientific name must not have been used for any other known organism, so each organism has only one name.

explanation: ICBN is for plants and ICZN for animals. Both follow the universally accepted binomial format with a generic name and a specific epithet.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Systematics deals with the kinds and diversity of organisms and the relationships among them, and it now takes evolutionary relationships into account. correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
explanation: Linnaeus titled his publication Systema Naturae. The scope of systematics was later enlarged to include identification, nomenclature and classification, and it takes into account evolutionary relationships.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: The earliest classifications were based on uses of organisms. The scope of systematics was enlarged to include identification, nomenclature and classification. Both statements are incorrect.

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Insects share common features such as three pairs of jointed legs, so they are recognisable concrete objects that can be classified and were therefore given a rank or category. The reason explains the assertion.

correct_answer: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
explanation: Taxonomic groups or categories are distinct biological entities and not merely morphological aggregates. The reason contradicts this.

correct_answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
explanation: Species is the lowest category for all organisms. The category division is used for plants and phylum for animals, so Statement II is incorrect.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: knowledge of characters of an individual or group of organisms
explanation: Knowledge of characters helps identify similarities and dissimilarities among individuals of the same kind and of other kinds, which is needed to place organisms in categories.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Each category represents a rank, is a unit of classification and is termed a taxon
explanation: Since the category is part of the overall taxonomic arrangement, it is called a taxonomic category, and all categories form the taxonomic hierarchy. Each category, a unit of classification, represents a rank and is commonly termed a taxon (plural taxa).
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Moving up the hierarchy, members of a taxon share fewer characteristics. With fewer shared features, relationships to other taxa at the same level become harder to determine, making classification more complex.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: facilitate more sound and scientific placement of various taxa
explanation: The categories from species to kingdom are broad; sub-categories were developed to facilitate more sound and scientific placement of taxa.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: From highest to lowest: kingdom, phylum, class, order, then family, genus and species.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: The number of common characteristics among members of a taxon decreases
explanation: From species to kingdom, the number of common characteristics goes on decreasing, and relationships at the same level become harder to determine.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Categories are parts of the taxonomic arrangement and together constitute the hierarchy; groups represent categories and a category denotes rank. Plants use division where animals use phylum, so IV is wrong.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
explanation: Common characteristics decrease from species to kingdom, so Statement I is wrong. Members of lower taxa share more characteristics, so Statement II is correct.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Lower taxa share more characters, Animalia comprises all animal phyla, and sub-categories exist. Higher categories make relationships harder to determine, so III is wrong.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Taxonomic studies consider a group of individual organisms with fundamental similarities as a species, and one species should be distinguishable from closely related species by distinct morphological differences.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Mangifera indica is mango, Solanum tuberosum is potato, Panthera leo is lion and Homo sapiens is human being.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Panthera has another specific epithet, tigris; Solanum includes nigrum and melongena; humans are Homo sapiens; mango is Mangifera indica.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Solanum includes S. tuberosum (potato) and species such as nigrum and melongena. Pardus is the epithet of leopard, Panthera pardus.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: A genus is a group of related species with more characters in common than species of other genera; a family is a group of related genera with still less similarities; an order is an assemblage of families with a few similar characters; a class includes related orders.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Potato, tomato and brinjal are different species that all belong to the genus Solanum.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Lion (Panthera leo), leopard (P. pardus) and tiger (P. tigris), with several common features, belong to Panthera. Felis, which includes cats, is a different genus. Both are true, but the reason does not explain the assertion.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Panthera pardus is leopard and Panthera tigris is tiger; Felis includes cats; the dog belongs to family Canidae.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: A family is a group of related genera with still less similarities than genus and species, and plant families are characterised on the basis of both vegetative and reproductive features.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Solanum, Petunia and Datura are three different genera placed in the family Solanaceae.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
explanation: Panthera (lion, tiger, leopard) is placed along with Felis (cats) in family Felidae. Cat and dog show some similarities but are separated into Felidae and Canidae respectively. Both statements are incorrect.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Convolvulaceae and Solanaceae are included in the order Polymoniales mainly based on floral characters.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Polymoniales includes Convolvulaceae and Solanaceae; Carnivora includes Felidae and Canidae; Primata comprises monkey, gorilla and gibbon; Chordata includes fishes, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
explanation: An order, being higher, is an assemblage of families which exhibit a few similar characters; these are fewer than those among genera of a family. Orders are identified on aggregates of characters. The assertion is false and the reason true.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: The class category includes related orders: Primata (monkey, gorilla, gibbon) is placed in class Mammalia along with Carnivora (tiger, cat, dog). Mammalia has other orders also.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
explanation: Classes of fishes, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals constitute phylum Chordata, based on common features such as notochord and dorsal hollow neural system. The assertion is false and the reason true.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
explanation: In plants, classes are grouped into divisions; all animals of various phyla form kingdom Animalia. Both statements are correct.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Felidae and Canidae are both included in order Carnivora, so tiger and dog share the order. They also share class Mammalia, but order is the lowest shared category.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: The class category includes related orders; for example, class Mammalia includes Primata and Carnivora.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Genus Solanum: includes Petunia and Datura
explanation: Petunia and Datura are separate genera placed with Solanum in the family Solanaceae; they are not part of genus Solanum. The other pairings are correct.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Man belongs to Hominidae, housefly to Muscidae, mango to Anacardiaceae and wheat to Poaceae.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

source_page: NCERT section: Organisms with their taxonomic categories (Table 1.1)

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Man is in class Mammalia, housefly in Insecta, mango in Dicotyledonae and wheat in Monocotyledonae.

source_page: NCERT section: Organisms with their taxonomic categories (Table 1.1)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
explanation: Mango (Dicotyledonae) and wheat (Monocotyledonae) are both in division Angiospermae. Man is in phylum Chordata and housefly in Arthropoda, so Statement II is incorrect.

source_page: NCERT section: Organisms with their taxonomic categories (Table 1.1)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Mango is in Sapindales, housefly in Insecta and man in Hominidae. Wheat (Triticum aestivum) is in Poaceae; Anacardiaceae is the family of mango.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo101.pdf)
source_page: NCERT section: Organisms with their taxonomic categories (Table 1.1)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Mango (Mangifera indica) belongs to family Anacardiaceae, order Sapindales, class Dicotyledonae and division Angiospermae. Monocotyledonae is the class of wheat.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo101.pdf)
source_page: NCERT section: Organisms with their taxonomic categories (Table 1.1)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: They share the division Angiospermae but differ from the class level downwards
explanation: Mango: Anacardiaceae, Sapindales, Dicotyledonae, Angiospermae. Wheat: Poaceae, Poales, Monocotyledonae, Angiospermae. They share only the division and differ from class downwards.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo101.pdf)
source_page: NCERT section: Organisms with their taxonomic categories (Table 1.1)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Ascending order for housefly: genus Musca, family Muscidae, order Diptera, class Insecta, then phylum Arthropoda.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo101.pdf)
source_page: NCERT section: Organisms with their taxonomic categories (Table 1.1)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Muscidae, Diptera, Insecta and Arthropoda are the family, order, class and phylum of housefly, Musca domestica, whose genus is Musca.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo101.pdf)
source_page: NCERT section: Organisms with their taxonomic categories (Table 1.1)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Lion, leopard and tiger are Panthera species, Felis includes cats, and both genera are in Felidae. Felidae and Canidae are in order Carnivora, not Primata.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Housefly is in Arthropoda and man in Chordata, so the assertion is true. Their classes, Insecta and Mammalia, are correctly stated, but belonging to different classes does not by itself explain a difference in phylum, since many different classes lie within one phylum.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo101.pdf)
source_page: NCERT section: Organisms with their taxonomic categories (Table 1.1)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Aristotle used simple morphological characters and grouped plants into trees, shrubs and herbs. Divisions such as monocots and dicots or algae and bryophytes came much later.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Whether or not they had red blood
explanation: Aristotle divided animals into those which had red blood and those which did not. The vertebrate and invertebrate distinction is a later idea.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: In Linnaeus's time a two-kingdom system was developed, placing every organism in either Plantae or Animalia.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: The two-kingdom system lumped prokaryotes with eukaryotes, unicellular with multicellular forms, and photosynthetic green algae with non-photosynthetic fungi. Fungi were placed under plants, not animals.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Both statements are true. The wall composition difference is a further distinction that the two-kingdom system overlooked; it does not explain why fungi were grouped with plants.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Whittaker proposed the five-kingdom classification in 1969, with the kingdoms Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae and Animalia.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Monera have a noncellulosic wall of polysaccharide and amino acid, fungi have chitin, plants have cellulose, and animal cells lack a wall.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Protists show cellular organisation, fungi multicellular or loose tissue, plants tissue or organ level, and animals reach tissue, organ or organ system level.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Both Monera and Protista have cellular body organisation, whereas plants are organised at tissue or organ level. Only Protista among the two has a nuclear membrane.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Only Monera show chemosynthetic autotrophy along with photosynthetic and heterotrophic modes, and they are prokaryotic with a noncellulosic wall.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
explanation: Protista united Chlamydomonas and Chlorella, earlier placed in algae within plants and having cell walls, with Paramoecium and Amoeba, earlier in the animal kingdom and lacking walls. The reason is false.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
explanation: Both are drawbacks of earlier systems: prokaryotic bacteria and blue-green algae were placed with eukaryotic plants, and unicellular and multicellular forms such as Chlamydomonas and Spirogyra were grouped as algae.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: The three-domain system splits Monera into two domains and places all eukaryotic kingdoms in the third, giving a six-kingdom classification.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Whittaker's criteria were cell structure, thallus or body organisation, mode of nutrition, reproduction and phylogenetic relationships. Habitat was not a criterion.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Some protists have walls; only Monera lack a nuclear membrane; Plantae are photosynthetic autotrophs. Fungi have multicellular or loose tissue organisation, not organ systems.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
explanation: Aristotle used simple morphological characters. Linnaeus recognised only Plantae and Animalia, and bacteria were placed under plants.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Bacteria are grouped into four shapes: coccus is spherical, bacillus rod-shaped, vibrium comma-shaped and spirillum spiral.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Chemosynthetic bacteria help recycle N, P, Fe and S; heterotrophic bacteria are used to make curd; methanogens produce biogas from dung; cyanobacteria such as Nostoc fix nitrogen in heterocysts.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Halophiles live in extreme salty areas, thermoacidophiles in hot springs and methanogens in marshy areas. Cyanobacteria often form blooms in polluted water.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: The different cell wall structure of archaebacteria is responsible for their survival in extreme conditions, so the reason explains the assertion.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Eubacteria or true bacteria have a rigid cell wall and, if motile, a flagellum. Cyanobacteria are eubacteria. Extreme habitats characterise archaebacteria, and eubacteria are not confined to them.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
explanation: Cyanobacterial colonies are usually enclosed in a gelatinous sheath, and they frequently form blooms in polluted water bodies.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Oxidising inorganic substances such as nitrates, nitrites and ammonia
explanation: Chemosynthetic autotrophs oxidise inorganic substances such as nitrates, nitrites and ammonia and use the released energy for ATP production.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Chemosynthetic bacteria are autotrophs that oxidise inorganic compounds for energy and help recycle N, P, Fe and S. They do not use light.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
explanation: Some bacteria are pathogens causing cholera, typhoid and tetanus in humans and citrus canker in plants. Citrus canker is bacterial, so Statement II is incorrect.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Heterotrophic bacteria are the most abundant, mostly decomposers, and some are useful in curd making, antibiotics and nitrogen fixation in legume roots. Only some are pathogens.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Mycoplasma, which completely lack a cell wall, are the smallest living cells known. Viruses and viroids are smaller agents but are acellular.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Bacteria reproduce mainly by fission; under unfavourable conditions they may produce spores.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Bacteria also reproduce by a sort of sexual reproduction by adopting a primitive type of DNA transfer from one bacterium to another, so the reason explains the assertion.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
explanation: Bacteria reproduce mainly by fission, and under unfavourable conditions they produce spores. Both statements are incorrect.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Bacteria are the sole members of Monera and the most abundant micro-organisms; hundreds occur in a handful of soil.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
explanation: Mycoplasma are organisms that completely lack a cell wall; many are pathogenic in animals and plants. The reason is false.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Mycoplasma completely lack a cell wall, whereas eubacteria have a rigid cell wall
explanation: Eubacteria have a rigid cell wall, while Mycoplasma lack a wall completely. Mycoplasma are the smallest living cells and can survive without oxygen.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Cyanobacteria (blue-green algae) contain chlorophyll a, are photosynthetic autotrophs and some, like Nostoc and Anabaena, fix nitrogen in heterocysts.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Cyanobacteria are prokaryotic, unicellular, colonial or filamentous, with colonies surrounded by a gelatinous sheath, and they often form blooms in polluted water.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Methanogens, present in the gut of ruminants such as cows and buffaloes, are responsible for the production of methane (biogas) from dung.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Archaebacteria living in hot springs are thermoacidophiles; their distinct cell wall structure is responsible for survival in such extreme conditions.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: In Nostoc, the larger nitrogen-fixing heterocysts appear at intervals along the filament, and the colony is surrounded by a gelatinous (mucilaginous) sheath.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Bacteria show the most extensive metabolic diversity, live in extreme habitats and many are parasites. They are simple in structure but very complex in behaviour.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
explanation: Bacteria are the sole members of Monera, so Statement I is incorrect. Bacteria are the most abundant microbes, with hundreds in a handful of soil.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Protista includes chrysophytes, dinoflagellates, euglenoids, slime moulds and protozoans, all eukaryotic with a nucleus and organelles. Its boundaries are not well defined, and cyanobacteria are in Monera.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Both are true: protists are primarily aquatic and, being eukaryotes, form a link with plants, animals and fungi. Habitat does not explain this evolutionary link.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
explanation: Protists reproduce asexually and sexually by cell fusion and zygote formation, and some bear flagella or cilia.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: The chrysophyte group includes diatoms and golden algae (desmids).
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: In diatoms the walls form two thin overlapping shells fitting together like a soap box and are embedded with silica.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Diatom walls are indestructible because they are embedded with silica. Diatoms are also the chief producers in the oceans, but that does not explain wall durability.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Accumulated cell wall deposits of diatoms
explanation: Diatoms have left behind large amounts of cell wall deposits over billions of years; this diatomaceous earth is gritty and used in polishing and filtration of oils and syrups.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Diatoms are the chief producers in the oceans.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Chrysophytes live in fresh water and marine environments, are microscopic, planktonic and mostly photosynthetic. A pellicle is a euglenoid feature.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: The main pigments present in their cells
explanation: Dinoflagellates are mostly marine and photosynthetic; they appear yellow, green, brown, blue or red depending on the main pigments in their cells.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
explanation: Dinoflagellates have stiff cellulose plates on the wall surface. They are mostly marine and photosynthetic, so Statement II is incorrect.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: During red tides, the toxins released by the large numbers of dinoflagellates may even kill marine animals such as fishes, so the reason explains the assertion.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Diatoms have silica-embedded overlapping shells, dinoflagellates stiff cellulose plates, euglenoids a protein-rich pellicle, and slime mould spores possess true walls.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Two flagella, one short and one long
explanation: Euglenoids have two flagella, a short and a long one. The longitudinal and transverse arrangement belongs to dinoflagellates.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
explanation: Euglenoids are photosynthetic in sunlight but, when deprived of it, behave like heterotrophs by predating on smaller organisms. Their pigments are identical to those of higher plants, so the reason is false.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Instead of a cell wall, euglenoids have a protein-rich layer called the pellicle which makes the body flexible.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Fresh water organisms found in stagnant water
explanation: Majority of euglenoids are fresh water organisms found in stagnant water.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Slime moulds are saprophytic protists whose body moves along decaying twigs and leaves, engulfing organic material.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Slime moulds are saprophytic protists that move along decaying twigs and leaves engulfing organic material. Under suitable conditions they form an aggregation called plasmodium; under unfavourable conditions the plasmodium forms fruiting bodies bearing spores at their tips. The spores possess true walls, survive for many years and are dispersed by air currents.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
explanation: Slime mould spores possess true walls, are extremely resistant and survive many years even under adverse conditions. They are dispersed by air currents.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
explanation: Fruiting bodies form during unfavourable conditions, so the assertion is false. The spores do possess true walls and are extremely resistant.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Protozoans live as predators or parasites and are believed to be primitive relatives of animals.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Amoeba is amoeboid, Trypanosoma flagellated, Paramoecium ciliated and Plasmodium a sporozoan.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Trypanosoma causes sleeping sickness, Plasmodium causes malaria, Paramoecium has a gullet into which cilia steer food-laden water, and Amoeba captures prey with pseudopodia.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Amoeboid protozoans live in fresh water, sea water or moist soil; marine forms have silica shells on their surface.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
explanation: Pseudopodia are used by amoeboid forms like Amoeba. Paramoecium feeds through a gullet into which cilia steer food-laden water, so the assertion is false and the reason true.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Sporozoans have an infectious spore-like stage; Plasmodium, the malarial parasite, is the most notorious member.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Paramoecium is a free-living aquatic ciliate. Trypanosoma, Plasmodium and Entamoeba are parasites.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Dinoflagellates have cellulose wall plates, whereas euglenoids have a pellicle
explanation: Dinoflagellates are mostly marine with cellulose-plated walls and two flagella in longitudinal and transverse positions; euglenoids are mostly fresh water, have a pellicle, two flagella of unequal length and can become heterotrophic in darkness.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Amoeboid forms live in fresh water, sea water or moist soil; flagellates are free-living or parasitic; all protozoans are heterotrophs. Ciliates are actively moving because of thousands of cilia.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Albugo causes white spots on mustard leaves, Puccinia causes wheat rust, Penicillium is a source of antibiotics and yeast is used to make bread and beer.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Fungi prefer warm, humid places, and low temperature slows down their growth
explanation: Fungi prefer warm and humid places, so bread on a shelf in the monsoon is quickly colonised. Food is refrigerated because low temperature slows fungal and bacterial growth and so prevents spoilage; it does not kill all spores or keep them out.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: With the exception of yeasts, which are unicellular, fungi are filamentous with bodies made of hyphae.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Fungal bodies consist of thread-like hyphae; their network is the mycelium. Some hyphae are continuous multinucleate tubes called coenocytic hyphae, while others have septae or cross walls.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
explanation: Fungi can be saprophytes, parasites or symbionts; they form lichens with algae and mycorrhiza with roots of higher plants. Most fungi are saprophytes, so the reason is false.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Most fungi are heterotrophic, absorbing soluble organic matter from dead substrates; these are saprophytes.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Asexual spores are conidia, sporangiospores or zoospores; sexual spores are oospores, ascospores and basidiospores.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: The sexual cycle involves plasmogamy (fusion of protoplasms), then karyogamy (fusion of nuclei), then meiosis in the zygote giving haploid spores.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Plasmogamy is protoplasm fusion, karyogamy is nuclear fusion, a dikaryon has two nuclei per cell, and fruiting bodies are where reduction division forms haploid spores.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: In some fungi fusion of two haploid cells immediately gives diploid cells, but in ascomycetes and basidiomycetes a dikaryotic stage intervenes; later the nuclei fuse. The reason explains the assertion.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
explanation: Reduction division in fruiting bodies forms haploid spores. The dikaryotic stage is described for ascomycetes and basidiomycetes, not for all fungi.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Morphology of the mycelium, mode of spore formation and fruiting bodies
explanation: The morphology of the mycelium, mode of spore formation and fruiting bodies form the basis for dividing fungi into classes.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Phycomycetes have aseptate coenocytic mycelium, ascomycetes form endogenous ascospores in asci, basidiomycetes form four exogenous basidiospores, and deuteromycetes are known only by asexual conidia.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: In Phycomycetes, asexual reproduction is by motile zoospores or non-motile aplanospores, and a zygospore forms by gamete fusion. Conidia are produced exogenously on conidiophores in ascomycetes.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Mucor, Rhizopus (bread mould) and Albugo (parasite on mustard) are Phycomycetes.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
explanation: Phycomycete gametes may be isogamous, anisogamous or oogamous, and members occur in water, on moist decaying wood or as obligate plant parasites.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Albugo is a parasitic fungus on mustard placed with Mucor and Rhizopus in Phycomycetes.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Ascomycetes are sac fungi, deuteromycetes imperfect fungi, basidiomycetes include mushrooms, bracket fungi and puffballs, and Phycomycetes include Rhizopus.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Ascomycetes may be saprophytic, decomposers, parasitic or coprophilous, that is, growing on dung.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
explanation: Asexual conidia of ascomycetes are produced exogenously on conidiophores. Endogenous sporangial spores occur in Phycomycetes. The assertion is false, the reason true.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Neurospora is used in biochemical and genetic work, morels and truffles are edible delicacies, Saccharomyces (yeast) is a unicellular ascomycete, and asci are arranged in ascocarps.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Aspergillus, Claviceps and Neurospora are ascomycetes; Agaricus, the mushroom, is a basidiomycete.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Ascospores are produced endogenously in asci, whereas basidiospores are produced exogenously on basidia
explanation: Ascospores form endogenously inside sac-like asci; basidiospores form exogenously on basidia, four per basidium.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Mushrooms, bracket fungi and puffballs are commonly known basidiomycetes.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Sex organs are absent in basidiomycetes, but plasmogamy occurs through fusion of somatic cells of different strains; this explains the assertion.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Karyogamy and meiosis take place in the basidium, producing four basidiospores borne exogenously.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Somatic cells of different strains fuse (plasmogamy), giving a dikaryotic structure that ultimately forms a basidium, where karyogamy and meiosis produce exogenous basidiospores.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World
