source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo103.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Bryophyte sex organs are multicellular; antherozoids are released into water and reach the archegonium. The archegonium produces a single egg, and the sporophyte is attached to and nourished by the gametophyte.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo103.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Sphagnum is used as packing material because of its capacity to hold water. Some mosses do provide food for animals, but that does not explain the packing use.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo103.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Species of the moss Sphagnum are used as packing material for trans-shipment of living material because of their capacity to hold water.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo103.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
explanation: The main plant body of bryophytes is haploid and produces gametes, so it is called the gametophyte. Some cells of the sporophyte undergo reduction division to produce haploid spores. Both statements are correct.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo103.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Moist, shady places such as stream banks, marshy ground and tree bark
explanation: Liverworts grow usually in moist, shady habitats such as banks of streams, marshy ground, damp soil, bark of trees and deep in the woods.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo103.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: The plant body of a liverwort is thalloid, for example Marchantia; the thallus is dorsiventral and closely appressed to the substrate.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo103.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: fragmentation of thalli or formation of gemmae
explanation: Asexual reproduction in liverworts takes place by fragmentation of thalli, or by the formation of specialised structures called gemmae.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo103.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Marchantia has a dorsiventral thallus closely appressed to the substrate; leafy members have tiny leaf-like appendages in two rows; gemmae develop in gemma cups; the sporophyte has foot, seta and capsule.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo103.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
explanation: In liverworts, male and female sex organs are produced either on the same or on different thalli, so Statement I is wrong. The sporophyte is differentiated into foot, seta and capsule.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo103.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
explanation: Gemmae are green, multicellular asexual buds that develop in gemma cups on the thallus and detach to form new individuals. Spores, not gemmae, are formed after meiosis in the capsule.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo103.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Gemmae are green, multicellular, asexual buds that develop in small receptacles called gemma cups on the thalli; they detach and germinate into new individuals.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo103.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
explanation: The protonema develops directly from a spore. It is the leafy stage that develops from the secondary protonema as a lateral bud. So the reason is false.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo103.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: The leafy stage arises from the secondary protonema as a lateral bud, is attached by multicellular branched rhizoids and bears the sex organs. The sporophyte has foot, seta and capsule.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo103.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: upright, slender axes bearing spirally arranged leaves
explanation: The leafy stage of mosses consists of upright, slender axes bearing spirally arranged leaves.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo103.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: fragmentation and budding in the secondary protonema
explanation: Vegetative reproduction in mosses is by fragmentation and budding in the secondary protonema.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo103.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
explanation: In mosses the sex organs are produced at the apex of the leafy shoots. The moss sporophyte is more elaborate than that of liverworts, so Statement II is incorrect.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo103.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: The protonema is the creeping filamentous stage from a spore; the leafy stage bears spiral leaves and sex organs; the capsule contains spores formed after meiosis; moss rhizoids are multicellular and branched.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo103.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Common examples of mosses are Funaria, Polytrichum and Sphagnum.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo103.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Liverworts: asexual reproduction by gemmae; Mosses: elaborate mechanism of spore dispersal
explanation: Liverworts reproduce asexually by fragmentation and gemmae. Mosses have a more elaborate sporophyte than liverworts and an elaborate mechanism of spore dispersal.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo103.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: The leafy stage bears sex organs and mosses have an elaborate spore dispersal mechanism. Moss rhizoids are multicellular and branched, and spores are formed after meiosis.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo103.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Pteridophytes include horsetails and ferns; they are used for medicinal purposes and as soil-binders and are frequently grown as ornamentals. They are the first terrestrial plants with xylem and phloem.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo103.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: The sporangia of pteridophytes produce spores by meiosis in spore mother cells.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo103.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
explanation: Pteridophytes are found in cool, damp, shady places, though some flourish in sandy-soil conditions. They are used for medicinal purposes and as soil-binders. Both statements are incorrect.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo103.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Pteridophytes are classified into Psilopsida (Psilotum), Lycopsida (Selaginella, Lycopodium), Sphenopsida (Equisetum) and Pteropsida (Dryopteris, Pteris, Adiantum).
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo103.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Equisetum, a horsetail, is placed in Sphenopsida.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo103.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Dryopteris, Pteris and Adiantum are members of Pteropsida. Lycopodium belongs to Lycopsida.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo103.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Leaves are small (microphylls) as in Selaginella or large (macrophylls) as in ferns. Homosporous plants produce spores of similar kind; heterosporous plants produce macro and micro spores.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo103.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
explanation: The sporophytes bear sporangia subtended by sporophylls. Spores are produced by meiosis in spore mother cells, so the reason is false.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo103.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: In some cases sporophylls form distinct compact structures called strobili or cones, as in Selaginella and Equisetum.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo103.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Because of the specific restricted requirement of the gametophytes and the need for water for fertilisation, the spread of living pteridophytes is limited to narrow geographical regions.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo103.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
explanation: Spores germinate to give rise to inconspicuous, small but multicellular, free-living, mostly photosynthetic thalloid gametophytes called prothallus. Both statements are correct.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo103.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: transfer of antherozoids to the mouth of the archegonium
explanation: Water is required for transfer of antherozoids, the male gametes released from the antheridia, to the mouth of the archegonium.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo103.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: The sporophyte forms spores by meiosis; spores germinate into the prothallus, which bears sex organs; antherozoids reach the archegonium through water; the zygote develops into the dominant sporophyte.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo103.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Pteridophyte gametophytes bear male and female sex organs called antheridia and archegonia.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo103.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Embryo development within a female gametophyte retained on the sporophyte
explanation: In Selaginella and Salvinia, the female gametophytes are retained on the parent sporophytes and zygotes develop into young embryos within them. This event is a precursor to the seed habit.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo103.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Megaspores and microspores give rise to female and male gametophytes respectively, and the female gametophytes are retained on the parent sporophytes for variable periods. In the majority of pteridophytes all spores are of similar kind.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo103.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Selaginella and Salvinia produce macro and micro spores and are heterosporous; their female gametophytes are retained on the parent sporophyte.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo103.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
explanation: In pteridophytes the main plant body is the dominant sporophyte, differentiated into true root, stem and leaves with well-differentiated vascular tissues. It is not dependent on the gametophyte. Only Statement II is correct.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo103.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Sporophylls are leaf-like appendages subtending sporangia and may form compact strobili. The prothallus is the free-living thalloid gametophyte. Megaspores germinate into female gametophytes.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo103.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Lycopodium is in Lycopsida, Adiantum in Pteropsida and Salvinia is heterosporous. Psilotum belongs to Psilopsida; Sphenopsida contains Equisetum.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo103.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: their ovules lack an ovary wall, so the seeds formed later also stay uncovered
explanation: In gymnosperms (gymnos: naked, sperma: seeds) the ovules are not enclosed by any ovary wall and remain exposed both before and after fertilisation. The seeds that develop post-fertilisation are not covered.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo103.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: One of the gymnosperms, the giant redwood tree Sequoia, is one of the tallest tree species.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo103.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Pinus roots have mycorrhiza; Cycas has coralloid roots with N2-fixing cyanobacteria; the Cycas stem is unbranched; conifer leaves are needle-like, reducing surface area.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo103.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Both statements are true, but the mycorrhiza of Pinus does not explain the coralloid roots of Cycas.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo103.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
explanation: In conifers the needle-like leaves reduce the surface area, and a thick cuticle and sunken stomata help reduce water loss. The assertion is false and the reason is true.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo103.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Microsporangiate (male) strobili bear microsporophylls with microsporangia; macrosporangiate (female) strobili bear megasporophylls with ovules. The pollen grain is the highly reduced male gametophyte. The ovule is the nucellus protected by envelopes.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo103.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
explanation: Male and female cones may be borne on the same tree, as in Pinus. In Cycas, male cones and megasporophylls are borne on different trees. Only Statement II is correct.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo103.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: The megaspore mother cell differentiates from a nucellus cell and divides meiotically into four megaspores. One megaspore develops into the multicellular female gametophyte bearing two or more archegonia. After fertilisation the ovule develops into a seed.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo103.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Pollen grains released from the microsporangium are carried in air currents to the opening of ovules. The pollen tube then grows towards the archegonia. Both are true, but the second does not explain the first.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo103.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: discharges its contents near the mouth of the archegonia
explanation: The pollen tube carrying the male gametes grows towards the archegonia in the ovules and discharges its contents near the mouth of the archegonia.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo103.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Cycas pinnate leaves persist for a few years; Pinus and Cedrus have branched stems; roots are generally tap roots. The female gametophyte bears two or more archegonia.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo103.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Gymnosperm leaves are adapted to withstand extremes of temperature, humidity and wind. Needle-like leaves reduce surface area, and thick cuticle and sunken stomata reduce water loss.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo103.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Pteridophytes: free-living prothallus; Gymnosperms: gametophytes retained within sporangia on the sporophyte
explanation: Unlike bryophytes and pteridophytes, gymnosperm male and female gametophytes do not have an independent free-living existence; they remain within the sporangia retained on the sporophytes.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo103.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Cycas has an unbranched stem, coralloid roots with N2-fixing cyanobacteria, and bears male cones and megasporophylls on different trees.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo103.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: The organ level of organisation is found in members of Platyhelminthes and other higher phyla, where tissues are grouped into organs. Coelenterates remain at the tissue level and sponges at the cellular level.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo104.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Annelids, arthropods, molluscs, echinoderms and chordates show an organ system level of organisation. Coelenterates show only the tissue level.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo104.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Platyhelminthes have an incomplete digestive system with only one opening. A complete digestive system with two openings, mouth and anus, is seen from Aschelminthes onward.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo104.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
explanation: In open circulation blood leaves the heart and bathes cells and tissues directly. In closed circulation blood stays within arteries, veins and capillaries.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo104.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Arthropods and hemichordates have an open type of circulatory system. In such a system the blood is not confined to vessels; it is pumped by the heart into open spaces, so the cells and tissues are directly bathed in it. The Reason therefore explains the Assertion.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo104.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Balanoglossus is a hemichordate and hemichordates have an open circulatory system. Annelids, cyclostomes and other chordates have closed circulation.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo104.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Sponges are mostly asymmetrical: any plane passing through the centre does not divide them into equal halves.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo104.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Coelenterates are diploblastic. Platyhelminthes are triploblastic acoelomates, Aschelminthes are triploblastic pseudocoelomates and annelids are triploblastic coelomates.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo104.pdf)
source_page: NCERT section: Diploblastic and Triploblastic Organisation; Coelom
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: The diagram describes radial symmetry, seen in coelenterates, ctenophores and adult echinoderms. Aurelia is a coelenterate and is radially symmetrical.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo104.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo104.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Triploblastic animals develop from three germ layers; the mesoderm lies between ectoderm and endoderm. Platyhelminthes to chordates are triploblastic.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo104.pdf)
source_page: NCERT section: Diploblastic and Triploblastic Organisation
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: Animals without a body cavity are acoelomates, for example Platyhelminthes. Fasciola, the liver fluke, is a flatworm.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo104.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 1: Diversity in Living World

explanation: In most dicots the radicle elongates into a primary root bearing secondary and tertiary roots; this tap root system is seen in mustard. Wheat, a monocot, shows a fibrous root system.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: It is short-lived and is replaced by many roots from the stem base
explanation: In monocots such as wheat the primary root is short-lived and is replaced by a large number of roots that originate from the base of the stem, forming the fibrous root system.
source_document: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Official Syllabus (NEET_UG_2026_Official_Syllabus.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: They bear roots arising from parts of the plant other than the radicle
explanation: Roots that arise from parts of the plant other than the radicle are adventitious roots; grass, Monstera and the banyan tree are the examples given for them.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: The root system absorbs water and minerals, anchors the plant, stores reserve food and synthesises plant growth regulators. Bearing and spreading branches with leaves, flowers and fruits is the main function of the stem.
source_document: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Official Syllabus (NEET_UG_2026_Official_Syllabus.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: The root is covered at the apex by a thimble-like root cap, which protects the tender apex as the root pushes through the soil.
source_document: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Official Syllabus (NEET_UG_2026_Official_Syllabus.pdf)
source_page: NCERT section: Regions of the Root
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: very small and thin-walled, with dense protoplasm, dividing repeatedly
explanation: The region of meristematic activity lies a few millimetres above the root cap; its cells are very small, thin-walled, have dense protoplasm and divide repeatedly.
source_document: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Official Syllabus (NEET_UG_2026_Official_Syllabus.pdf)
source_page: NCERT section: Regions of the Root
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: From the tip: root cap, then the region of meristematic activity a few millimetres above it, then the region of elongation formed by cells proximal to it, and finally the region of maturation where cells differentiate and root hairs arise.
source_document: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Official Syllabus (NEET_UG_2026_Official_Syllabus.pdf)
source_page: NCERT section: Regions of the Root
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Cells proximal to the meristematic region undergo rapid elongation and enlargement, and this is what makes the root grow in length; so the reason explains the assertion.
source_document: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Official Syllabus (NEET_UG_2026_Official_Syllabus.pdf)
source_page: NCERT section: Regions of the Root
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Carrot has a swollen tap root, sweet potato has swollen adventitious roots, maize has stilt roots from the lower nodes, and Rhizophora has pneumatophores that help it get oxygen for respiration.
source_document: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Official Syllabus (NEET_UG_2026_Official_Syllabus.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Incorrect; these stilt roots arise from stem nodes, so they are adventitious
explanation: Stilt roots of maize and sugarcane arise from the lower nodes of the stem. Since they do not come from the radicle, they are adventitious roots and do not make a tap root system.
source_document: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Official Syllabus (NEET_UG_2026_Official_Syllabus.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
explanation: Maize and sugarcane have supporting stilt roots from the lower nodes of the stem, and banyan is supported by hanging prop roots. Both statements are correct.
source_document: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Official Syllabus (NEET_UG_2026_Official_Syllabus.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
explanation: Rhizophora bears pneumatophores that grow vertically upward out of the swampy soil; their role is to help the plant get oxygen for respiration, not food storage.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
explanation: Potato is a modified underground stem, but the swollen part of sweet potato is an adventitious root that stores food. The assertion is false and the reason is true.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Carrot and turnip have storage tap roots, whereas sweet potato has storage adventitious roots. Stilt roots of maize and sugarcane arise from lower nodes, and pneumatophores of Rhizophora help in obtaining oxygen.
source_document: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Official Syllabus (NEET_UG_2026_Official_Syllabus.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
explanation: Grass is an example of adventitious roots, which arise from parts other than the radicle. In monocots the primary root is short-lived and is replaced by many roots from the base of the stem. Both statements are incorrect.
source_document: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Official Syllabus (NEET_UG_2026_Official_Syllabus.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Prop roots hang down to support banyan; stilt roots arise from lower stem nodes of maize
explanation: Both are supporting roots. Prop roots are the hanging structures that support the banyan tree, while stilt roots of maize and sugarcane come out of the lower nodes of the stem.
source_document: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Official Syllabus (NEET_UG_2026_Official_Syllabus.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Adventitious roots arise from parts other than the radicle, root hairs come from epidermal cells in the zone of maturation, and pneumatophores help in respiration. Meristematic cells are very small, thin-walled and have dense protoplasm.
source_document: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Official Syllabus (NEET_UG_2026_Official_Syllabus.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: It is generally green when young and later often becomes woody and dark brown
explanation: The stem develops from the plumule, bears nodes and internodes, and is generally green when young, often becoming woody and dark brown later.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Nodes bear leaves, internodes lie between nodes, the axillary bud in the leaf axil grows into a branch, and the stem develops from the plumule of the germinating seed.
source_document: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Official Syllabus (NEET_UG_2026_Official_Syllabus.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: The main function of the stem is spreading out branches bearing leaves, flowers and fruits; it conducts water, minerals and photosynthates, and some stems store food, give support, protect or help in vegetative propagation.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: In arid regions Opuntia has a flattened stem and Euphorbia a fleshy cylindrical one, both photosynthetic. Citrus bears thorns and cucumber, a gourd, bears stem tendrils; both come from axillary buds.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: In mint and jasmine a slender lateral branch from the base of the main axis grows in the air for some time and then arches down to touch the ground.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
explanation: Thorns are woody, straight, pointed modified axillary buds that protect against browsing animals. Opuntia has a flattened stem that contains chlorophyll and photosynthesises; the fleshy cylindrical stem is Euphorbia.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Potato, ginger, turmeric, zaminkand and Colocasia are underground stems that store food and act as organs of perennation. Sweet potato is a root modification.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Thorns are modified axillary buds; cactus spines are modified leaves

source_document: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Official Syllabus (NEET_UG_2026_Official_Syllabus.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Some arid-region plants modify their stems into flattened (Opuntia) or fleshy cylindrical (Euphorbia) structures that contain chlorophyll and carry out photosynthesis. The reason explains the assertion.
source_document: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Official Syllabus (NEET_UG_2026_Official_Syllabus.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: spread to new niches, forming new plants when older parts die

source_document: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Official Syllabus (NEET_UG_2026_Official_Syllabus.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Opuntia has a flattened stem and Euphorbia a fleshy cylindrical one. Stem tendrils and thorns both come from axillary buds, and stems bear terminal or axillary buds.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Leaves arise from the shoot apical meristem and are arranged in acropetal order, the youngest being nearest the apex.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: The leaf base may bear two small lateral stipules; in monocots it expands into a sheath; in some legumes it swells into a pulvinus. The middle prominent vein of the lamina is the midrib.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Assertion is true, but Reason is false

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: give rigidity to the blade and transport water, minerals and food
explanation: Veins provide rigidity to the leaf blade and act as channels of transport for water, minerals and food materials.
source_document: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Official Syllabus (NEET_UG_2026_Official_Syllabus.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
explanation: The leaf base forms a sheath in monocots and may be swollen into a pulvinus in some leguminous plants. Both statements are correct.
source_document: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Official Syllabus (NEET_UG_2026_Official_Syllabus.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: In a compound leaf incisions reach the midrib to form leaflets; in a simple leaf they do not touch it
explanation: A leaf is simple when its lamina is entire or its incisions do not touch the midrib. When incisions reach the midrib and break the lamina into leaflets, the leaf is compound.

correct_answer: Only the whole axis, not each unit, has a bud in its axil
explanation: A bud is present in the axil of the petiole of both simple and compound leaves, but not in the axils of leaflets. If the units lack axillary buds while the whole axis has one, it is a compound leaf.

explanation: Neem has a pinnately compound leaf and silk cotton a palmately compound leaf. Alstonia shows whorled phyllotaxy and Calotropis shows opposite phyllotaxy.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion

correct_answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: expanded green petioles, the leaves being small and short-lived

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Leaves become tendrils in peas, spines in cacti, fleshy food-storing leaves in onion and garlic, and insect-catching structures in pitcher plant and venus-fly trap.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

source_page: NCERT section: Venation; Types of Leaves
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Racemose: acropetal succession; cymose: basipetal order

correct_answer: Assertion is false, but Reason is true

correct_answer: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
explanation: In cereals such as maize the seed coat is membranous and generally fused with the fruit wall. The endosperm is bulky and stores food, so maize seed is endospermic.

correct_answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect

correct_answer: Small, in a groove at one end of the endosperm
explanation: In maize the endosperm is bulky and stores food. The embryo is small and situated in a groove at one end of the endosperm, separated from it by the proteinous aleurone layer.

explanation: Within the seed coat is the embryo with an embryonal axis and two cotyledons, often fleshy with reserve food; radicle and plumule lie at its two ends. The hilum is a scar and the micropyle is a small pore above it.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Castor is an endospermous dicot seed and pea a non-endospermous one. Monocot seeds such as maize are generally endospermic, while orchids are non-endospermic.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: The embryo has one cotyledon in wheat and maize and two in gram and pea. The coleoptile encloses the plumule and the coleorhiza the radicle. Castor endosperm is formed by double fertilisation.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Two fleshy cotyledons with no endosperm in the mature seed indicate a non-endospermous dicot seed such as bean, gram or pea; the scar is the hilum and the pore above it the micropyle.

correct_answer: The position of the mother axis with respect to the flower

correct_answer: Four free sepals in two whorls, four free petals, six free stamens in two whorls, two fused carpels
explanation: Plus signs show members in separate whorls and a bracket shows fusion. So K2+2 is four free sepals in two whorls, C4 four free petals, A2+4 six free stamens in two whorls and G(2) two fused carpels.
