correct_answer: Papilionoideae, a subfamily of the family Leguminosae
explanation: Fabaceae was earlier called Papilionoideae, a subfamily of the family Leguminosae; it is distributed all over the world.
source_document: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Official Syllabus (NEET_UG_2026_Official_Syllabus.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: In Fabaceae, Indigofera gives dye, sunhemp gives fibre, Sesbania and Trifolium are fodder, and muliathi is medicinal. Gram, arhar, sem, moong and soyabean are pulses; soyabean and groundnut give edible oil.
source_document: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Official Syllabus (NEET_UG_2026_Official_Syllabus.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Fabaceae includes trees, shrubs and herbs with root nodules; the stem is erect or climber; leaves are alternate, pinnately compound or simple, with pulvinate base, stipules and reticulate venation.
source_document: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Official Syllabus (NEET_UG_2026_Official_Syllabus.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Fabaceae has ten diadelphous stamens, nine fused and one free, written A(9)+1. The anthers are dithecous, which is true but does not explain the grouping of stamens.
source_document: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Official Syllabus (NEET_UG_2026_Official_Syllabus.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: ovary superior, monocarpellary, unilocular with many ovules, style single
explanation: In Fabaceae the ovary is superior, monocarpellary and unilocular with many ovules, and the style is single; the fruit is a legume.
source_document: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Official Syllabus (NEET_UG_2026_Official_Syllabus.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
explanation: Fabaceae has five gamosepalous sepals with imbricate aestivation, and its seeds (one to many) are non-endospermic. Both statements are incorrect.
source_document: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Official Syllabus (NEET_UG_2026_Official_Syllabus.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: One posterior standard, two lateral wings and two anterior petals forming a keel
explanation: Fabaceae has a papilionaceous corolla of five petals: a posterior standard, two lateral wings and two anterior petals forming a keel that encloses the stamens and pistil. Only the keel pair is bracketed.
source_document: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Official Syllabus (NEET_UG_2026_Official_Syllabus.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Solanaceae is a large family commonly called the potato family, widely distributed in tropics, subtropics and even temperate zones.
source_document: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Official Syllabus (NEET_UG_2026_Official_Syllabus.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: In Solanaceae, tomato, brinjal and potato are food; chilli is a spice; belladonna and ashwagandha are medicinal; tobacco is fumigatory; petunia is ornamental.
source_document: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Official Syllabus (NEET_UG_2026_Official_Syllabus.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Solanaceae has five united, persistent sepals with valvate aestivation. Number, union and aestivation are separate facts and do not explain persistence.
source_document: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Official Syllabus (NEET_UG_2026_Official_Syllabus.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Solanaceae flowers are bisexual and actinomorphic, with five epipetalous stamens and a bicarpellary syncarpous superior ovary, bilocular with a swollen placenta and many ovules, axile. Fruit is a berry or capsule and seeds are many and endospermous.
source_document: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Official Syllabus (NEET_UG_2026_Official_Syllabus.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: leaves stipulate with a pulvinate leaf base
explanation: Solanaceae leaves are alternate, simple, rarely pinnately compound, exstipulate with reticulate venation. Stipulate leaves with a pulvinate base belong to Fabaceae.
source_document: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Official Syllabus (NEET_UG_2026_Official_Syllabus.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
explanation: Solanaceae fruits are berries or capsules; legumes belong to Fabaceae. Solanaceae stems are mostly herbaceous and aerial, with an underground stem in potato (Solanum tuberosum).
source_document: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Official Syllabus (NEET_UG_2026_Official_Syllabus.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Liliaceae members are perennial herbs with underground bulbs, corms or rhizomes; leaves are mostly basal, alternate, linear, exstipulate with parallel venation; inflorescence is solitary or cymose, often in umbellate clusters; fruit a capsule, rarely a berry.
source_document: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Official Syllabus (NEET_UG_2026_Official_Syllabus.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: In Liliaceae, tulip and Gloriosa are ornamentals, Aloe is medicinal, Asparagus is a vegetable, and Colchicum autumnale is the source of colchicine.
source_document: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Official Syllabus (NEET_UG_2026_Official_Syllabus.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Br, actinomorphic, bisexual, P(3+3) A3+3 G(3), ovary superior
explanation: Liliaceae flowers are bracteate, actinomorphic and bisexual, with six tepals (3+3) often united, six stamens (3+3) and a tricarpellary syncarpous superior ovary: Br P(3+3) A3+3 G(3).
source_document: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Official Syllabus (NEET_UG_2026_Official_Syllabus.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
explanation: Liliaceae is trimerous with a perianth of six tepals (3+3), often united into a tube, with valvate aestivation. A distinct calyx and corolla of five each is not a Liliaceae feature.
source_document: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Official Syllabus (NEET_UG_2026_Official_Syllabus.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Both families have a syncarpous superior ovary with axile placentation: bicarpellary and bilocular in Solanaceae, tricarpellary and trilocular in Liliaceae.
source_document: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Official Syllabus (NEET_UG_2026_Official_Syllabus.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Fabaceae has a monocarpellary unilocular ovary with many ovules; Solanaceae a bicarpellary bilocular ovary with a swollen placenta; Liliaceae a tricarpellary trilocular ovary; mustard a parietal ovary made two-chambered by a false septum.
source_document: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Official Syllabus (NEET_UG_2026_Official_Syllabus.pdf)
source_page: NCERT section: Description of Some Important Families; Gynoecium
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Anatomy is the study of the internal structure of plants. Morphology deals with external form, taxonomy with classification and physiology with functions.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: have a common origin and usually perform a common function
explanation: A tissue is a group of cells having a common origin and usually performing a common function. A plant body is built of several kinds of tissues.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
explanation: Meristematic and permanent tissues are separated on the basis of whether the cells formed can divide. Among permanent tissues, those with all cells similar in structure and function are simple tissues; those with many types of cells are complex tissues.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Apical meristems at root and shoot tips produce primary tissues. The root apical meristem is at the root tip and the shoot apical meristem at the distant most region of the stem axis. Axillary buds arise from cells left behind by the shoot apical meristem, not the root apical meristem.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Some cells left behind from the shoot apical meristem during leaf formation and stem elongation constitute the axillary bud, present in leaf axils and capable of forming a branch or a flower.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: The meristem occurring between mature tissues is the intercalary meristem. In grasses it regenerates parts removed by grazing herbivores, so the Reason explains the Assertion.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Apical and intercalary meristems are primary because they appear early in the life of the plant and contribute to the primary plant body. Their occurrence in grasses is true but is not the reason they are called primary.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
explanation: Lateral (secondary) meristems are cylindrical, occur in the mature regions of roots and shoots of many plants, especially those with a woody axis, and produce secondary tissues. Tips of roots and shoots bear apical meristems.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Root apical meristem is at the root tip and shoot apical meristem at the distant most region of the stem axis. Intercalary meristem lies between mature tissues, as in grasses. Lateral meristem is cylindrical, in mature regions, and produces secondary tissues.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Lateral meristems produce secondary tissues and appear later than primary meristems. Intercalary meristem is a primary meristem. Axillary buds can form a branch or a flower.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
explanation: Following divisions in both primary and secondary meristems, the new cells specialise and lose the ability to divide, forming permanent tissues. So permanent tissues arise from secondary meristems too.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: dermal tissues, ground tissues and vascular tissues
explanation: During primary body formation, specific regions of the apical meristem give rise to dermal, ground and vascular tissues. Secondary tissues are produced by lateral meristems.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: The secondary or lateral meristem is cylindrical, appears later than primary meristems and occurs in mature regions of roots and shoots of many plants, particularly those with a woody axis.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Apical and intercalary meristems are primary meristems because they appear early and build the primary plant body. The lateral meristem is the secondary meristem that appears later and produces secondary tissues.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: It is wrong; they appear early and contribute to the primary plant body
explanation: Apical and intercalary meristems are primary meristems because they appear early in the life of the plant and contribute to the formation of the primary plant body. Position between mature tissues does not make them secondary.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Apical: primary, at tips, increases length; Lateral: secondary, cylindrical, increases girth
explanation: Apical meristems at root and shoot tips are primary and add length. Lateral meristems are secondary, cylindrical and add girth by producing secondary tissues.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: A simple tissue is made of only one type of cells, for example parenchyma, collenchyma and sclerenchyma. Complex tissues have more than one type of cells working together.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
explanation: Parenchyma, not collenchyma, forms the major component within organs. Collenchyma occurs in layers below the epidermis in dicotyledonous plants, as a homogeneous layer or in patches.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Parenchyma cells are generally isodiametric with thin cellulose walls and may be closely packed or have small intercellular spaces. Thick lignified walls with pits belong to sclerenchyma.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Parenchyma performs photosynthesis, storage and secretion. Collenchyma supports growing parts such as young stem and petiole. Sclereids occur in fruit walls of nuts and seed coats of legumes. Xylem conducts water and minerals.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Collenchyma cells are thickened at the corners due to deposition of cellulose, hemicellulose and pectin. Lignin is typical of sclerenchyma and suberin of cork and endodermis.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Collenchymatous cells often contain chloroplasts, and when they do they assimilate food. Hence the Reason explains the Assertion.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
explanation: Collenchyma supports growing parts like young stems and petioles. Its cells are living, with corners thickened by cellulose, hemicellulose and pectin, not lignin; uniform lignified walls and death at maturity describe sclerenchyma.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Collenchyma lies in layers below the epidermis in dicots. Sclereids occur in seed coats of legumes and tea leaves. Intercalary meristem lies between mature tissues in grasses. Ray parenchyma cells carry out radial conduction of water.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Collenchyma lacks intercellular spaces. Its cells are thickened at corners, often contain chloroplasts and occur as a homogeneous layer or in patches.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Sclerenchyma may be fibres or sclereids, distinguished by form, structure, origin and development.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Parenchyma cells are isodiametric with thin cellulose walls. Collenchyma is thickened at corners without intercellular spaces. Fibres are elongated, pointed and occur in groups. Sclereids are spherical, oval or cylindrical with very narrow lumen.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Sclereids are commonly found in fruit walls of nuts, pulp of fruits like guava, pear and sapota, seed coats of legumes and leaves of tea.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Sclereids occur in fruit walls of nuts, pulp of guava, pear and sapota, seed coats of legumes and leaves of tea. The petiole of a young leaf is supported by collenchyma.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
explanation: Sclereids occur in the pulp of guava, pear and sapota. They are highly thickened dead cells with very narrow cavities, so the Reason is false.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
explanation: Fibres are thick-walled, elongated and pointed cells generally occurring in groups. Sclereids are spherical, oval or cylindrical highly thickened dead cells with very narrow lumen. The two statements interchange these descriptions.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Complex tissues are made of more than one type of cells working together as a unit. Xylem and phloem are the complex tissues in plants.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Xylem conducts water and minerals; phloem transports food usually from leaves. Guard cells regulate stomatal opening and closing. Companion cells help maintain pressure gradient in sieve tubes.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: In flowering plants, tracheids and vessels are the main water transporting elements. Xylem fibres give support and xylem parenchyma stores food.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Tracheids are elongated with thick lignified walls and tapering ends. Vessels are long tubes of vessel members joined by perforations. Xylem fibres have highly thickened walls and obliterated lumens, septate or aseptate. Xylem parenchyma is living and stores starch, fat and tannins.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Xylem fibres may be septate or aseptate, and ray parenchyma cells carry out radial conduction of water. Vessel cells are devoid of protoplasm, and xylem parenchyma has thin cellulose walls.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Gymnosperms lack vessels but have tracheids. Vessels are characteristic of angiosperms, where tracheids and vessels are the main water conducting elements.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Tracheids are dead, without protoplasm, with thick lignified walls. Gymnosperms lack vessels. Both are true, but the absence of vessels in gymnosperms does not explain why tracheids are dead.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Protoxylem is first formed and metaxylem later formed primary xylem. In endarch xylem (stems) protoxylem faces the pith; in exarch xylem (roots) it faces the periphery.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: A tracheid is a single cell with tapering ends; a vessel is a tube of many members joined by perforations
explanation: Tracheids are elongated single cells with thick lignified walls and tapering ends. A vessel is a long tube made of many vessel members interconnected through perforations. Both are dead, and vessels are characteristic of angiosperms.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
explanation: In endarch xylem (stems) protoxylem lies towards the pith and metaxylem towards the periphery. In roots protoxylem faces the periphery; this exarch arrangement is characteristic of roots.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Exarch xylem (protoxylem towards periphery) and radial arrangement of xylem and phloem on alternate radii are features of roots. Stems are endarch with conjoint bundles, as are leaf veins.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: The sample is from an angiosperm
explanation: These are vessels, made of vessel members interconnected by perforations. Vessels are characteristic of angiosperms; gymnosperms lack vessels.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Cells are the basic unit; cells are organised into tissues, tissues into organs, and organs make up the plant body.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Collenchyma has no intercellular spaces and parenchyma cells can be of various shapes. Elongated, pointed cells in groups are fibres, not sclereids. Intercalary meristems are primary meristems contributing to the primary body.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: food materials, usually from leaves to other parts of the plant
explanation: Phloem transports food materials, usually from leaves to other parts of the plant. Water and minerals move upward in xylem.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Gymnosperms have albuminous cells and sieve cells in their phloem; they lack sieve tubes and companion cells, which occur in angiosperms.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: A mature sieve element has peripheral cytoplasm and a large vacuole but no nucleus. Its functions are therefore controlled by the nucleus of the companion cell, so the Reason explains the Assertion.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: end walls of sieve tube elements perforated in a sieve-like manner
explanation: The end walls of sieve tube elements are perforated in a sieve-like manner to form sieve plates.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
explanation: A mature sieve element has peripheral cytoplasm and a large vacuole but lacks a nucleus. Control runs the other way: the companion cell nucleus controls the sieve tube.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: pit fields present between their common longitudinal walls
explanation: Sieve tube elements and companion cells are connected by pit fields present between their common longitudinal walls. Sieve plates are on end walls between successive sieve tube elements.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
explanation: Gymnosperms lack sieve tubes and companion cells; they have albuminous cells and sieve cells. Companion cells in angiosperms help maintain the pressure gradient in sieve tubes.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Sieve tube elements have sieve plates. Companion cells maintain the pressure gradient. Phloem parenchyma stores resins, latex and mucilage. Phloem fibres of jute, flax and hemp are used commercially.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Phloem parenchyma cells are elongated, tapering, cylindrical with dense cytoplasm and nucleus. The wall is of cellulose with pits bearing plasmodesmatal connections. It stores food, resins, latex and mucilage and is absent in most monocots.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: generally abundant in the primary phloem
explanation: Phloem fibres are generally absent in the primary phloem but found in the secondary phloem. They are sclerenchymatous, elongated, unbranched, with needle-like apices, and dead at maturity.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
explanation: Phloem fibres (bast fibres) are made of sclerenchymatous cells. They are generally absent in the primary phloem and found in the secondary phloem.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Protophloem: first formed, narrow sieve tubes; Metaphloem: later formed, bigger sieve tubes
explanation: The first formed primary phloem has narrow sieve tubes and is protophloem; the later formed phloem with bigger sieve tubes is metaphloem.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Phloem parenchyma is absent in most of the monocotyledons
explanation: Phloem parenchyma is absent in most monocotyledons; the monocot stem in particular lacks phloem parenchyma. So not every angiosperm has it.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Phloem fibres of jute, flax and hemp are used commercially.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: On the basis of structure and location, there are three tissue systems: epidermal, ground (fundamental) and vascular (conducting).
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: The epidermal system has epidermal cells, stomata and appendages. Ground tissue is everything except epidermis and vascular bundles. The vascular system is made of xylem and phloem. In leaves the ground tissue is mesophyll.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: parenchymatous, with little cytoplasm and a large vacuole
explanation: Epidermal cells are parenchymatous with a small amount of cytoplasm lining the cell wall and a large vacuole.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
explanation: The outside of the epidermis is often covered with a waxy thick cuticle that prevents water loss, but the cuticle is absent in roots.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Stomata are structures in the epidermis of leaves that regulate transpiration and gaseous exchange.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Guard cells are usually bean-shaped, but in grasses they are dumb-bell shaped. Guard cells possess chloroplasts. Both statements are true, but chloroplasts do not explain the dumb-bell shape.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: In guard cells the outer walls (away from the pore) are thin and the inner walls (towards the pore) are highly thickened. Both are true descriptions; one does not explain the other.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
explanation: Guard cells contain chloroplasts and regulate stomatal opening and closing. A few epidermal cells near the guard cells become specialised in shape and size; these are subsidiary cells.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: The two cells enclosing a stomatal pore are guard cells. Dumb-bell shaped guard cells are typical of grasses; in most other plants they are bean-shaped. The specialised cells around them are subsidiary cells.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Root hairs are unicellular elongations of epidermal cells that absorb water and minerals. Trichomes on the shoot are usually multicellular. Guard cells are bean-shaped and enclose the pore. The cuticle is a waxy layer absent in roots.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Trichomes in the shoot system are usually multicellular, branched or unbranched, soft or stiff, may be secretory and help prevent water loss due to transpiration.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
explanation: Root hairs are unicellular elongations of epidermal cells and help absorb water and minerals from the soil.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
explanation: Trichomes in the shoot system are usually multicellular, and the epidermal hairs on the stem are called trichomes. Root hairs are unicellular outgrowths of root epidermis.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: all tissues except epidermis and vascular bundles
explanation: All tissues except epidermis and vascular bundles constitute the ground tissue. It consists of simple tissues such as parenchyma, collenchyma and sclerenchyma.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
source_page: NCERT section: The Ground Tissue System
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Ground tissue is everything except epidermis and vascular bundles and is made of parenchyma, collenchyma and sclerenchyma. In leaves it forms the mesophyll.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
source_page: NCERT section: The Ground Tissue System
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
explanation: In leaves the ground tissue is mesophyll, made of thin-walled chloroplast containing cells. Parenchymatous cells are usually present in the cortex, pericycle, pith and medullary rays of primary stems and roots.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
source_page: NCERT section: The Ground Tissue System
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: All tissues except the epidermis and vascular bundles constitute the ground tissue. Parenchymatous cells are present in the cortex, pericycle, pith and medullary rays of primary stems and roots. The endodermis is the innermost layer of the cortex, so it belongs to the ground tissue, not the vascular tissue system.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
source_page: NCERT section: The Ground Tissue System
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: In dicot stems, cambium is present between phloem and xylem; such bundles can form secondary tissues and are open. Bundles without cambium are closed.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
source_page: NCERT section: The Vascular Tissue System
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: In monocotyledons the vascular bundles have no cambium, so they do not form secondary tissues and are called closed.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
source_page: NCERT section: The Vascular Tissue System
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Radial bundles have xylem and phloem on alternate radii, as in roots. Conjoint bundles have them on the same radius, as in stems and leaves. Open bundles have cambium; closed bundles lack it.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
source_page: NCERT section: The Vascular Tissue System
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
explanation: Conjoint bundles, common in stems and leaves, usually have phloem only on the outer side of xylem. Radial bundles occur in roots.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
source_page: NCERT section: The Vascular Tissue System
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: jointly situated along the same radius
explanation: In conjoint vascular bundles, xylem and phloem are jointly situated along the same radius. Such bundles are common in stems and leaves.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
source_page: NCERT section: The Vascular Tissue System
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: They are closed and do not form secondary xylem and phloem
explanation: Bundles without cambium cannot form secondary tissues and are called closed, as in monocotyledons.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
source_page: NCERT section: The Vascular Tissue System
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Each stoma is enclosed by two bean-shaped guard cells that possess chloroplasts and regulate opening and closing of the pore.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: A ring of conjoint, open bundles is typical of the dicot stem. Radial bundles with polyarch xylem (more than six bundles) and a large pith are typical of the monocot root.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
source_page: NCERT section: The Vascular Tissue System
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: It is wrong; the mature sieve element retains peripheral cytoplasm and a large vacuole
explanation: A mature sieve element possesses peripheral cytoplasm and a large vacuole but lacks a nucleus; its functions are controlled by the companion cell nucleus. Vessel members, by contrast, lack protoplasm.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: In a conjoint open bundle of the dicot stem, phloem is on the outer side, cambium lies between phloem and xylem, and the xylem is endarch, so metaxylem is towards the periphery and protoxylem towards the pith.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
source_page: NCERT section: The Vascular Tissue System
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: The epidermal tissue system forms the outermost covering of the whole plant body. Fundamental tissue is another name for ground tissue.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: The epidermis is usually single-layered, made of elongated compactly arranged cells forming a continuous layer, and is the outermost layer of the primary plant body. Its cells are parenchymatous, not sclerenchymatous.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: A mature sieve element lacks a nucleus but has cytoplasm. Vessel members are devoid of protoplasm. Collenchyma lacks intercellular spaces. Gymnosperm xylem lacks vessels.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Companion cells are specialised parenchymatous cells associated with sieve tube elements. Sieve tube element end walls form sieve plates. Gymnosperms have albuminous cells and sieve cells instead. Vessel members are joined by perforations and are characteristic of angiosperms.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: The transverse section of the sunflower root illustrates dicot root anatomy. Sugarcane, wheat and onion are monocots.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: It is the epiblema; it lacks cuticle and many of its cells form unicellular root hairs
explanation: The outermost layer of the root is the epiblema. Many of its cells protrude as unicellular root hairs, and cuticle is absent in roots.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: a single layer of barrel-shaped cells without intercellular spaces
explanation: The innermost layer of the root cortex, the endodermis, is a single layer of barrel-shaped cells without intercellular spaces, with casparian strips.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: The tangential and radial walls of root endodermal cells have deposition of water-impermeable waxy suberin in the form of casparian strips, so the Reason explains the Assertion.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Collenchyma corners have cellulose, hemicellulose and pectin. Casparian strips are suberin. Sclerenchyma walls are thick and lignified. Parenchyma walls are thin and of cellulose.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
source_page: NCERT section: Anatomy of Dicotyledonous and Monocotyledonous Plants
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
explanation: Lateral roots are initiated in the pericycle, which consists of a few layers of thick-walled parenchymatous cells lying next to the endodermis. Barrel-shaped cells with casparian strips describe the endodermis.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
explanation: Conjunctive tissue is the parenchymatous tissue lying between xylem and phloem. The stele comprises all tissues on the inner side of the endodermis, such as pericycle, vascular bundles and pith.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: all tissues inner to the endodermis, such as pericycle, vascular bundles and pith
explanation: All tissues on the inner side of the endodermis, such as pericycle, vascular bundles and pith, constitute the stele. The endodermis is the innermost layer of cortex.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: The dicot root has a small or inconspicuous pith; a large well-developed pith is a monocot root feature. Root hairs, parenchymatous cortex and two to four xylem and phloem patches are dicot root features.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Dicot: two to four xylem patches, small pith; Monocot: more than six xylem bundles, large pith
explanation: The dicot root usually has two to four xylem and phloem patches and a small or inconspicuous pith. The monocot root is polyarch, usually with more than six xylem bundles, and has a large, well-developed pith.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
source_page: NCERT section: Anatomy of Dicotyledonous and Monocotyledonous Plants
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: As compared to dicot roots with fewer xylem bundles, monocot roots usually have more than six (polyarch) xylem bundles.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
explanation: The monocot root is similar to the dicot root in many respects and has epidermis, cortex, endodermis, pericycle, vascular bundles and pith. Monocot roots do not undergo any secondary growth.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Radial bundles with exarch xylem indicate a root; polyarch xylem and a large pith indicate a monocot root.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: From outside: epidermis, then the cortex (hypodermis, cortical parenchyma, endodermis), then the pericycle on the inner side of the endodermis.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: a few layers of collenchymatous cells
explanation: The outer hypodermis of the dicot stem consists of a few layers of collenchymatous cells just below the epidermis, giving mechanical strength to the young stem.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: The innermost layer of the cortex of a dicot stem, the endodermis, is rich in starch grains and is also called the starch sheath.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: The dicot stem cortex has three sub-zones: collenchymatous hypodermis, parenchymatous cortical layers with intercellular spaces, and the endodermis (starch sheath). The pericycle lies inside the endodermis and is not part of the cortex.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: on the inner side of the endodermis and above the phloem as semi-lunar patches of sclerenchyma
explanation: In the dicot stem the pericycle lies on the inner side of the endodermis and above the phloem in the form of semi-lunar patches of sclerenchyma.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Medullary rays are radially placed parenchyma between bundles, and bundles are in a ring. The pericycle is in semi-lunar sclerenchyma patches and the hypodermis is collenchymatous.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Hypodermis is collenchymatous; endodermis is the starch sheath; pericycle forms semi-lunar sclerenchyma patches above the phloem; the pith is rounded parenchyma with large intercellular spaces.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: A ring of vascular bundles is characteristic of the dicot stem, and each bundle is conjoint, open and endarch. Both are true, but the internal structure of each bundle does not explain their arrangement in a ring.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: The dicot stem epidermis has a thin cuticle and may bear trichomes and a few stomata; the pith is rounded parenchyma with large intercellular spaces. The cortex lies between epidermis and pericycle, and stem bundles are endarch.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: The monocot stem has a sclerenchymatous hypodermis, while the dicot stem has a collenchymatous hypodermis.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
explanation: In the monocot stem the peripheral vascular bundles are generally smaller than the central ones, so the Assertion is false. Each bundle is surrounded by a sclerenchymatous bundle sheath.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: The monocot stem lacks phloem parenchyma, has water-containing cavities within its conjoint, closed bundles, and has a large conspicuous parenchymatous ground tissue. Only the hypodermis and bundle sheaths are sclerenchymatous.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Dicot: collenchymatous hypodermis, bundles in a ring; Monocot: sclerenchymatous hypodermis, scattered bundles
explanation: The dicot stem has a collenchymatous hypodermis and a ring of vascular bundles; the monocot stem has a sclerenchymatous hypodermis and numerous scattered bundles.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
source_page: NCERT section: Anatomy of Dicotyledonous and Monocotyledonous Plants
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: A sclerenchymatous hypodermis and no phloem parenchyma
explanation: The features describe a monocot stem, which also has a sclerenchymatous hypodermis, a large parenchymatous ground tissue, conjoint closed bundles and no phloem parenchyma.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: A vertical section of a dorsiventral leaf through the lamina shows epidermis, mesophyll and the vascular system.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Both epidermal surfaces bear a conspicuous cuticle, the adaxial epidermis may lack stomata, and spongy parenchyma extends to the lower epidermis with large spaces. Palisade cells are elongated, vertical and parallel, not oval and loose.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Palisade cells are elongated, vertical and parallel; spongy cells are oval or round, loose, reaching the lower epidermis. Vascular bundles are surrounded by thick-walled bundle sheath cells. The adaxial (upper) epidermis may even lack stomata.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
explanation: Mesophyll is parenchyma with chloroplasts and carries out photosynthesis. The size of the vascular bundles depends on the size of the veins.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: The size of vascular bundles depends on the size of the veins, and veins vary in thickness in the reticulate venation of dicot leaves. Hence the Reason explains the Assertion.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Xylem towards the adaxial (upper) side and phloem towards the abaxial (lower) side
explanation: Leaf bundles are conjoint with phloem on one side only. In the vertical section of a dorsiventral leaf, xylem lies towards the adaxial (upper) surface and phloem towards the abaxial (lower) surface.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: From top: adaxial (upper) epidermis, palisade parenchyma, spongy parenchyma, abaxial (lower) epidermis.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: its stomata occur on both surfaces and its mesophyll is not differentiated
explanation: In an isobilateral leaf stomata are present on both surfaces of the epidermis and the mesophyll is not differentiated into palisade and spongy parenchyma.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Bulliform cells are large, empty and colourless. Guard cells of grasses are dumb-bell shaped. Root endodermal cells are barrel-shaped. Palisade cells are elongated and arranged vertically and parallel.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
source_page: NCERT section: Anatomy of Dicotyledonous and Monocotyledonous Plants
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
explanation: Turgid bulliform cells keep the leaf surface exposed, while flaccid ones make leaves curl inwards. Bulliform cells are large, empty, colourless modified adaxial epidermal cells along the veins.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Casparian strips are in root endodermis; the starch sheath is the dicot stem endodermis; bulliform cells lie in the adaxial epidermis of grass leaves; water-containing cavities lie within monocot stem vascular bundles.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
source_page: NCERT section: Anatomy of Dicotyledonous and Monocotyledonous Plants
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: It is wrong; bundles are of near similar sizes except in the main veins
explanation: Parallel venation in monocot leaves is reflected in the near similar sizes of vascular bundles, except in the main veins, as seen in vertical sections.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: flaccid under water stress and turgid after water absorption
explanation: When bulliform cells are flaccid due to water stress, the leaves curl inwards to minimise water loss. When they absorb water and become turgid, the leaf surface is exposed.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: dicot root, monocot stem and isobilateral leaf
explanation: Two to four xylem patches with a small pith mark a dicot root. Scattered conjoint closed bundles with a sclerenchymatous hypodermis mark a monocot stem. Stomata on both surfaces with undifferentiated mesophyll mark an isobilateral leaf.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
source_page: NCERT section: Anatomy of Dicotyledonous and Monocotyledonous Plants
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: The dicot root has radial bundles with two to four xylem patches; the monocot root is polyarch. The dicot stem has a ring of conjoint, open, endarch bundles; the monocot stem has scattered conjoint, closed bundles with sclerenchymatous sheaths.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
source_page: NCERT section: Anatomy of Dicotyledonous and Monocotyledonous Plants
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Epiblema is the outermost layer with root hairs; cortex is several layers of thin-walled parenchyma; endodermis is barrel-shaped cells with casparian strips; pericycle is a few layers of thick-walled parenchyma where lateral roots initiate.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
explanation: A monocot root usually has more than six (polyarch) xylem bundles and a large, well-developed pith. Both statements describe the dicot root instead.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
explanation: Isobilateral leaves have stomata on both surfaces. In grasses, certain adaxial epidermal cells along the veins become large, empty, colourless bulliform cells.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo106.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: a group of similar cells along with intercellular substances performing a specific function
explanation: A tissue is a group of similar cells, together with intercellular substances, that performs one or more specific functions. Organs are made of tissues, and organ systems are made of organs.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: It contains epithelial, connective, muscular and neural tissues
explanation: Each organ is made of one or more types of tissues. The heart is a classic example of an organ made of all four basic tissues: epithelial, connective, muscular and neural.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
source_page: NCERT section: Organ and Organ System
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Morphology refers to the study of form or externally visible features; in animals it covers the external appearance of organs or parts. Anatomy is conventionally used for the study of morphology of internal organs.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
source_page: NCERT section: Organ and Organ System
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
explanation: The assertion is false: each organ is made of one or more types of tissues, for example the heart contains all four basic tissues. The reason is true: organisation into organs and organ systems is essential for more efficient and better coordinated activities of millions of cells.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
source_page: NCERT section: Organ and Organ System
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Epithelia are sheet-like linings with a free surface; connective tissues bind, support, strengthen, protect and insulate; muscle tissue contracts on stimulation to bring about movement; neural tissue exerts the greatest control over responsiveness to changing conditions.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: It has a free surface that faces either a body fluid or the outside environment
explanation: Epithelial tissue has a free surface which faces a body fluid or the outside environment, providing a covering or lining. Its cells are compactly packed with little intercellular matrix and are linked by specialised junctions.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Squamous epithelium lines blood vessels and lung air sacs; cuboidal lines ducts of glands and tubular parts of nephrons; columnar lines the stomach and intestine; ciliated epithelium lines the inner surface of hollow organs such as bronchioles and fallopian tubes.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Squamous cells are thin and flattened with irregular boundaries; cuboidal cells are cube-like; columnar cells are tall and slender with basal nuclei; compound epithelium has two or more cell layers.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Squamous epithelium is a single thin layer of flattened cells with irregular boundaries, found in walls of blood vessels and air sacs of lungs, where it forms a diffusion boundary.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Cuboidal epithelium is found in ducts of glands and tubular parts of nephrons, where it performs secretion and absorption. The epithelium of the proximal convoluted tubule has microvilli, which increase the absorptive surface.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Ciliated epithelium, made of columnar or cuboidal cells bearing cilia, lines hollow organs such as bronchioles and fallopian tubes. The cilia move particles or mucus in a specific direction, which is how the bronchial passages are cleared. The Reason explains the Assertion.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
