syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
explanation: Thin flattened cells with irregular boundaries describe squamous epithelium; cuboidal cells are cube-like. Endocrine glands do not have ducts; their hormones are secreted directly into the fluid bathing the gland.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Goblet cells of the alimentary canal are unicellular glands; the salivary gland is multicellular. Exocrine glands release products through ducts; endocrine glands are ductless and secrete hormones into the surrounding fluid.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Exocrine glands secrete mucus, saliva, earwax, oil, milk, digestive enzymes and other cell products through ducts. Hormones are products of ductless endocrine glands.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: directly into the fluid bathing the gland
explanation: Endocrine glands do not have ducts. Their products, called hormones, are secreted directly into the fluid bathing the gland.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: is made of more than one layer of cells
explanation: Compound epithelium is multilayered, which limits its role in secretion and absorption. Its main function is to provide protection against chemical and mechanical stresses.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Compound epithelium covers the dry surface of the skin, the moist surface of the buccal cavity and pharynx, and the inner lining of ducts of salivary glands and pancreatic ducts. Air sacs of lungs have simple squamous epithelium.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Simple epithelium lines body cavities, ducts and tubes; compound epithelium mainly protects against chemical and mechanical stresses
explanation: Simple epithelium is a single layer of cells that functions as a lining for body cavities, ducts and tubes. Compound epithelium has two or more layers and has a protective function, as in the skin.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
explanation: Compound epithelium does cover the dry surface of skin. Being multilayered, it has a limited role in secretion and absorption; its main role is protection against chemical and mechanical stresses.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Tight junctions stop substances from leaking across a tissue; adhering junctions cement neighbouring cells together; gap junctions connect the cytoplasm of adjoining cells, allowing rapid transfer of ions, small molecules and sometimes big molecules.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Gap junctions connect the cytoplasm of adjoining cells, which is why ions and small molecules pass rapidly between them. Tight junctions prevent leakage across a tissue; this is true but is a different junction and does not explain the assertion.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
explanation: Cementing is the role of adhering junctions; tight junctions stop leakage of substances across a tissue. Specialised junctions in nearly all animal tissues give both structural and functional links between cells.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Tight junctions help to stop substances from leaking across a tissue. Their destruction would make the epithelial sheet leaky, while adhering junctions (cementing) and gap junctions (communication) serve other roles.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Gap junctions are present, but adhering junctions are deficient
explanation: Rapid passage of dye between cytoplasms indicates gap junctions, which connect the cytoplasm of adjoining cells. Easy separation indicates failure of cementing, which is the role of adhering junctions.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Glandular epithelium is of two types: unicellular, made of isolated glandular cells such as goblet cells of the alimentary canal, and multicellular, made of clusters of cells such as the salivary gland.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Ciliated epithelium: walls of blood vessels
explanation: Walls of blood vessels are lined by squamous epithelium. Ciliated epithelium lines hollow organs such as bronchioles and fallopian tubes.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Epithelial cells are compactly packed with little matrix, and columnar cells are tall and slender with possible microvilli. Cuboidal epithelium mainly does secretion and absorption; protection is the role of compound epithelium. Endocrine glands are ductless.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
explanation: The salivary gland is a multicellular gland made of a cluster of cells; goblet cells are the unicellular example. Some columnar or cuboidal cells get specialised for secretion and are called glandular epithelium.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Tall cells with basal nuclei are columnar; hair-like projections are cilia, so this is ciliated epithelium. It is present on the inner surface of hollow organs such as bronchioles and fallopian tubes.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Columnar epithelium, and the cuboidal epithelium of the proximal convoluted tubule
explanation: The free surface of columnar cells may have microvilli, and the cuboidal epithelium of the proximal convoluted tubule also has microvilli. Both are absorptive surfaces. Cilia, found on ciliated epithelium, are different structures that move mucus or particles.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Connective tissues are the most abundant and widely distributed in the body of complex animals. They are named for their special function of linking and supporting other tissues and organs.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: In all connective tissues except blood, the cells secrete fibres of collagen or elastin, which give strength, elasticity and flexibility. Blood is a fluid connective tissue without such secreted fibres.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: modified polysaccharides secreted by the cells that accumulate between cells and fibres
explanation: Connective tissue cells secrete modified polysaccharides that accumulate between cells and fibres and act as the matrix or ground substance.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Areolar tissue beneath the skin is loose connective tissue. Tendons and ligaments are dense regular connective tissue; the skin has dense irregular connective tissue. Cartilage, bone and blood are specialised connective tissues.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Areolar tissue, a loose connective tissue beneath the skin, contains fibroblasts (which produce and secrete fibres), macrophages and mast cells. Osteocytes are bone cells.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Fibroblasts produce and secrete fibres. Chondrocytes lie in small cavities in the pliable cartilage matrix they secrete. Osteocytes lie in lacunae in the hard bone matrix rich in calcium salts. Adipose cells store fats.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Adipose tissue is a loose connective tissue located mainly beneath the skin, and its cells are specialised to store fats made from excess nutrients. The storage function is true but does not explain its classification or location.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
explanation: Dense regular tissue has collagen fibres in rows between parallel bundles. Tendons attach skeletal muscles to bones, and ligaments attach one bone to another, so Statement II reverses them.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: In loose tissue, cells and fibres lie loosely in a semi-fluid ground substance; in dense tissue, fibres and fibroblasts are compactly packed
explanation: Loose connective tissue has cells and fibres loosely arranged in a semi-fluid ground substance, for example areolar tissue. Dense connective tissue has fibres and fibroblasts compactly packed, as in tendons, ligaments and the skin.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Dense irregular connective tissue has fibroblasts and many fibres, mostly collagen, oriented differently. It is present in the skin.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: solid and pliable, and resists compression
explanation: The intercellular material of cartilage is solid and pliable and resists compression. Its cells, chondrocytes, are enclosed in small cavities within the matrix they secrete.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Most cartilages of vertebrate embryos are replaced by bone, but in adults cartilage remains in the tip of the nose, outer ear joints, between adjacent bones of the vertebral column, and in limbs and hands.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Most cartilages in vertebrate embryos are replaced by bones in adults. This is exactly why much embryonic cartilage is absent as cartilage in the adult, though some persists at sites such as the nose and ear.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: hard and non-pliable, rich in calcium salts and collagen fibres
explanation: Bones have a hard and non-pliable ground substance rich in calcium salts and collagen fibres, which give bone its strength.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Bone marrow in some bones is the site of production of blood cells. Limb bones such as long bones of legs serve weight-bearing functions. Adipose tissue stores fat, and blood is the main circulating fluid for transport.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
explanation: Osteocytes lie in lacunae within the bone matrix. Bones support and protect softer organs and interact with attached skeletal muscles to bring about movements.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Cartilage matrix is solid and pliable and resists compression; bone matrix is hard and non-pliable
explanation: Cartilage has a solid, pliable matrix that resists compression, with chondrocytes in small cavities. Bone has a hard, non-pliable matrix rich in calcium salts and collagen fibres, with osteocytes in lacunae.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Tendons and ligaments are both dense regular connective tissue. Tendons attach skeletal muscles to bones, and ligaments attach one bone to another.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
explanation: Blood is a fluid connective tissue containing plasma, red blood cells, white blood cells and platelets. In all connective tissues except blood, cells secrete collagen or elastin fibres, so the reason is false.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Cartilage, bones and blood are specialised connective tissues. Tendons are dense regular connective tissue attaching skeletal muscles to bones.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Areolar tissue is loose connective tissue beneath the skin. It often serves as a support framework for epithelium and contains fibroblasts, macrophages and mast cells.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: A solid, pliable matrix resisting compression with cells in small cavities is cartilage. In adults, cartilage is present at the tip of the nose, among other sites.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Collagen and elastin fibres provide strength, elasticity and flexibility. Bone has a hard, non-pliable matrix; a pliable matrix that resists compression is cartilage. Bone is the main structural frame, and bone marrow in some bones produces blood cells.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Muscle fibres are composed of fine fibrils called myofibrils. Intercalated discs are communication junctions in cardiac muscle. A tough connective tissue sheath encloses several bundles of skeletal muscle fibres. Smooth muscle fibres are fusiform, tapering at both ends.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Skeletal muscle is closely attached to skeletal bones, as in the biceps. Smooth muscle is found in walls of internal organs such as blood vessels, stomach and intestine. Cardiac muscle is present only in the heart.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: many long, cylindrical fibres arranged in parallel arrays
explanation: Each muscle is made of many long, cylindrical fibres arranged in parallel arrays. These fibres are composed of numerous fine fibrils called myofibrils.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
explanation: Smooth muscles are involuntary because their functioning cannot be directly controlled; we usually cannot make them contract merely by thinking about it, as we can with skeletal muscles.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
explanation: Cell junctions fuse the plasma membranes of cardiac muscle cells, and communication junctions called intercalated discs at some fusion points allow the cells to contract as a unit. The reason denies these junctions and is false.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
explanation: In the biceps, striated skeletal muscle fibres are bundled in parallel, and a sheath of tough connective tissue encloses several bundles of these fibres.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: The walls of internal organs such as blood vessels, stomach and intestine contain smooth muscle. The heart contains cardiac muscle, which is present only in the heart.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: The ability of cardiac cells to contract as a unit
explanation: Intercalated discs are communication junctions at some fusion points that allow cardiac cells to contract as a unit: when one cell receives a signal, its neighbours are also stimulated. Blocking them would disrupt this coordinated contraction.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Both are held by cell junctions; only cardiac muscle has communication junctions called intercalated discs
explanation: Smooth muscle fibres are held together by cell junctions and bundled in a connective tissue sheath. In cardiac muscle, cell junctions fuse the plasma membranes, and intercalated discs at some fusion points let the cells contract as a unit.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: contract (shorten), then relax (lengthen) and return to the uncontracted state
explanation: Muscle fibres contract (shorten) in response to stimulation, then relax (lengthen) and return to the uncontracted state in a coordinated fashion.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Smooth muscle fibres are fusiform, non-striated and bundled in a connective tissue sheath. Skeletal muscle is attached to bones. Cardiac muscle is present only in the heart; blood vessel walls have smooth muscle.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Fusiform, non-striated fibres bundled in a connective tissue sheath are smooth muscle, which lines walls of internal organs such as blood vessels, stomach and intestine.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Neurons are excitable cells and the units of the neural system. Neuroglia protect and support neurons and make up more than half the volume of neural tissue. Connective tissue, not neural tissue, is the most abundant and widely distributed.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Neurons are excitable: on suitable stimulation an electrical disturbance is generated that swiftly travels along the plasma membrane. This property is precisely what makes them excitable.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
explanation: Neurons, not neuroglia, are the excitable units; neuroglia protect and support neurons. When the disturbance reaches the neuron's endings or output zone, it triggers events that may stimulate or inhibit adjacent neurons and other cells.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Dendrites receive the stimulus and pass it to the cell body; the axon carries the disturbance away from the cell body to its endings, the output zone, where it influences adjacent cells.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: the neuron's endings, where arrival of the disturbance triggers events in adjacent cells
explanation: The disturbance generated in a stimulated neuron travels along its membrane to the neuron's endings, or output zone, where it triggers events that may stimulate or inhibit adjacent neurons and other cells.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Epithelia are sheet-like linings, and neurons are the basic units of neural tissue. Cartilage and bone are structural materials, but blood is a fluid tissue with transport functions. Cardiac muscle forms the contractile walls of the heart.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Frogs can live both on land and in freshwater. The most common species found in India is Rana tigrina.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Frogs can live both on land and in freshwater and belong to class Amphibia of phylum Chordata.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Frogs do not have a constant body temperature; it varies with the temperature of the environment. Such animals are called cold-blooded or poikilotherms.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Frogs take shelter in deep burrows during peak summer and winter; summer sleep is aestivation and winter sleep is hibernation. Changing colour to hide from enemies is camouflage. The nictitating membrane covers the bulged eyes and protects them in water.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
explanation: The dorsal side of a frog is generally olive green with dark irregular spots. On the ventral side the skin is uniformly pale yellow.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: A frog never drinks water but absorbs it through its skin. Its skin is smooth and slippery due to mucus, which is true, but this is not the explanation for the absence of drinking.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: The frog's body is divisible into head and trunk; neck and tail are absent. A pair of nostrils lies above the mouth, and webbed digits on the feet help in swimming.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Hind limbs end in five digits and are larger and more muscular than forelimbs, which end in four digits
explanation: Hind limbs of the frog end in five digits and are larger and more muscular than the forelimbs, which end in four digits. The limbs help in swimming, walking, leaping and burrowing.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Frogs exhibit sexual dimorphism. Male frogs have sound-producing vocal sacs and a copulatory pad on the first digit of the forelimbs, which are absent in females. Webbed feet and the tympanum occur in both sexes.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: It is a membranous structure on either side of the eyes that receives sound signals
explanation: On either side of the eyes a membranous tympanum (ear) receives sound signals. The external ear is absent in frogs; only the tympanum is seen externally. The nictitating membrane protects the eyes, and vocal sacs produce sound in males.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Forelimbs and hind limbs help in swimming, walking, leaping and burrowing. Prey is captured by the bilobed tongue.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: The skin of a frog is smooth and slippery due to mucus and is always kept moist. It helps in respiration and absorption of water.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Frogs can change colour to hide from enemies (camouflage). This protective coloration is called mimicry.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: The eyes of a frog are bulged and covered by a nictitating membrane that protects them while in water.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: take shelter in deep burrows to protect themselves from extreme heat and cold
explanation: Frogs are not seen during peak summer and winter; they take shelter in deep burrows to protect themselves from extreme heat and cold, undergoing aestivation and hibernation respectively.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
explanation: The mid-brain of a frog is characterised by a pair of optic lobes; olfactory lobes belong to the fore-brain. Ten pairs of cranial nerves arise from the frog brain.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: frogs are carnivores, so the length of the intestine is reduced
explanation: The alimentary canal of a frog is short because frogs are carnivores, and hence the length of the intestine is reduced.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: The mouth opens into the buccal cavity, which leads to the oesophagus through the pharynx. The short oesophagus opens into the stomach.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: The liver secretes bile, which is stored in the gall bladder. The pancreas produces pancreatic juice containing digestive enzymes that digest carbohydrates and proteins. The stomach wall secretes HCl and gastric juices.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Partially digested food called chyme passes from the stomach to the duodenum, which receives bile and pancreatic juice. Villi and microvilli absorb digested food, and undigested waste moves into the rectum and passes out through the cloaca.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
explanation: The duodenum receives bile from the gall bladder and pancreatic juice from the pancreas through a common bile duct, not two separate ducts.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
explanation: Bile emulsifies fat; it is pancreatic juice that digests carbohydrates and proteins. The gall bladder stores bile secreted by the liver, not pancreatic juice.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: finger-like folds of the intestinal wall called villi and microvilli
explanation: Final digestion takes place in the intestine, and digested food is absorbed by numerous finger-like folds in its inner wall called villi and microvilli.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Emulsification of fats in the duodenum
explanation: Bile reaches the duodenum through the common bile duct and emulsifies fats there. Blocking the duct stops bile reaching the duodenum, so fat emulsification is impaired, while bile production, prey capture and gastric secretion continue.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Food is captured by the bilobed tongue. The muscular tongue, bilobed at the tip, is used in capturing prey.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: The short oesophagus opens into the stomach, where HCl and gastric juices digest food. Final digestion occurs in the intestine, and undigested waste moves into the rectum and out through the cloaca.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: During aestivation and hibernation, gaseous exchange in the frog takes place through the skin. The lungs are a pair of elongated, pink coloured sac-like structures in the upper part of the trunk region. Both are true, but the description of the lungs does not explain the Assertion.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
explanation: In water, the skin acts as the aquatic respiratory organ (cutaneous respiration). On land, the buccal cavity, skin and lungs act as respiratory organs.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Air enters through the nostrils into the buccal cavity and then to the lungs. Respiration by lungs is called pulmonary respiration.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: In water only the skin acts; on land the buccal cavity, skin and lungs act
explanation: Frogs respire on land and in water by two different methods. In water, the skin acts as the aquatic respiratory organ. On land, the buccal cavity, skin and lungs act as respiratory organs.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: a well developed closed type, and a lymphatic system is also present
explanation: Frogs have a well developed closed vascular system. They also have a lymphatic system consisting of lymph, lymph channels and lymph nodes.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: The frog heart is covered by the pericardium. The triangular sinus venosus joins the right atrium and receives blood through the venae cavae. The ventricle opens into the sac-like conus arteriosus on the ventral side.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Venae cavae bring blood into the sinus venosus, which joins the right atrium. Blood passes from the atrium to the single ventricle, which opens into the conus arteriosus.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Frogs have special venous connections between liver and intestine (hepatic portal system) and between kidney and lower parts of the body (renal portal system). Both statements are true, but the reason describes the hepatic portal system.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
explanation: The lymphatic system consists of lymph, lymph channels and lymph nodes; heart, blood vessels and blood form the blood vascular system. The ventricle opens into the conus arteriosus on the ventral side; the sinus venosus joins the right atrium.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: lacks a few proteins and RBCs
explanation: Lymph is different from blood: it lacks a few proteins and RBCs.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: The muscular heart lies in the upper part of the body cavity and is covered by the pericardium. The sinus venosus receives blood through the venae cavae, and the ventricle opens into the conus arteriosus on the ventral side.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Lungs are a pair of elongated, pink, sac-like structures in the upper trunk (thorax). Kidneys are compact, dark red and bean-like. Testes are yellowish and ovoid. The thin-walled urinary bladder lies ventral to the rectum.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: In males the ureters act as urinogenital ducts; in females the ureters and oviducts open separately into the cloaca
explanation: Two ureters emerge from the kidneys. In male frogs the ureters act as urinogenital ducts opening into the cloaca. In females the ureters and oviducts open separately into the cloaca.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
explanation: The frog excretes urea and is therefore ureotelic, not ammonotelic. Excretory wastes are carried by blood into the kidneys, where they are separated and excreted.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: The kidneys of frog are compact, dark red, bean-like structures. Each is composed of several structural and functional units called uriniferous tubules or nephrons.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
explanation: The excretory system of frog consists of a pair of kidneys, ureters, cloaca and urinary bladder. The thin-walled urinary bladder is ventral to the rectum and also opens into the cloaca.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: ureter, acting as a urinogenital duct
explanation: Vasa efferentia from the testes enter the kidney and open into Bidder's canal, which communicates with the urinogenital duct. In males the ureter acts as this urinogenital duct and opens into the cloaca.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Prominent endocrine glands in frog are pituitary, thyroid, parathyroid, thymus, pineal body, pancreatic islets, adrenals and gonads.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Ten pairs of cranial nerves arise from the brain of a frog.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: The fore-brain includes olfactory lobes, paired cerebral hemispheres and unpaired diencephalon. The mid-brain has a pair of optic lobes. The hind-brain consists of cerebellum and medulla oblongata.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: The CNS is the brain and spinal cord; the PNS consists of cranial and spinal nerves; the ANS consists of sympathetic and parasympathetic parts. The spinal cord is enclosed in the vertebral column.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
explanation: The medulla oblongata passes out through the foramen magnum and continues into the spinal cord, enclosed in the vertebral column. The diencephalon is an unpaired part of the fore-brain.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: The fore-brain includes olfactory lobes, paired cerebral hemispheres and unpaired diencephalon. Optic lobes characterise the mid-brain.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
explanation: The control and coordination system of frog includes both the neural system and endocrine glands. Chemical coordination of organs is achieved by hormones from glands such as pituitary, thyroid and adrenals.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: The frog has organs of touch (sensory papillae), taste (taste buds), smell (nasal epithelium), vision (eyes) and hearing (tympanum with internal ears).
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Eyes and internal ears are well-organised structures; the organs of touch, taste and smell are cellular aggregations around nerve endings. Nasal epithelium is the organ of smell; taste buds serve taste. The external ear is absent, so only the tympanum is seen externally.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
explanation: The frog ear is an organ of hearing as well as balancing (equilibrium). The external ear is absent in frogs; only the tympanum can be seen externally.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: a pair of spherical, simple eyes situated in the orbit of the skull
explanation: The eyes of a frog are a pair of spherical structures situated in the orbit of the skull. They are simple eyes, possessing only one unit.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: a double fold of peritoneum called mesorchium
explanation: The male frog has a pair of yellowish, ovoid testes adhered to the upper part of the kidneys by a double fold of peritoneum called mesorchium.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Vasa efferentia arising from the testes enter the kidneys and open into Bidder's canal, which communicates with the urinogenital duct that comes out of the kidney and opens into the cloaca.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
explanation: The ovaries lie near the kidneys but have no functional connection with them; a pair of oviducts opens separately into the cloaca. A mature female can lay 2500 to 3000 ova at a time.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: The rectum opens to the outside through the cloaca, and in the male the urinogenital ducts, which carry urine and sperms, also open into it. Hence the cloaca, a small median chamber, passes faecal matter, urine and sperms to the exterior. The Reason explains the Assertion.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Male gametes pass through the kidney via vasa efferentia and Bidder's canal; female gametes travel in oviducts with no kidney connection
explanation: In males, vasa efferentia from the testes enter the kidney and open into Bidder's canal, which joins the urinogenital duct. In females, ovaries have no functional connection with the kidneys and the oviducts open separately into the cloaca.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Sensory papillae are organs of touch. The mesorchium attaches the testes to the kidneys. Vasa efferentia open into Bidder's canal within the kidney. The ventricle opens into the conus arteriosus.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: A frog has ten pairs of cranial nerves; 10 to 12 vasa efferentia arise from the testes; a mature female lays 2500 to 3000 ova at a time; each hind limb ends in five digits.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Fertilisation is external and takes place in water. Development involves a larval stage called tadpole, which undergoes metamorphosis to form the adult. A mature female lays 2500 to 3000 ova at a time.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Frogs are beneficial because they eat insects and protect crops, maintain ecological balance as an important link in food chains and food webs, and in some countries their muscular legs are used as food.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Frogs maintain ecological balance because they serve as an important link of the food chain and food web in the ecosystem.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo107.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

explanation: Anton Von Leeuwenhoek first saw and described a live cell. Robert Brown later discovered the nucleus, while Schleiden and Virchow contributed to the cell theory.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
source_page: NCERT section: What is a Cell?
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: Robert Brown described the nucleus as a cell organelle in 1831. Golgi bodies were described by Camillo Golgi (1898) and ribosomes by George Palade (1953).
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
source_page: NCERT section: What is a Cell?
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: Schleiden (1838) found that plants are made of different kinds of cells forming tissues. Schwann (1839) reported the thin outer layer of animal cells, now called the plasma membrane. Virchow (1855) stated Omnis cellula-e cellula. Leeuwenhoek first saw and described a live cell.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: The Schleiden and Schwann theory did not explain how new cells were formed. Virchow (1855) explained that cells divide and new cells are formed from pre-existing cells, and so modified their hypothesis. The reason therefore explains the assertion.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
explanation: Both observations belong to Schwann (1839). He studied animal cells and reported the thin outer layer, and from plant tissues he concluded that the cell wall is unique to plant cells. On this basis he proposed that bodies of animals and plants are composed of cells and products of cells.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: Robert Brown described the nucleus in 1831, Schleiden reported on plant cells in 1838, Schwann on animal cells in 1839, and Virchow explained the origin of new cells from pre-existing cells in 1855.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: all cells arise from pre-existing cells
explanation: Virchow (1855) explained that cells divide and new cells are formed from pre-existing cells, summarised as Omnis cellula-e cellula.

correct_answer: 52 per cent protein and 40 per cent lipids

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Movement of ions by the Na+/K+ pump

explanation: Neutral solutes may move across the membrane by simple diffusion along the concentration gradient, from higher to lower concentration, without any requirement of energy.
