explanation: Neutral solutes move by simple diffusion; water moves by osmosis; polar molecules need a carrier protein; and the Na+/K+ pump is active transport using ATP.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: A non-living rigid structure called the cell wall forms an outer covering for the plasma membrane of fungi and plants.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: Algae have cell walls of cellulose, galactans, mannans and minerals like calcium carbonate; other plants have cellulose, hemicellulose, pectins and proteins. The middle lamella is mainly calcium pectate, and plasmodesmata connect the cytoplasm of neighbouring cells.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: As a plant cell matures, the secondary wall is formed on the inner (towards membrane) side of the primary wall. The middle lamella, mainly calcium pectate, holds neighbouring cells together. Both statements are true, but the composition of the middle lamella does not explain where the secondary wall forms.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: The cell wall gives shape, protects from mechanical damage and infection, helps in cell-to-cell interaction and provides a barrier to undesirable macromolecules. It is non-living; selective transport is a property of the plasma membrane.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
explanation: The primary wall of a young plant cell is capable of growth, which gradually diminishes as the cell matures. The secondary wall is then formed on the inner (towards membrane) side of the cell.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: The middle lamella glues neighbouring cells together. Inside it lies the primary wall, and the secondary wall is formed on the inner side towards the membrane, followed by the plasma membrane.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: It is a living, metabolically active outer layer
explanation: The cell wall is a non-living rigid structure covering the plasma membrane. It gives shape and protection, and the wall and middle lamella may be traversed by plasmodesmata.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: The ER, Golgi complex, lysosomes and vacuoles are considered together as the endomembrane system because their functions are coordinated. Mitochondria, chloroplasts and peroxisomes are excluded because their functions are not coordinated with these components.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: The ER divides the intracellular space into two distinct compartments, luminal (inside ER) and extra luminal (cytoplasm).
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: The smooth endoplasmic reticulum is the major site for synthesis of lipid. In animal cells lipid-like steroidal hormones are synthesised in SER.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: X has abundant rough ER; Y has abundant smooth ER
explanation: Rough ER is frequently observed in cells actively involved in protein synthesis and secretion. Smooth ER is the major site of lipid synthesis, and in animal cells steroidal hormones are synthesised in SER.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: Camillo Golgi (1898) first observed densely stained reticular structures near the nucleus, later named Golgi bodies after him.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: Golgi cisternae are 0.5 to 1.0 micrometre in diameter; mitochondria have a diameter of 0.2 to 1.0 micrometre (average 0.5); chloroplasts are 5 to 10 micrometre long; the perinuclear space is 10 to 50 nm.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
explanation: Golgi cisternae are concentrically arranged near the nucleus with a distinct convex cis or forming face and a concave trans or maturing face. Both statements reverse these descriptions.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Materials to be packaged in the form of vesicles from the ER fuse with the cis face of the Golgi and move towards the maturing face. This explains why the Golgi apparatus remains in close association with the ER.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: The Golgi apparatus is the important site of formation of glycoproteins and glycolipids.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: Proteins are synthesised by ribosomes on the ER, packaged into vesicles from the ER, which fuse with the cis face of the Golgi; they are modified in the cisternae and released from the trans face.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: Rough ER is found in cells active in protein synthesis and secretion; smooth ER synthesises lipids including steroidal hormones; Golgi forms glycoproteins and glycolipids; lysosomal hydrolases are optimally active at acidic pH.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: Lysosomes are very rich in almost all types of hydrolytic enzymes (hydrolases: lipases, proteases, carbohydrases) optimally active at acidic pH. These enzymes are capable of digesting carbohydrates, proteins, lipids and nucleic acids.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: In plant cells the vacuoles can occupy up to 90 per cent of the volume of the cell.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
explanation: In plants, the tonoplast facilitates the transport of a number of ions and other materials against concentration gradients into the vacuole, hence their concentration is significantly higher in the vacuole. Simple diffusion could not build up such a higher concentration.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: The contractile vacuole of Amoeba is important for osmoregulation and excretion; food vacuoles are formed by engulfing food particles in protists; the plant vacuole can occupy up to 90 per cent of cell volume; gas vacuoles occur in some photosynthetic bacteria.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: Ribosomes are attached to the outer surface of rough ER. The cis and trans faces of the Golgi are entirely different but interconnected. Lysosomal enzymes are optimally active at acidic pH, and a varied number of cisternae is present in a Golgi complex.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
explanation: The Golgi apparatus principally packages materials to be delivered either to intracellular targets or secreted outside the cell. Proteins made on ER ribosomes are modified in its cisternae before release from the trans face.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Formation of lysosomes and of glycoproteins
explanation: Lysosomes are formed by the process of packaging in the Golgi apparatus, and the Golgi is an important site of formation of glycoproteins and glycolipids. These would be affected; processes of SER, ribosomes and mitochondria would not be directly affected.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: produce cellular energy in the form of ATP
explanation: Mitochondria are the sites of aerobic respiration. They produce cellular energy in the form of ATP, hence they are called power houses of the cell.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Diameter 0.2 to 1.0 micrometre, length 1.0 to 4.1 micrometre
explanation: Mitochondria are typically sausage-shaped or cylindrical, with a diameter of 0.2 to 1.0 micrometre (average 0.5 micrometre) and length 1.0 to 4.1 micrometre.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Both statements are true. Mitochondria need specific staining to be seen, and their number per cell varies with physiological activity. Variation in number does not explain the need for staining.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
explanation: The outer membrane forms the continuous limiting boundary, while the inner membrane forms infoldings called cristae towards the matrix. Mitochondria divide by fission.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: The matrix possesses a single circular DNA molecule, a few RNA molecules, ribosomes (70S) and the components required for the synthesis of proteins. Its ribosomes are 70S, not 80S.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
explanation: The inner membrane forms a number of infoldings called cristae towards the matrix, and these increase the surface area. The outer membrane forms the continuous limiting boundary and is not folded into cristae.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: X is the outer compartment; Y is the matrix
explanation: Each mitochondrion is double membrane-bound, the outer and inner membranes dividing its lumen into two aqueous compartments: the outer compartment and the inner compartment, called the matrix. The inner membrane folds into cristae towards the matrix.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: The outer membrane forms the continuous limiting boundary, the inner membrane forms cristae towards the matrix, the matrix contains a single circular DNA, a few RNA molecules and 70S ribosomes, and mitochondria divide by fission.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: Amyloplasts store carbohydrates (starch), as in potato; elaioplasts store oils and fats; aleuroplasts store proteins; chromoplasts contain fat-soluble carotenoid pigments.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: Plastids are found in all plant cells and in euglenoides.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: 1 in Chlamydomonas to 20 to 40 in a mesophyll cell
explanation: The number of chloroplasts varies from 1 per cell of Chlamydomonas, a green alga, to 20 to 40 per cell in the mesophyll.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
explanation: Like mitochondria, chloroplasts are double membrane bound; of the two, the inner chloroplast membrane is relatively less permeable. The space limited by the inner membrane is called the stroma.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Flat membranous tubules called stroma lamellae connect the thylakoids of the different grana, and thylakoid membranes enclose a space called the lumen. Both are true, but the lumen does not explain the connecting role of stroma lamellae.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: The stroma contains enzymes required for the synthesis of carbohydrates and proteins, small double-stranded circular DNA molecules and ribosomes. Chlorophyll pigments are present in the thylakoids.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: Thylakoids are organised flattened membranous sacs in the stroma, stacked like piles of coins into grana. Stroma lamellae are flat membranous tubules connecting thylakoids of different grana, and thylakoid membranes enclose a space called the lumen.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: Leucoplasts are colourless plastids with stored nutrients. Amyloplasts store carbohydrates (starch), for example in potato.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Chlorophyll is in the thylakoids; grana are the site of light reactions
explanation: Chlorophyll pigments are present in the thylakoids. The grana are the site of light reactions and the stroma of dark reactions; the stroma contains enzymes for synthesis of carbohydrates and proteins.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
explanation: Leucoplasts are colourless plastids of varied shapes and sizes with stored nutrients, such as amyloplasts, elaioplasts and aleuroplasts. Trapping light is the function of chloroplasts.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: In chromoplasts, fat-soluble carotenoid pigments like carotene, xanthophylls and others are present, giving the part of the plant a yellow, orange or red colour.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: Ribosomes are granular structures first observed under the electron microscope as dense particles by George Palade (1953).
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: Eukaryotic cytoplasmic ribosomes are 80S, made of 60S and 40S subunits. Prokaryotic ribosomes are 70S, made of 50S and 30S subunits. Ribosomes of chloroplasts are 70S.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
explanation: Ribosomes are composed of RNA and proteins and are not surrounded by any membrane. S (Svedberg unit) stands for the sedimentation coefficient, which is indirectly a measure of density and size.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
explanation: The ribosomes of the chloroplasts are smaller (70S) than the cytoplasmic ribosomes (80S). The reason is true and shows that the assertion is false.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: The cytoskeleton, a network of microtubules, microfilaments and intermediate filaments, is involved in mechanical support, motility and maintenance of the shape of the cell. Ribosomal RNA is synthesised in the nucleolus.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
explanation: The cytoskeleton is an elaborate network of filamentous proteinaceous structures (microtubules, microfilaments and intermediate filaments) involved in mechanical support, motility and maintenance of cell shape. Cellulose and pectins are cell wall materials.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Cilia are small and work like oars; flagella are longer and move the cell
explanation: Cilia are small structures which work like oars, causing movement of either the cell or the surrounding fluid. Flagella are comparatively longer and responsible for cell movement. Both are covered with plasma membrane and emerge from basal bodies.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: The central tubules are connected by bridges and enclosed by a central sheath, which is connected to one of the tubules of each peripheral doublet by a radial spoke. The peripheral doublets are interconnected by linkers.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: The axoneme has nine doublets of peripheral microtubules (18) and a central pair (2), giving 20. A centriole has nine peripheral triplet fibrils (27) and a proteinaceous hub, not central microtubules.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
explanation: Electron microscopic study shows that cilia and flagella are covered with plasma membrane. Their core, the axoneme, possesses a number of microtubules running parallel to the long axis.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
explanation: The central sheath is connected to one of the tubules of each of the nine peripheral doublets by a radial spoke, so there are nine radial spokes. Adjacent peripheral doublets are interconnected by linkers, not by radial spokes.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: Cilia are small and work like oars; eukaryotic flagella are comparatively longer and move the cell; bacterial flagella have filament, hook and basal body; fimbriae help some bacteria attach to rocks and host tissues.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: The central part of the proximal region of the centriole is proteinaceous and called the hub, which is connected with the tubules of the peripheral triplets by radial spokes made of protein.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
explanation: A centriole is made up of nine evenly spaced peripheral fibrils of tubulin protein, each a triplet. The adjacent triplets are also linked.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: The centrosome usually contains two cylindrical centrioles surrounded by amorphous pericentriolar materials. They lie perpendicular to each other, each with a cartwheel organisation, and form the basal body of cilia or flagella. The centre of a centriole is a proteinaceous hub, not a pair of microtubules.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: The centrosome usually contains two centrioles; the hub is the proteinaceous central part of the proximal region of a centriole; cilia and flagella emerge from centriole-like basal bodies; centrioles form spindle fibres that give rise to the spindle apparatus in animal cells.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: Robert Brown described the nucleus in 1831; Flemming gave the name chromatin to the material of the nucleus stained by basic dyes; George Palade observed ribosomes in 1953; Singer and Nicolson proposed the fluid mosaic model in 1972.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: A single human cell has approximately two metre long thread of DNA distributed among its forty six (twenty three pairs) chromosomes.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: At a number of places the nuclear envelope is interrupted by minute pores formed by the fusion of its two membranes. These pores are passages for two-way movement of RNA and protein. Both statements are true, but the mode of pore formation does not explain the direction of traffic.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Sieve tube cell of a vascular plant
explanation: Some mature cells even lack a nucleus, for example erythrocytes of many mammals and sieve tube cells of vascular plants.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
explanation: Nucleoli are spherical structures in the nucleoplasm. The content of the nucleolus is continuous with the rest of the nucleoplasm as it is not a membrane bound structure. It is a site for active rRNA synthesis, so the reason is true.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo108.pdf)

explanation: Cells in G0 remain metabolically active but do not proliferate unless required. Plants show mitosis in both haploid and diploid cells, and in some lower plants and social insects haploid cells also divide by mitosis. Heart cells of adult animals do not appear to divide, so IV is wrong.

correct_answer: Haploid and usually genetically identical to the parent
explanation: Mitosis is an equational division: daughter cells have the same chromosome number and usually the same genetic complement as the parent. A haploid cell dividing mitotically therefore yields haploid, genetically identical daughters.

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
explanation: Interphase occupies more than 95 percent of the cycle. The M phase is the most dramatic period of the cycle, involving a major reorganisation of virtually all components of the cell. Both statements are incorrect.

correct_answer: Parent and progeny cells have the same chromosome number
explanation: Since the number of chromosomes in the parent and progeny cells is the same, mitosis is called equational division.

correct_answer: Assertion is false, but Reason is true

explanation: In prophase, each centrosome radiates out microtubules called asters. The two asters together with the spindle fibres form the mitotic apparatus.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: Cells at the end of prophase do not show Golgi complexes, endoplasmic reticulum, nucleolus or the nuclear envelope. These re-form during telophase.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: complete disintegration of the nuclear envelope
explanation: The complete disintegration of the nuclear envelope marks the start of metaphase, so chromosomes are spread through the cytoplasm of the cell.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Condensation of chromosomes is complete by metaphase and they are clearly visible, which is why chromosome morphology is most easily studied at this stage. The Reason explains the Assertion.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo110.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: small disc-shaped structures at the surface of centromeres
explanation: Small disc-shaped structures at the surface of the centromeres are called kinetochores. They serve as the sites of attachment of spindle fibres to the chromosomes.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo110.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: A metaphase chromosome consists of two sister chromatids held together by the centromere, and the plane of chromosome alignment is called the metaphase plate. Both are true, but the name of the plate does not explain why chromosomes have two chromatids.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: During anaphase, the centromere of each chromosome remains directed towards the pole and hence at the leading edge, with the arms of the chromosome trailing behind.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo110.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
explanation: At the onset of anaphase, each chromosome at the metaphase plate splits simultaneously, and the two daughter chromatids, now called chromosomes of the future daughter nuclei, migrate to opposite poles. Both statements are correct.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo110.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Nucleolus, Golgi complex and endoplasmic reticulum
explanation: In telophase, a nuclear envelope develops around the chromosome clusters at each pole, and the nucleolus, Golgi complex and ER re-form.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo110.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: Prophase: asters radiate from centrosomes. Metaphase: sister kinetochores attach to fibres from opposite poles. Anaphase: centromere leads, arms trail. Telophase: chromosomes lose individuality and collect at the poles.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo110.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: Asters are microtubules radiating from each centrosome; kinetochores are disc-shaped structures at the centromere surface; the metaphase plate is the plane of chromosome alignment; the cell plate is the wall precursor representing the middle lamella.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo110.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: Centrosomes begin moving to opposite poles in prophase; complete disintegration of the nuclear envelope marks the start of metaphase; chromatids migrate in anaphase; Golgi and ER re-form in telophase.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo110.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: starts in the centre and grows outward to the lateral walls
explanation: In plant cells, wall formation starts in the centre of the cell and grows outward to meet the existing lateral walls. It begins with a simple precursor called the cell plate.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: middle lamella between the walls of two adjacent cells
explanation: The formation of the new cell wall begins with a simple precursor, the cell plate, which represents the middle lamella between the walls of two adjacent cells.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo110.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Because plant cells are enclosed by a relatively inextensible cell wall, they cannot divide by furrowing; instead they form a cell plate that grows from the centre outward. The Reason explains the Assertion.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: In some organisms karyokinesis is not followed by cytokinesis, giving a multinucleate condition called a syncytium, for example the liquid endosperm in coconut.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Coconut liquid endosperm is a syncytium because karyokinesis is not followed by cytokinesis. The inextensible plant cell wall is true, but it explains why plants use a cell plate, not why a syncytium forms.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Animal: a furrow deepens and joins in the centre; plant: a wall grows from the centre outward
explanation: In an animal cell, a furrow appears in the plasma membrane, gradually deepens and joins in the centre. In a plant cell, the new wall starts in the centre as a cell plate and grows outward to meet the lateral walls.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: A single cell with two nuclei
explanation: Karyokinesis gives two daughter nuclei, but without cell-plate formation the cytoplasm is not divided. The result is one cell with two nuclei, a condition like the syncytium that arises when karyokinesis is not followed by cytokinesis.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: At metaphase each chromosome consists of two sister chromatids held by the centromere. Therefore 46 chromosomes contain 46 x 2 = 92 chromatids.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: Mitosis is equational: each daughter cell keeps the parental chromosome number (18) and receives half the G2 DNA, i.e. 2C.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: Statements I, III and IV are correct. At telophase chromosomes decondense and lose their individuality; maximum condensation and the clearest morphology are seen at metaphase.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: In telophase, chromosomes that have reached their poles decondense and lose their individuality; chromatin collects at each pole and a nuclear envelope forms around each cluster.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo110.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: Metaphase is characterised by complete condensation, absence of the nuclear envelope, and all chromosomes at the equator with sister kinetochores attached to fibres from opposite poles.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: In anaphase, the daughter chromosomes migrate to opposite poles with the centromere at the leading edge and the arms trailing behind, giving bent shapes in diagrams.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: Karyokinesis finishes with daughter nuclei at the poles. Cytokinesis then begins with a cell plate in the centre, which grows outward until it meets the lateral walls.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: meristematic tissues, the apical and lateral cambium
explanation: Mitotic divisions in the meristematic tissues, the apical and the lateral cambium, result in continuous growth of plants throughout their life.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Cell growth disturbs the ratio between the nucleus and the cytoplasm, so it becomes essential for the cell to divide to restore the nucleo-cytoplasmic ratio. The Reason explains the Assertion.

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
explanation: Mitosis usually produces diploid daughter cells with identical genetic complement. It is usually restricted to diploid cells, but in some lower plants and some social insects haploid cells also divide by mitosis. Both statements are correct.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: Replacement of upper epidermal cells is cell repair by mitosis; apical and lateral cambium give continuous plant growth; disturbed nucleo-cytoplasmic ratio is restored by division; haploid gametes arise by meiosis in gametogenesis.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Increasing genetic variability in a population
explanation: Mitosis produces daughter cells with identical genetic complement; it supports growth, repair and restoration of the nucleo-cytoplasmic ratio. Increasing genetic variability is a significance of meiosis.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: Mitosis drives growth of multicellular organisms, replaces cells such as blood cells, and is usually restricted to diploid cells. It produces genetically identical daughter cells, so II is wrong.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Some lower plants and social insects show haploid mitosis
explanation: Mitosis is usually restricted to diploid cells, but in some lower plants and in some social insects haploid cells also divide by mitosis. Being equational, it simply keeps the haploid number unchanged.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Assertion is true, but Reason is false

correct_answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Meiosis produces the haploid phase and fertilisation restores the diploid phase. Both statements are true, but fertilisation is a separate event and does not explain how meiosis yields haploid cells.

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Because the DNA is replicated once but the cell divides twice, each of the four products receives half the chromosome number. The Reason explains the Assertion.

correct_answer: chromosomes replicate in S phase to form sister chromatids

explanation: Meiosis I starts after replication in S phase has produced sister chromatids, and there is no DNA replication during interkinesis. Both statements are incorrect.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: Crossing over is the exchange of genetic material between homologous chromosomes. It is an enzyme-mediated process, and the enzyme involved is called recombinase.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
explanation: Crossing over occurs at recombination nodules during pachytene, but it is an enzyme-mediated process involving recombinase. The Assertion is true and the Reason is false.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: The beginning of diplotene is recognised by the dissolution of the synaptonemal complex and the tendency of the recombined homologues to separate except at the sites of crossovers.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
explanation: The synaptonemal complex forms during zygotene along with synapsis and dissolves at the beginning of diplotene. The Assertion is false and the Reason is true.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo110.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Diplotene can last for months or years in oocytes of some vertebrates, and its onset is marked by dissolution of the synaptonemal complex. Both are true, but the dissolution of the complex does not explain the long duration.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: In diakinesis chromosomes are fully condensed, the meiotic spindle is assembled, and by its end the nucleolus disappears and the nuclear envelope breaks down. The synaptonemal complex forms in zygotene and dissolves in diplotene.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
explanation: Diakinesis is marked by terminalisation of chiasmata, and the chromosomes are fully condensed at this stage. Only Statement I is correct.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo110.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: Leptotene: chromosomes gradually become visible. Zygotene: synapsis with synaptonemal complex. Pachytene: recombination nodules appear. Diplotene: synaptonemal complex dissolves.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo110.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: Diakinesis: terminalisation of chiasmata. Diplotene: may last months or years in some vertebrate oocytes. Zygotene: pairing of homologues. Pachytene: recombinase-mediated crossing over.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: Leptotene: compaction continues. Pachytene: four chromatids of each bivalent become distinct. Diplotene: homologues tend to separate except at crossovers. Diakinesis: chromosomes fully condensed and spindle assembled.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo110.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: Prophase I proceeds through leptotene, zygotene, pachytene, diplotene and diakinesis. Of the four given, the order is zygotene, pachytene, diplotene, diakinesis.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo110.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: The synaptonemal complex dissolves at the start of diplotene, chiasmata terminalise in diakinesis, homologues separate in anaphase I, and centromeres split in anaphase II.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo110.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: Dissolution of the synaptonemal complex with homologues held only at X-shaped chiasmata marks diplotene. Full condensation and spindle assembly come later, in diakinesis.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo110.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Crossing over occurs in pachytene; chiasmata are seen in diplotene
explanation: Recombination is completed by the end of pachytene, leaving homologues linked at crossover sites. These sites become visible as chiasmata only when homologues begin to separate in diplotene.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo110.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: In metaphase I the bivalents align on the equatorial plate, and microtubules from opposite poles attach to the pair of homologous chromosomes. This prepares homologues, not sister chromatids, for separation.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo110.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: In anaphase I, homologous chromosomes separate, while sister chromatids remain associated at their centromeres. This is why each product of meiosis I has chromosomes with two chromatids.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo110.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: Metaphase I: bivalents align on the equator. Anaphase I: homologues separate. Telophase I with cytokinesis: dyad of cells. Telophase II with cytokinesis: tetrad of four haploid cells.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo110.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
explanation: In telophase I the chromosomes may undergo some dispersion but do not reach the extremely extended state of the interphase nucleus. Interkinesis is generally short-lived. Only Statement II is correct.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo110.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: generally short-lived and lacks DNA replication
explanation: Interkinesis, the stage between meiosis I and meiosis II, is generally short-lived and there is no replication of DNA during it. It is followed by prophase II.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo110.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
explanation: The stage between the two meiotic divisions is interkinesis, and there is no replication of DNA during it. The Assertion is true and the Reason is false.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo110.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: In telophase I the nuclear membrane and nucleolus reappear, and cytokinesis gives a dyad of cells. Chromosomes do not reach the fully extended interphase state, and prophase II is much simpler than prophase I.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo110.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: right after cytokinesis, before chromosomes fully elongate
explanation: Meiosis II is initiated immediately after cytokinesis, usually before the chromosomes have fully elongated. In contrast to meiosis I, it resembles a normal mitosis.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo110.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: At metaphase II the chromosomes align at the equator and microtubules from opposite poles attach to the kinetochores of sister chromatids, preparing them for separation in anaphase II.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo110.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
explanation: Meiosis II resembles a normal mitosis: sister chromatids separate, so each product keeps the same chromosome number it had at the start of meiosis II. The Assertion is false and the Reason is true.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo110.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
explanation: Anaphase II begins with the simultaneous splitting of the centromere of each chromosome. In anaphase I, homologues separate while sister chromatids remain associated at their centromeres. The Assertion is true and the Reason is false.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo110.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
explanation: In metaphase I microtubules attach to the pair of homologous chromosomes, and anaphase I separates homologues, not sister chromatids. In anaphase II, chromatids move to opposite poles by shortening of microtubules attached to kinetochores. Only Statement II is correct.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo110.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: Prophase II: nuclear membrane disappears and chromosomes become compact. Metaphase II: microtubules attach to sister kinetochores. Anaphase II: centromeres split simultaneously. Telophase II: nuclear envelopes form and four haploid cells result.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo110.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: The synaptonemal complex dissolves at the start of diplotene; diakinesis ends with loss of nucleolus and nuclear envelope as the transition to metaphase; telophase I restores nuclear membrane and nucleolus and gives a dyad; metaphase II has sister kinetochores attached to opposite poles.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo110.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: Interkinesis lies between the two divisions; diakinesis is the transition to metaphase I; prophase II is much simpler; prophase I is long and complex with five substages.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo110.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Anaphase I: homologues separate, centromeres intact; anaphase II: centromeres split, sister chromatids separate
explanation: In anaphase I, homologous chromosomes separate while sister chromatids remain associated at their centromeres. Anaphase II begins with the simultaneous splitting of centromeres, so sister chromatids move to opposite poles.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo110.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Prophase I is long and complex with five substages; prophase II is much simpler
explanation: Prophase I is typically longer and more complex, with leptotene, zygotene, pachytene, diplotene and diakinesis. Prophase II, which follows a short interkinesis without DNA replication, is much simpler.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo110.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: Crossing over occurs in pachytene of prophase I. Meiosis II resembles mitosis: the nuclear membrane disappears in prophase II, chromosomes align in metaphase II and centromeres split in anaphase II.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo110.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: Statements I, II and III are correct. In metaphase II, microtubules attach to the kinetochores of sister chromatids; attachment to homologous pairs is the feature of metaphase I.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo110.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: Statements I, III and IV are correct. Terminalisation of chiasmata marks diakinesis, not diplotene; diplotene is marked by dissolution of the synaptonemal complex and appearance of chiasmata.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo110.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: Pachytene shows distinct tetrads and recombination nodules where crossing over occurs. The synaptonemal complex dissolves at the start of diplotene, and terminalisation of chiasmata occurs in diakinesis.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo110.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: Meiosis II resembles mitosis, the nuclear membrane disappears by the end of prophase II, and telophase II with cytokinesis gives a tetrad of four haploid cells. There is no DNA replication in interkinesis.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo110.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: conservation of the specific chromosome number across generations
explanation: Meiosis halves the chromosome number in gametes, and fertilisation restores it. In this way the specific chromosome number of each species is conserved across generations.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo110.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
explanation: Meiosis conserves the chromosome number across generations even though, paradoxically, the process itself halves the chromosome number; fertilisation restores the diploid number. Both statements are correct.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo110.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Meiosis increases genetic variability from one generation to the next, and variations are very important for evolution. The Reason explains the Assertion.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo110.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: Meiosis halves the chromosome number, increases genetic variability, and variations are important for evolution. It does not double the chromosome number; fertilisation restores it.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo110.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: A bivalent is a pair of synapsed homologous chromosomes. With 24 chromosomes, there are 24/2 = 12 homologous pairs, hence 12 bivalents.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: There are 10 bivalents, and in pachytene the four chromatids of each bivalent become distinct as tetrads. So the cell has 10 x 4 = 40 chromatids.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: After S phase the meiocyte has 12 pg. Meiosis I divides this between two cells, each with 6 pg. There is no replication in interkinesis, so a cell at metaphase II still has 6 pg; meiosis II then gives 3 pg per cell.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: After meiosis I each cell has 10 chromosomes, each with two chromatids. In anaphase II the centromeres split, and each chromatid counts as a chromosome, so the cell temporarily has 20 chromosomes, 10 moving to each pole.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: Four haploid cells are formed at the end of meiosis II from one meiocyte. To obtain 400 haploid cells, 400/4 = 100 cells must undergo meiosis.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: Each round doubles the number of cells, so after n rounds there are 2^n cells. 2^7 = 128, so 7 rounds are needed.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo110.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: In anaphase I, homologues separate, so each pole receives 10 chromosomes. Sister chromatids remain associated at their centromeres, so each pole receives 10 x 2 = 20 chromatids.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: Meiosis I separates homologous chromosomes while sister chromatids stay together, so each product of meiosis I has 23 chromosomes with two chromatids each. Meiosis II then separates the chromatids.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: G2 meiocyte: 20 chromosomes with 40 chromatids. Metaphase I: 10 bivalents. After meiosis I: 10 chromosomes, each still with two chromatids, so III is wrong. After meiosis II: 10 chromosomes, each with one chromatid.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo110.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: After S phase the meiocyte has 4C, so prophase I has 4C and I is wrong. Meiosis I gives cells with 2C, which is unchanged through interkinesis because there is no replication. Meiosis II gives cells with 1C.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: G2 cell: 12 chromosomes (replication does not change number). One bivalent: 4 chromatids. Pachytene: 12/2 = 6 bivalents. Mitotic metaphase: 12 x 2 = 24 chromatids.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: G1 meiocyte: 2n, 2C. Metaphase I: 2n, 4C (after S phase). After meiosis I: n chromosomes with two chromatids each, 2C. After meiosis II: n, C.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo110.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: S phase doubles DNA without changing chromosome number; meiosis I halves chromosome number while chromosomes retain two chromatids; meiosis II separates sister chromatids, completing four haploid cells; mitosis gives two cells identical to the parent.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo110.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

explanation: Chromosomes move to the spindle equator in metaphase; centromeres split and chromatids separate in anaphase; homologues pair in zygotene; crossing over occurs in pachytene.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo110.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 3: Cell Structure and Function

correct_answer: absorbs CO2 from the air inside the tube

explanation: PEP in mesophyll cells is carboxylated by PEPcase to OAA, which forms malic or aspartic acid. These move to bundle sheath cells, where they release CO2 and a 3-carbon molecule that returns to mesophyll cells to form PEP again.

explanation: C3 plants fix CO2 on RuBP forming 3-PGA; C4 plants fix CO2 on PEP forming OAA.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

correct_answer: Cell types fixing CO2: one in C3, two in C4; carbons in primary acceptor: 5 in C3, 3 in C4
explanation: In C3 plants, mesophyll cells alone fix CO2 onto 5-carbon RuBP. In C4 plants, mesophyll cells fix CO2 onto 3-carbon PEP and bundle sheath cells re-fix it through RuBisCO, so two cell types are involved.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

explanation: OAA forms in mesophyll cells; C4 acids are decarboxylated in bundle sheath cells, which lack PEPcase. The 3-carbon molecule is transported back to mesophyll cells, where it is converted to PEP.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Both statements are correct features of C4 leaves. The site of OAA formation does not explain why bundle sheath walls are impervious to gases.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
explanation: In C3 plants the Calvin pathway occurs in all mesophyll cells. In C4 plants it does not take place in mesophyll cells but only in bundle sheath cells.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

explanation: Bundle sheath cells may form several layers around vascular bundles and are characterised by a large number of chloroplasts, thick walls impervious to gaseous exchange and no intercellular spaces.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

explanation: Kranz anatomy is the wreath-like arrangement of bundle sheath cells; the C4 pathway is the Hatch and Slack pathway; Calvin traced the C3 pathway using 14C; Blackman gave the law of limiting factors.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

correct_answer: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
explanation: In C4 plants PEP is the primary acceptor and the first stable product is the 4-carbon OAA, not PGA.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
explanation: C4 acids are decarboxylated in bundle sheath cells. The released CO2 enters the Calvin cycle, while the 3-carbon molecule returns to mesophyll cells and is converted to PEP.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

explanation: C4 mesophyll cells have PEPcase but no RuBisCO; C4 bundle sheath cells have RuBisCO but no PEPcase and get CO2 from C4 acids; C3 mesophyll cells fix CO2 directly by the Calvin cycle; thylakoids carry out the light reaction.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

explanation: RuBisCO is the most abundant enzyme in the world; PEPcase fixes CO2 in C4 mesophyll cells; ATP synthase has F0 and F1 parts; NADP reductase reduces NADP+ on the stroma side.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Both are true: RuBisCO is the most abundant enzyme, and its active site binds both CO2 and O2. The ability to bind both gases does not explain its abundance.
