syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
explanation: CO2 and O2 compete for the active site of RuBisCO, and their relative concentrations decide which binds.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

correct_answer: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
explanation: RuBisCO has a much greater affinity for CO2 than for O2 when their concentrations are nearly equal. Even so, some O2 binds RuBisCO in C3 plants, decreasing CO2 fixation.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

explanation: Carboxylation of RuBP gives two 3-PGA; oxygenation gives one phosphoglycerate and one phosphoglycolate; PEP carboxylation gives OAA; decarboxylation of C4 acids gives CO2 and a 3-carbon molecule.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
explanation: In photorespiration RuBP binds O2 to form one phosphoglycerate and one phosphoglycolate, not two PGA. There is no synthesis of ATP or NADPH in this pathway.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

correct_answer: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
explanation: In C4 plants photorespiration does not occur because C4 acids broken down in bundle sheath cells raise the CO2 concentration at the RuBisCO site, so it acts as a carboxylase.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

explanation: Photorespiration releases CO2 while using ATP and makes neither sugar, ATP nor NADPH, so it is wasteful. It does not occur in C4 plants because CO2 is concentrated in bundle sheath cells.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

explanation: C4 plants lack photorespiration, have a higher temperature optimum, use 3-carbon PEP as primary acceptor and involve two cell types in CO2 fixation.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

explanation: The CO2 concentrating mechanism of C4 plants ensures RuBisCO acts as a carboxylase, minimising its oxygenase activity, so photorespiration is avoided. PEPcase is in mesophyll cells and does not fix O2.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

explanation: RuBP has 5 carbons; one product is 3-carbon phosphoglycerate, so phosphoglycolate has 5 - 3 = 2 carbons.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

correct_answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
explanation: In C3 plants some O2 binds RuBisCO, and photorespiration releases CO2, so fixed carbon is lost. In C4 plants the C4 acid releases CO2 in bundle sheath cells, keeping RuBisCO acting as a carboxylase.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

explanation: Blackman stated the law in 1905; light saturation occurs at about 10 per cent of full sunlight; atmospheric CO2 is 0.03 to 0.04 per cent; an increase up to 0.05 per cent can raise CO2 fixation rates.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

explanation: C4 plants saturate at about 360 microlitre per litre, while C3 plants respond to increased CO2 and saturate only beyond 450 microlitre per litre. At low light neither group responds to high CO2; at high light both show increased photosynthesis.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

explanation: Plant factors include the number, size, age and orientation of leaves, mesophyll cells and chloroplasts, internal CO2 concentration and the amount of chlorophyll. Sunlight is an external factor.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

explanation: The response is linear at low light, saturating at about 10 per cent of full sunlight; very high light breaks down chlorophyll. Except for plants in shade or dense forests, light is rarely limiting in nature.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

correct_answer: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
explanation: Light rarely limits photosynthesis in nature because saturation occurs at about 10 per cent of full sunlight, not 50 per cent.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Even though water is a reactant in the light reaction, its effect as a factor is mainly through the plant: water stress closes stomata, reducing CO2 availability, and causes wilting, which reduces leaf surface area and metabolic activity. The reason is true but does not explain the assertion.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

correct_answer: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
explanation: C3 plants keep responding to increased CO2, and saturation is seen only beyond 450 microlitre per litre; about 360 microlitre per litre is the saturation value for C4 plants. Hence current CO2 levels limit C3 plants.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

correct_answer: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
explanation: Dark reactions, being enzymatic, are temperature controlled. Light reactions are also temperature sensitive, but much less so.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
explanation: C4 plants respond to higher temperatures and show higher rates, while C3 plants have a much lower temperature optimum. Tropical plants have a higher temperature optimum than temperate plants.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
explanation: Blackman stated the law in 1905; 1854 relates to Sachs. An increase in CO2 up to 0.05 per cent can increase fixation, but beyond this levels can become damaging over longer periods.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
explanation: Water stress closes stomata, reducing CO2 availability, and causes wilting, which reduces leaf surface area and metabolic activity.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

explanation: Water stress closes stomata; excessive light breaks down chlorophyll; a leaf at very low temperature may not photosynthesise despite optimal light and CO2; at low light the rate rises linearly with light.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

explanation: Greenhouse tomatoes give higher yields in CO2-enriched air; C4 plants have higher temperature optima; light limits plants on dense forest floors; wilting reduces leaf surface area and metabolic activity.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

explanation: Dark reactions are enzymatic and temperature controlled; light reactions are less sensitive; C4 plants respond to higher temperatures; C3 plants have a much lower optimum.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

explanation: External factors include the availability of sunlight, temperature, CO2 concentration and water. The amount of chlorophyll is an internal (plant) factor.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

correct_answer: temperature was the factor nearest its minimal value and therefore set the rate
explanation: When a process is affected by more than one factor, its rate is determined by the factor nearest its minimal value. Here temperature was limiting; raising it allowed photosynthesis to start.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

explanation: CO2 is the major limiting factor; it is 0.03 to 0.04 per cent of the air. C3 plants saturate only beyond 450 microlitre per litre, so they still respond above 360. This response is used to raise yields of greenhouse tomatoes and bell pepper.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

explanation: Respiration is the oxidation of complex compounds within cells, breaking their C-C bonds and releasing energy. Combustion also oxidises but happens in a single uncontrolled step outside the cell.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo112.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

explanation: Respiratory substrates are the compounds oxidised; RQ is CO2 evolved over O2 consumed; the respiratory pathway is amphibolic because it serves both breakdown and synthesis; oxidative phosphorylation uses redox energy to make ATP.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo112.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

explanation: Usually carbohydrates are oxidised, but proteins, fats and organic acids can also serve in some plants. The energy is not used directly; it is used to make ATP, which is broken down when energy is needed. Carbon skeletons from respiration act as precursors for biosynthesis.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo112.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Energy from oxidation is stored as ATP and released by breaking ATP wherever work must be done; this storing and spending role is what the term energy currency describes.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo112.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

correct_answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
explanation: Statement I is correct. Statement II is wrong: only cells with chloroplasts, mostly in superficial layers, photosynthesise, so non-green cells need food translocated to them for oxidation.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

correct_answer: Roots are non-green, so food must be translocated to them for oxidation
explanation: Only chloroplast-containing cells photosynthesise. All other living cells, including root cells, still respire and must receive food translocated from photosynthetic parts.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo112.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

correct_answer: It is given out as heat
explanation: In combustion, most of the energy of glucose escapes as heat. Cells avoid this by oxidising glucose in several small steps so that some steps release just enough energy to be coupled to ATP synthesis.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo112.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

correct_answer: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
explanation: Combustion releases energy in one step, mostly as heat. It is the cell that oxidises glucose in several small, enzyme-controlled steps, coupling some of them to ATP synthesis.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo112.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

explanation: Plants lack specialised respiratory organs; stomata and lenticels allow gaseous exchange by diffusion.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo112.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

explanation: Each part meets its own needs, plant organs respire slowly, and every living cell lies close to the surface so diffusion distances are short. Plants do not present great demands for gas exchange, so IV is wrong.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo112.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

correct_answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
explanation: Statement I is wrong: plants respire at low rates and exchange large gas volumes only during photosynthesis; they have no specialised organs. Statement II is correct and explains why diffusion suffices.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo112.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

correct_answer: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
explanation: Interior stem cells are dead and serve only for mechanical support, so they do not respire and need no oxygen. The living cells are in thin layers beneath the bark, close to the surface.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo112.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

correct_answer: Inside and beneath the bark, in thin layers
explanation: The living cells of stems are organised in thin layers inside and beneath the bark, which keeps them close to the surface for gas exchange; interior cells are dead.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo112.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

correct_answer: It forms a connected network of air spaces reaching most cells
explanation: Loose packing leaves an interconnected network of air spaces, so most cells have at least part of their surface in contact with air and exchange gases by diffusion.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo112.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
explanation: Both are wrong. Plants have no specialised respiratory organs; stomata and lenticels suffice because most cells have at least a part of their surface in contact with air.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo112.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

explanation: Lenticels are openings in the bark of stems through which gases diffuse to the living cells beneath.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

explanation: Large gas volumes are exchanged only during photosynthesis, each leaf is adapted to handle this itself, and photosynthesising cells release oxygen internally. There is very little transport of gases between plant parts, so IV is wrong.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

explanation: Among present-day organisms adapted to anaerobic conditions, some are facultative anaerobes, able to live with or without oxygen, while others are obligate anaerobes.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

explanation: All living organisms, including anaerobes, retain the machinery to partially oxidise glucose without oxygen, that is glycolysis. In anaerobes it is the only respiratory process, so the assertion is false.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

explanation: The letters E, M and P stand for Embden, Meyerhof and Parnas, who gave the scheme of glycolysis.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 4: Plant Physiology

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: Group A has anti-B, group B has anti-A, group AB has no natural antibodies, and group O has both anti-A and anti-B.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: Group A receives from A and O, B from B and O, AB from AB, A, B and O, and O only from O.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: AB persons have no natural anti-A or anti-B antibodies in plasma and can accept blood from persons with AB as well as the other groups.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Group O RBCs have no A or B antigens, so the antibodies in any recipient's plasma do not attack them; hence group O persons can donate to any group.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
explanation: Group AB plasma lacks both anti-A and anti-B (Nil), which is why AB persons are universal recipients. The Reason describes group O.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: Group B plasma has anti-A, so donor RBCs must lack antigen A; donors of group B and group O are suitable.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: Group A plasma carries anti-B. Donor group B RBCs carry antigen B, which this antibody recognises.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: The Rh antigen, similar to one in Rhesus monkeys, is present on RBCs of the majority, nearly 80 per cent, of humans, who are called Rh positive.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
explanation: An Rh-ve person forms anti-Rh antibodies on exposure to Rh+ve blood. Therefore the Rh group should also be matched before transfusions.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: Exposure during the first delivery sensitises the mother, who forms anti-Rh antibodies; in a later pregnancy these enter an Rh+ve foetus and destroy its RBCs.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: giving anti-Rh antibodies to the mother right after this delivery
explanation: Erythroblastosis foetalis can be avoided by administering anti-Rh antibodies to the mother immediately after delivery of the first child.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Rh antigens of the foetus do not reach the Rh-ve mother's blood in the first pregnancy because the placenta separates the two bloods; exposure happens during delivery.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: The condition arises when an Rh-ve mother carries an Rh+ve foetus after sensitisation; her antibodies destroy foetal RBCs, causing severe anaemia and jaundice, and it could be fatal.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: No, since the foetal RBCs lack the Rh antigen
explanation: Maternal anti-Rh antibodies destroy only Rh+ve RBCs. An Rh-ve foetus has no Rh antigen, so it is not affected.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: chemicals that can induce an immune response
explanation: Antigens are chemicals that can induce an immune response; antibodies are proteins produced in response to antigens.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: Rh is named after a similar antigen in Rhesus monkeys and is present in nearly 80 per cent of humans. Anti-Rh antibodies given to the mother after the first delivery prevent erythroblastosis foetalis. Group O persons are universal donors.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: Nearly 80 per cent of humans are Rh+ve. Anti-Rh antibodies are not natural; an Rh-ve person forms them after exposure, so the Rh group must be matched before transfusion.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: Group B donor to group A recipient
explanation: Group A plasma has anti-B, which acts against the B antigen of group B donor RBCs.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
explanation: Group O plasma contains anti-A and anti-B. Group AB RBCs carry both A and B antigens and the plasma has no natural antibodies.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: AB plasma lacks natural antibodies; group B blood can go to B and AB; group A receives from A and O. Group O can receive only from O.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: A clot is a network of fibrin threads in which dead and damaged formed elements of blood are trapped.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: Injury stimulates platelets to release factors; a cascade forms thrombokinase; thrombokinase helps convert prothrombin to thrombin; thrombin converts fibrinogen to fibrin.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: Thrombokinase is the enzyme complex needed to form thrombin from inactive prothrombin; thrombin converts fibrinogen into fibrin threads.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Calcium ions play a very important role in the clotting process, so removing them from blood interferes with coagulation.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
explanation: Both platelets and injured tissues release factors that can start coagulation. Thrombokinase is formed by a cascade of linked enzymic reactions involving many factors.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: Plasma is straw coloured and viscous; lymph is colourless; a dark reddish brown scum forms at a cut; haemoglobin is a red coloured, iron containing complex protein.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: The clot is a network of fibrin threads, formed from fibrinogen by thrombin, in which dead and damaged formed elements are trapped.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: Thrombin forms from inactive prothrombin through thrombokinase
explanation: Thrombin is formed from prothrombin, an inactive plasma substance; the enzyme complex thrombokinase is required for this reaction.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Fewer platelets cause clotting disorders and excessive blood loss because platelets release clotting substances. Their origin from megakaryocytes is true but not the explanation.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: a cascade of linked enzymic reactions of inactive plasma factors
explanation: Thrombokinase is formed by a cascade process: a series of linked enzymic reactions involving a number of factors present in plasma in an inactive state.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: X: platelets; Y: thrombokinase; Z: thrombin
explanation: Platelets release factors after injury; the cascade forms thrombokinase; thrombokinase helps form thrombin from prothrombin; thrombin forms fibrin.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: Fibrinogen, prothrombin and cascade factors are present in plasma in inactive forms. Fibrin is formed only during clotting.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: water and small solutes move out, leaving larger proteins behind
explanation: Some water and small water soluble substances move out of capillaries into spaces between cells, forming interstitial or tissue fluid; larger proteins and most formed elements stay in the vessels.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
explanation: Tissue fluid has the same mineral distribution as plasma, and exchange of nutrients and gases between blood and cells always occurs through it.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: An elaborate network of lymphatic vessels collects the tissue fluid and drains it back to the major veins.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Fats are absorbed through lymph in the lacteals present in the intestinal villi. Lymph also contains specialised lymphocytes for immunity, a true but unrelated fact.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: It has plasma-like minerals but lacks larger proteins and most formed elements
explanation: Tissue fluid forms by filtration of water and small solutes, so it has the same mineral distribution as plasma but lacks the larger proteins and most formed elements.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: Lymph is colourless, contains specialised lymphocytes responsible for immune responses, and carries nutrients and hormones.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: Transport of oxygen bound to haemoglobin
explanation: Lymph carries nutrients, hormones and absorbed fats and contains lymphocytes. Oxygen transport by haemoglobin is a function of RBCs in blood.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: Larger proteins and most formed elements stay within vessels, so tissue fluid lacks them but shares the mineral distribution of plasma. It mediates all exchange with cells and is drained by lymphatics into major veins.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: Arthropods and molluscs have an open circulatory system in which blood from the heart passes through large vessels into sinuses.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: Fishes show single circulation, amphibians incomplete double circulation, birds double circulation, while molluscs have an open circulatory system.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
explanation: Amphibians and reptiles have a three chambered heart except crocodiles, which, like birds and mammals, have a four chambered heart.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: The heart is about the size of a clenched fist; the inter-atrial septum is thin and muscular, the inter-ventricular septum thick walled, and the AV septum thick fibrous tissue. Ventricular walls are much thicker than atrial walls.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: the flow of fluid can be more precisely regulated
explanation: In closed systems blood always circulates through a closed network of vessels, so the flow of fluid can be more precisely regulated.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
explanation: The fish heart has one atrium and one ventricle and pumps deoxygenated blood to the gills; oxygenated blood goes to the body and deoxygenated blood returns to the heart, which is single circulation.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: In amphibians and reptiles, the left atrium receives oxygenated blood and the right atrium deoxygenated blood, but these mix in the single ventricle, which pumps out mixed blood; this is incomplete double circulation.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: The heart pumps deoxygenated blood to the gills, from where oxygenated blood goes to the body
explanation: In fishes, the heart pumps out deoxygenated blood, which is oxygenated by the gills and supplied to the body; deoxygenated blood returns to the heart. This is single circulation.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: Annelids and chordates have a closed circulatory system; arthropods and molluscs have an open one.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: an amphibian with incomplete double circulation
explanation: Two atria with one ventricle, and gills, lungs or skin as respiratory surfaces, indicate an amphibian; mixing in the ventricle gives incomplete double circulation.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: Fishes have two chambers; amphibians and reptiles other than crocodiles have three (two atria, one ventricle); crocodiles, birds and mammals have four.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: Open systems use sinuses; all vertebrates have a chambered heart; birds and mammals show no mixing. In amphibians, the right atrium receives deoxygenated blood and the left atrium oxygenated blood.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: Arthropods have open circulation with sinuses; annelids are invertebrates with closed circulation; sponges circulate water from their surroundings; crocodiles have a four chambered heart in a closed system.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: Fishes have two chambers; amphibians and reptiles (except crocodiles) three; crocodiles four.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: mesodermally derived organ in the thoracic cavity, slightly tilted to the left
explanation: The heart is mesodermally derived, lies in the thoracic cavity between the two lungs, slightly tilted to the left, and is about the size of a clenched fist.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: a double walled pericardium enclosing pericardial fluid
explanation: The heart is protected by the pericardium, a double walled membranous bag that encloses pericardial fluid.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: The inter-atrial septum is thin and muscular, the inter-ventricular septum thick walled, the atrio-ventricular septum thick fibrous tissue, and the pericardium a double walled bag.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
explanation: The tricuspid valve has three muscular flaps and guards the opening between the right atrium and right ventricle.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: exits of the ventricles into the pulmonary artery and aorta
explanation: The openings of the right and left ventricles into the pulmonary artery and aorta respectively are provided with semilunar valves.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
explanation: Heart valves prevent backward flow and permit one-way flow. The entire heart is made of cardiac muscle, with the ventricle walls much thicker than the atrial walls.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: right upper corner of the right atrium
explanation: A patch of nodal tissue present in the right upper corner of the right atrium is the SAN.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: lower left corner of the right atrium, near the AV septum
explanation: The AVN is a mass of nodal tissue in the lower left corner of the right atrium, close to the atrio-ventricular septum.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: The impulse starts at the SAN, passes to the AVN, then the AV bundle and its right and left bundles, and finally the Purkinje fibres in the ventricles.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: Nodal tissue is autoexcitable; the AV bundle emerges on the inter-ventricular septum and divides; Purkinje fibres with the bundles form the bundle of His. The SAN, not the AVN, fires most often.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: The SAN generates the maximum number of action potentials, 70-75 per minute, and so initiates and maintains the rhythm; hence it is the pacemaker. Its location in the right upper corner of the right atrium is true but does not explain this.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: They are specialised cardiac musculature that is autoexcitable
explanation: Nodal tissue is specialised cardiac musculature distributed in the heart; it is autoexcitable, which makes the heart myogenic.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: Our heart normally beats 70-75 times a minute, about 72 on average, set by the SAN.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: The tricuspid valve has three cusps on the right side; the bicuspid or mitral valve is on the left. Semilunar valves guard the right ventricle's exit into the pulmonary artery and the left ventricle's exit into the aorta.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: The vena cava opens into the right atrium, which bears the SAN at its upper right corner and opens into the right ventricle through the tricuspid valve.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: Pulmonary veins bring oxygenated blood to the left atrium, vena cava brings deoxygenated blood to the right atrium, the aorta leaves the left ventricle and the pulmonary artery leaves the right ventricle.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: backflow of some blood from the left ventricle into the left atrium
explanation: The bicuspid valve closes during ventricular systole to prevent attempted backflow into the left atrium; if it fails, blood leaks back from the left ventricle to the left atrium.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo115.pdf)

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: Cross bridges cannot be broken, so the fibre stays in the contracted state

explanation: Both are due to excess GH. When excess occurs in adults, especially in middle age, it causes severe disfigurement, particularly of the face, called acromegaly; excess during growth causes gigantism.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: Prolactin acts on mammary glands, ACTH on the adrenal cortex, MSH on melanocytes and TSH on the thyroid.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: In males LH stimulates androgen secretion from testis, and FSH with androgens regulates spermatogenesis. In females LH induces ovulation and maintains the corpus luteum, and FSH stimulates growth and development of ovarian follicles.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: LH and FSH stimulate gonadal activity and hence are called gonadotrophins. They are produced by the pars distalis.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: LH stimulates androgen secretion in males and, in females, induces ovulation of graafian follicles and maintains the corpus luteum. FSH stimulates follicle growth in females and, with androgens, regulates spermatogenesis in males.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
explanation: LH maintains the corpus luteum, which forms from the remnants of the graafian follicle after ovulation. FSH stimulates growth of ovarian follicles.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Oxytocin stimulates smooth muscle contraction and milk ejection; prolactin regulates mammary growth and milk formation. Both are true, but milk formation by prolactin does not explain ejection by oxytocin.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: Reduces loss of water through urine
explanation: Vasopressin acts mainly at the kidney and stimulates resorption of water and electrolytes by the distal tubules, reducing water loss through urine (diuresis); hence it is the antidiuretic hormone.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: Impaired synthesis or release of ADH diminishes the kidney's ability to conserve water, causing water loss and dehydration; this is diabetes insipidus.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Diabetes insipidus results from impaired synthesis or release of ADH. Since ADH normally drives water resorption by the distal tubules, its lack reduces water conservation; the reason explains the assertion.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: Insipidus arises from impaired ADH; mellitus involves loss of glucose in urine
explanation: Diabetes insipidus follows impaired synthesis or release of ADH. Diabetes mellitus results from prolonged hyperglycemia and is associated with loss of glucose in urine and formation of ketone bodies.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: Over-secretion of GH gives gigantism, low secretion gives pituitary dwarfism, excess in adults gives acromegaly, and impaired ADH gives diabetes insipidus.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: The pars intermedia secretes MSH, the pineal melatonin, the thymus thymosins and the parathyroid PTH.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: TSH, ACTH and LH come from the pars distalis, so thyroid hormones, glucocorticoids and androgens would fall. Vasopressin is made in the hypothalamus and released from the intact neurohypophysis.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: Both hormones are made in the hypothalamus and transported axonally to the neurohypophysis. Oxytocin causes vigorous uterine contraction at childbirth. Vasopressin reduces water loss in urine, that is, it is antidiuretic.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
explanation: Milk ejection is stimulated by oxytocin, which also causes uterine contraction at childbirth. Prolactin regulates mammary growth and milk formation.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: Oxytocin contracts smooth muscles, vasopressin promotes water resorption, prolactin regulates milk formation and GH promotes body growth.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: Excess GH in adults causes severe disfigurement, especially of the face, which may lead to serious complications and premature death if unchecked.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
explanation: The neurohypophysis (pars nervosa), also known as the posterior pituitary, stores and releases oxytocin and vasopressin synthesised by the hypothalamus.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: The pars distalis (anterior pituitary) produces GH, PRL, TSH, ACTH, LH and FSH; the pars intermedia, almost merged with it in humans, secretes MSH, which regulates skin pigmentation.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
explanation: The adenohypophysis consists of pars distalis and pars intermedia, so the assertion is true. The pars intermedia secretes only MSH; oxytocin is made in the hypothalamus and released from the neurohypophysis.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
explanation: Acromegaly results from excess, not deficiency, of GH in adults, so the assertion is false. Over-secretion of GH leads to gigantism, so the reason is true.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: The pineal gland is located on the dorsal side of the forebrain and secretes melatonin.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: Melatonin regulates the 24-hour diurnal rhythm of the body, such as the sleep-wake cycle and body temperature.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: Melatonin maintains the normal rhythms of the sleep-wake cycle and body temperature, and also influences metabolism, pigmentation, the menstrual cycle and defense capability.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
explanation: Melatonin from the pineal influences metabolism and pigmentation, but MSH is secreted by the pars intermedia of the pituitary.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
explanation: The pineal lies on the dorsal side of the forebrain, so the assertion is false. Melatonin maintains the normal sleep-wake rhythm, so the reason is true.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: Melatonin from the pineal; MSH from the pars intermedia
explanation: The pineal secretes melatonin, which influences pigmentation among other effects; the pars intermedia secretes MSH, which acts on melanocytes.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: The thyroid has two lobes on either side of the trachea, interconnected by a thin flap of connective tissue called the isthmus.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: The thyroid is composed of follicles and stromal tissues. Each follicle is composed of follicular cells enclosing a cavity.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: The thyroid gland is composed of two lobes located on either side of the trachea.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: Follicular cells synthesise two hormones, tetraiodothyronine or thyroxine (T4) and triiodothyronine (T3).
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Iodine is essential for the normal rate of thyroid hormone synthesis, so its dietary deficiency lowers hormone production, causing hypothyroidism and goitre.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: Hypothyroidism during pregnancy causes defective development of the baby, leading to stunted growth (cretinism), mental retardation, low intelligence quotient, abnormal skin and deaf-mutism. Protrusion of eyeballs is a feature of exophthalmic goitre.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
explanation: Hypothyroidism may make the menstrual cycle irregular in adult women. During pregnancy it causes defective development and maturation of the growing baby, so the second statement is wrong.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: Graves' disease is exophthalmic goitre; Addison's disease follows underproduction of adrenal cortex hormones; diabetes insipidus reflects reduced water conservation by the kidney; cretinism follows hypothyroidism in pregnancy.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: Exophthalmic goitre, a form of hyperthyroidism, is characterised by thyroid enlargement, protrusion of eyeballs, increased basal metabolic rate and weight loss.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: Nodules or cancer of the thyroid can raise thyroid hormone secretion to abnormally high levels, causing hyperthyroidism. Exophthalmic goitre shows thyroid enlargement, protruding eyeballs, increased BMR and weight loss.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: Cretinism follows hypothyroidism in pregnancy; simple goitre follows iodine deficiency; exophthalmic goitre is hyperthyroidism with eyeball protrusion; irregular menstrual cycles can follow hypothyroidism in adult women.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: Thyroid hormones regulate BMR, support RBC formation, control carbohydrate, protein and fat metabolism and influence water and electrolyte balance. Stimulating renal Ca2+ reabsorption is an action of PTH.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
explanation: Maintenance of water and electrolyte balance is influenced by thyroid hormones. Thyrocalcitonin is a protein hormone, not a steroid. Both statements are wrong.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: The thyroid also secretes a protein hormone called thyrocalcitonin (TCT), which regulates blood calcium levels. T3 and T4 are iodothyronines.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
explanation: Cancer or nodules of the thyroid can raise thyroid hormone secretion to abnormally high levels, causing hyperthyroidism. Hyperthyroidism, as in exophthalmic goitre, increases the BMR, so the reason is false.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: Simple goitre with hypothyroidism; exophthalmic goitre with hyperthyroidism
explanation: Iodine deficiency causes hypothyroidism with thyroid enlargement (goitre). Exophthalmic goitre is a form of hyperthyroidism with protrusion of eyeballs and raised BMR.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Iodine deficiency leads to hypothyroidism and goitre. Thyroid hormones do control carbohydrate, protein and fat metabolism, but that does not explain why the gland enlarges.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: TCT is a protein hormone of the thyroid, PTH a peptide hormone of the parathyroid, T4 an iodothyronine made by follicular cells, and thymosins peptide hormones of the thymus.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: Four, on the back side of the thyroid
explanation: Four parathyroid glands are present on the back side of the thyroid gland, one pair each in the two lobes.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: The parathyroid glands secrete a peptide hormone called parathyroid hormone (PTH).
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: The secretion of PTH is regulated by the circulating levels of calcium ions.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: PTH stimulates bone resorption, renal tubular reabsorption of Ca2+ and absorption of Ca2+ from digested food. All of these raise blood Ca2+.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: PTH stimulates bone resorption (demineralisation), renal reabsorption of Ca2+ and absorption from food, all of which increase blood Ca2+. These actions make it a hypercalcemic hormone.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
explanation: PTH and TCT together maintain calcium balance. PTH increases blood Ca2+ by stimulating bone resorption, not mineralisation.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: PTH is a peptide raising blood Ca2+; TCT is a protein secreted by the thyroid
explanation: PTH is a peptide hormone of the parathyroid that increases blood Ca2+. TCT is a protein hormone of the thyroid that regulates blood calcium; together they maintain calcium balance.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: PTH is hypercalcemic. Without it, bone resorption, renal Ca2+ reabsorption and intestinal Ca2+ absorption would decrease, lowering blood Ca2+.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: PTH acts on bones, renal tubules and absorption of Ca2+ from digested food. The islets of Langerhans are pancreatic endocrine tissue regulating glucose.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: Between the lungs behind the sternum, ventral to the aorta
explanation: The thymus is a lobular structure located between the lungs behind the sternum on the ventral side of the aorta.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: The thymus secretes peptide hormones called thymosins.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
explanation: Thymosins play a major role in T-lymphocyte differentiation for cell-mediated immunity and also promote antibody production for humoral immunity.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Thymosins drive T-lymphocyte differentiation and antibody production. Degeneration of the thymus in old age reduces thymosins, so immune responses become weak.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: The thymus is lobular, lies between the lungs behind the sternum and degenerates with age. Thymosins are peptide hormones, not steroids.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: Promotion of antibody production for humoral immunity
explanation: In addition to T-lymphocyte differentiation, thymosins promote antibody production to provide humoral immunity. Cortisol, by contrast, suppresses the immune response.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: At the anterior part of each kidney
explanation: The body has one pair of adrenal glands, one at the anterior part of each kidney.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: The adrenal medulla secretes adrenaline (epinephrine) and noradrenaline (norepinephrine), commonly called catecholamines.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: The adrenal cortex has zona glomerulosa (outer), zona fasciculata (middle) and zona reticularis (inner) layers; the medulla is central.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: Catecholamines increase alertness, pupillary dilation, piloerection and sweating, and increase heart beat, strength of heart contraction and rate of respiration.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Catecholamines are called emergency hormones because they are rapidly secreted in response to stress and emergency situations. The central location of the medulla is true but does not explain the name.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
explanation: Catecholamines stimulate breakdown of glycogen, increasing blood glucose, and also stimulate breakdown of lipids and proteins. So only the second statement is correct.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: Cortisol is the main glucocorticoid, aldosterone the main mineralocorticoid, adrenaline a catecholamine, and testosterone the main androgen of the testis.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: Glucocorticoids are corticoids involved in carbohydrate metabolism; mineralocorticoids regulate water and electrolyte balance; catecholamines are fight or flight hormones; small amounts of adrenal androgens aid hair growth at puberty.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: Zona glomerulosa is the outer, zona fasciculata the middle and zona reticularis the inner layer of the cortex; the medulla is central.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

explanation: Glucocorticoids stimulate gluconeogenesis, lipolysis and proteolysis, and inhibit cellular uptake and utilisation of amino acids. Cortisol produces anti-inflammatory reactions and suppresses the immune response.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 5: Human Physiology

correct_answer: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
explanation: Glucocorticoids, particularly cortisol, produce anti-inflammatory reactions and suppress the immune response. Cortisol stimulates, not inhibits, RBC production.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XI, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (kebo119.pdf)

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

explanation: Synergids have special cellular thickenings at the micropylar tip called the filiform apparatus, which guide pollen tubes into the synergid.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)

correct_answer: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
explanation: One megaspore is functional and three degenerate (monosporic development). The MMC undergoes meiosis, not mitosis, to form the four megaspores.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
