syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Complete autogamy in open (chasmogamous) flowers is rare because it needs synchrony of pollen release and stigma receptivity and close placement of anthers and stigma.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

explanation: Some plants such as Viola (common pansy), Oxalis and Commelina produce chasmogamous flowers with exposed anthers and stigma, and cleistogamous flowers that do not open.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
explanation: Cleistogamous flowers do not open; anthers dehisce in the bud and pollen contacts the stigma, so they are invariably autogamous and give assured seed-set without pollinators.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

explanation: Geitonogamy transfers pollen to another flower of the same plant; it needs a pollinating agent (functionally cross-pollination) but the pollen is from the same plant (genetically like autogamy).
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

explanation: Autogamy in open flowers needs synchrony and closeness of anther and stigma; geitonogamy needs an agent but is genetically selfing; only xenogamy brings genetically different pollen; cleistogamous flowers never open.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

correct_answer: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
explanation: Chasmogamous flowers are similar to flowers of other species with exposed anthers and stigma; it is the cleistogamous flowers that do not open at all.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

correct_answer: Most plants use biotic agents, and wind is the commoner abiotic agent
explanation: The majority of plants use biotic agents; only a small proportion use abiotic agents, and among them wind pollination is more common than water pollination.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

explanation: Wind-pollinated flowers have light, non-sticky pollen, well-exposed stamens and large, often feathery stigmas; they are not colourful and produce no nectar.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Both statements are true, but the commonness of wind pollination in grasses does not explain why wind-pollinated flowers have single ovules and crowded inflorescences.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

explanation: In the corn cob the tassels seen are the stigma and style, which wave in the wind to trap pollen grains.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

correct_answer: Not very colourful and do not produce nectar
explanation: Wind- and water-pollinated flowers are not very colourful and do not produce nectar, since they need not attract animals.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

explanation: Pollination by water is rare, limited to about 30 genera, mostly monocotyledons.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: In most aquatic plants such as water hyacinth and water lily, the flowers emerge above the level of water and are pollinated by insects or wind, as in most land plants. Since the flowers are out of the water, water is not their pollinating agent. The Reason explains the Assertion.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

correct_answer: Vallisneria pollen is released on the water surface; sea-grass pollen is released inside water
explanation: In Vallisneria the female flower reaches the surface by a long stalk and male flowers or pollen are released on the surface; in sea grasses female flowers remain submerged and pollen is released inside water.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

explanation: In most water-pollinated species, pollen grains are protected from wetting by a mucilaginous covering.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

correct_answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
explanation: Water regularly transports male gametes in algae, bryophytes and pteridophytes. Zostera is a marine sea grass whose female flowers remain submerged and pollen is released inside water.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

correct_answer: Long, ribbon-like and carried passively inside water
explanation: In sea grasses, pollen grains are released inside water; in many species they are long and ribbon-like and carried passively to the stigma.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

explanation: Insects, particularly bees, are dominant pollinators; flies and beetles are attracted by foul odours; lemurs (primates) and gecko lizards (reptiles) are reported pollinators in some species.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

explanation: Besides insects, birds (sunbirds, humming birds) and bats, larger animals such as lemurs, arboreal rodents and reptiles like gecko and garden lizards are reported pollinators.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

correct_answer: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
explanation: Flowers pollinated by flies and beetles do secrete foul odours. Insect-pollinated flowers are generally large, colourful, fragrant and rich in nectar, so the reason is false.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

explanation: Amorphophallus offers a safe egg-laying site; in the sea grass Zostera pollen is released inside water; water hyacinth flowers emerge above water and are insect or wind pollinated; Commelina bears chasmogamous and cleistogamous flowers.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

correct_answer: Yucca in that region cannot complete its life cycle
explanation: The moth and Yucca cannot complete their life cycles without each other; the moth pollinates the flower while its larvae emerge as seeds develop.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

explanation: Floral rewards are nectar and pollen, and in some species (Amorphophallus) a safe place to lay eggs. Robbers take rewards without pollinating. Insect-pollinated flowers are generally large, colourful, fragrant and nectar-rich.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
explanation: Animal-pollinated pollen is generally sticky; light non-sticky pollen is a wind-pollination feature. Small insect-pollinated flowers are clustered into inflorescences to make them conspicuous.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

explanation: Viola produces cleistogamous flowers; Vallisneria female flowers reach the surface by a long stalk; Yucca is pollinated by a moth; corn is wind-pollinated.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

explanation: Vallisneria, Hydrilla and Zostera are water-pollinated. In water lily the flowers emerge above water and are pollinated by insects or wind.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

explanation: Continued self-pollination results in inbreeding depression, so flowering plants have evolved devices to discourage self-pollination.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

explanation: Monoecy (castor, maize) prevents autogamy but not geitonogamy; dioecy (papaya) places sexes on different plants; self-incompatibility genetically blocks self-pollen; cleistogamy ensures autogamy.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

correct_answer: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
explanation: Papaya is dioecious: male and female flowers are on different plants, which prevents both autogamy and geitonogamy. The reason describes monoecy, as in castor and maize.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

explanation: Non-synchronised pollen release and stigma receptivity (either way) and different positions of anther and stigma discourage selfing. Cleistogamous flowers ensure autogamy.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

correct_answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
explanation: Self-incompatibility prevents self-pollen, from the same flower or other flowers of the same plant, from fertilising ovules by inhibiting pollen germination or tube growth.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

explanation: Inhibition of germination of self-pollen in the pistil, with acceptance of non-self pollen, is self-incompatibility, a genetic mechanism.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

explanation: In monoecious plants (castor, maize) unisexual flowers prevent autogamy, but pollen can reach a female flower of the same plant, so geitonogamy is possible.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

correct_answer: Pollen deposition on the stigma until pollen tubes enter the ovule
explanation: All events from deposition of pollen on the stigma until pollen tubes enter the ovule are together referred to as pollen-pistil interaction, a dynamic process.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

explanation: The pollen germinates on the stigma through a germ pore, the tube grows through stigma and style to the ovary, enters the ovule through the micropyle and then a synergid through the filiform apparatus.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Both are true. Recognition is mediated by chemical components of pollen interacting with those of the pistil; germination through a germ pore is an event that follows acceptance, not its explanation.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
explanation: In 2-celled pollen the generative cell divides during pollen tube growth; in 3-celled pollen the two male gametes are present from the beginning.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

correct_answer: About 10 per cent sugar solution and observe after 15-30 minutes
explanation: Pollen of pea, chickpea, Crotalaria, balsam or Vinca dusted on a drop of about 10 per cent sugar solution shows pollen tubes after about 15-30 minutes under low power.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

explanation: If the pollen is incompatible, the pistil rejects it by preventing pollen germination on the stigma or pollen tube growth in the style. No enzyme is known to degrade sporopollenin.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

explanation: The pollen tube emerges through a germ pore, the pollen contents move into it, it enters the ovule through the micropyle and then a synergid through the filiform apparatus.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

explanation: If the female parent bears bisexual flowers, anthers are removed from the bud before dehiscence with forceps; this is emasculation.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

explanation: Emasculated flowers are covered with a bag of suitable size, generally made of butter paper, to prevent contamination of the stigma with unwanted pollen.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

explanation: Anthers are removed from the bud before dehiscence; flowers are covered with butter paper bags; after dusting pollen the flowers are rebagged. Unisexual female flowers need no emasculation.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

correct_answer: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
explanation: If the female parent bears unisexual flowers there is no need for emasculation; female flower buds are bagged before they open. Bagging does protect the stigma from unwanted pollen.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

correct_answer: Some may result from unwanted pollen, so hybrid purity is not assured
explanation: Bagging prevents contamination of the stigma with unwanted pollen. Without it, foreign pollen may reach the stigma, so the progeny may not all be the intended hybrid.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

correct_answer: Bag female buds before opening, then pollinate and rebag
explanation: With unisexual female flowers there is no need for emasculation; female buds are bagged before opening, pollinated with desired pollen when receptive, and rebagged.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

explanation: Syngamy involves one male gamete and the egg nucleus (2), triple fusion involves the second male gamete and two polar nuclei (3): total 5.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

correct_answer: Cytoplasm of one of the synergids
explanation: The pollen tube enters one of the synergids and releases the two male gametes into its cytoplasm; one moves to the egg and the other to the polar nuclei.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Since it involves fusion of three haploid nuclei (one male gamete and two polar nuclei), it is termed triple fusion, producing the triploid PEN.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

correct_answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
explanation: Syngamy of one haploid male gamete with the haploid egg gives a diploid zygote; the PEN is triploid. Double fertilisation is unique to flowering plants.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

explanation: Syngamy gives the diploid zygote; triple fusion gives the triploid PEN; the central cell becomes the PEC that develops into endosperm; the synergid receives the male gametes.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

explanation: The egg is haploid (n = 12). The PEN is formed by fusion of three haploid nuclei, so it is triploid: 3n = 36.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

explanation: The PEN arises from two polar nuclei (maternal, from the embryo sac) and one male gamete (paternal), giving two maternal sets and one paternal set.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Endosperm develops first because its cells store reserve food for the embryo; most zygotes divide only after some endosperm is formed, ensuring assured nutrition.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
source_page: NCERT section: Post-fertilisation: Structures and Events
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

explanation: Coconut water is free-nuclear endosperm made of thousands of nuclei; the surrounding white kernel is cellular endosperm.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
source_page: NCERT section: Post-fertilisation: Structures and Events
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

explanation: In pea the endosperm is consumed; in castor it persists; tender coconut water is free-nuclear endosperm; beet has persistent nucellus (perisperm).
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
source_page: NCERT section: Post-fertilisation: Structures and Events
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

explanation: The PEC forms triploid endosperm whose cells store food; in the common type free nuclei form first and then walls; the number of free nuclei before cellularisation varies greatly.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
source_page: NCERT section: Post-fertilisation: Structures and Events
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

explanation: 2n = 16, so n = 8. The endosperm is triploid (3n = 24); antipodals are haploid cells of the embryo sac (n = 8).
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
source_page: NCERT section: Post-fertilisation: Structures and Events
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

explanation: Endosperm is consumed before maturation in pea, groundnut and beans; it persists in castor, coconut, wheat, maize and barley.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
source_page: NCERT section: Post-fertilisation: Structures and Events
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

explanation: The embryo develops at the micropylar end; most zygotes divide after some endosperm forms. The zygote gives a proembryo, then globular, heart-shaped and mature embryos, and early embryogeny is similar in monocots and dicots.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
source_page: NCERT section: Post-fertilisation: Structures and Events
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

explanation: The zygote gives rise to the proembryo and subsequently to the globular, heart-shaped and mature embryo.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)
source_page: NCERT section: Post-fertilisation: Structures and Events
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

explanation: Above the cotyledons is the epicotyl ending in the plumule; below is the hypocotyl ending in the radicle, which is covered by a root cap.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo101.pdf)

correct_answer: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
explanation: Oxytocin acting on the uterine muscle during parturition is released from the maternal pituitary in response to the foetal ejection reflex. The placenta produces hCG, hPL, estrogens and progestogens, not oxytocin.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

explanation: The foetal ejection reflex is the mild uterine contraction induced by foetal and placental signals; oxytocin from the maternal pituitary causes stronger contractions; colostrum is the early milk; parturition is expulsion of the baby through the birth canal.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

explanation: Each breast has 15 to 20 mammary lobes; 60,000 to 80,000 primary follicles remain in each ovary at puberty; 200 to 300 million sperms are ejaculated per coitus; each oviduct is about 10 to 12 cm long.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

correct_answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
explanation: The foetal ejection reflex consists of mild uterine contractions induced by foetal and placental signals. The placenta is expelled soon after the infant is delivered, not before.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

correct_answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
explanation: Formation of gametes is gametogenesis; gestation is embryonic development within the uterus. Insemination is the transfer of sperms into the female genital tract.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

explanation: Mammary glands differentiate during pregnancy and begin producing milk towards its end, a process called lactation, not parturition. Colostrum, the milk of the initial few days of lactation, contains antibodies.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

explanation: Stronger uterine contractions stimulate further oxytocin secretion; this stimulatory reflex continues, resulting in stronger and stronger contractions that expel the baby. The placenta is expelled soon after.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

explanation: At least 60 per cent of sperms must have normal shape and size (60 per cent of 250 million = 150 million) and at least 40 per cent must show vigorous motility (40 per cent of 250 million = 100 million).
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

correct_answer: Mild contractions occur, but they fail to become stronger, delaying expulsion of the baby
explanation: Foetal and placental signals induce mild contractions (foetal ejection reflex), which trigger oxytocin release. Oxytocin acting on uterine muscle produces stronger contractions in a stimulatory loop; blocking its action prevents this build-up.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo102.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

explanation: WHO defines reproductive health as total well-being in all aspects of reproduction, that is physical, emotional, behavioural and social. Absence of disease alone does not make a person reproductively healthy.

source_page: NCERT section: Reproductive Health: Problems and Strategies
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Medically assisted deliveries and better post-natal care reduce maternal and infant mortality, and this decrease is one of the signs of improved reproductive health of the society. The reason therefore explains the assertion.

source_page: NCERT section: Reproductive Health: Problems and Strategies
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

explanation: India started national level programmes for total reproductive health very early, from 1951. These programmes were periodically assessed and improved, leading to the present RCH programmes, so Statement II is incorrect.

correct_answer: Give right information and dispel myths about sex
explanation: Sex education in schools provides right information to the young and discourages children from believing in myths and misconceptions about sex-related aspects. Parents, teachers and others continue to play a role.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

explanation: Couples are educated about birth control options, care of pregnant mothers, post-natal care of mother and child, importance of breast feeding and equal opportunities for the male and the female child. correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Awareness of problems from uncontrolled population growth and of sex-related social evils is created so that people can take steps to prevent them and build a socially responsible healthy society. The reason gives the purpose of the strategy and so explains it.

explanation: The statutory ban on amniocentesis for sex determination was imposed to legally check the increasing female foeticides, as sex determination was frequently followed by abortion of female foetuses.

correct_answer: Determining the sex of the unborn child
explanation: The statutory ban is on amniocentesis for sex determination. Its misuse to find the sex of the unborn child, frequently followed by MTP if the foetus is female, is against the law and promotes female foeticide.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 6: Reproduction

explanation: Since ovulation is expected from day 10 to 17, avoiding coitus during this fertile period reduces chances of ovum and sperm meeting. The reason directly explains the assertion.

correct_answer: The male withdraws the penis just before ejaculation

explanation: Lactational amenorrhoea depends on absence of ovulation during intense lactation following parturition. It is effective only up to a maximum period of six months after parturition, and its chances of failure are high.

correct_answer: alteration of DNA sequences and consequently changes in the genotype and phenotype of an organism

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Both are true. Chromosomal aberrations are commonly observed in cancer cells, and UV radiation is a physical mutagen. The Reason does not explain the Assertion.

correct_answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
explanation: Insertion or deletion of base pairs causes frame-shift mutations. Sickle-cell anaemia is a classical example of a point mutation, a single base substitution, not a frame shift.

correct_answer: five unaffected offspring whose sex is not specified

explanation: Unaffected parents with an affected child means the trait is recessive and both parents are carriers. Because the affected daughter's father is unaffected, an X-linked recessive mode is ruled out, so the trait is autosomal recessive.

explanation: A dominant allele is expressed whenever present, so the trait appears in every generation and each affected person has an affected parent. Equal occurrence in both sexes suggests an autosomal gene.

explanation: HbA HbS x HbA HbS gives 1 HbA HbA : 2 HbA HbS : 1 HbS HbS. So 1/4 affected, 1/2 carriers and 1/4 homozygous normal. Among the three unaffected, two are carriers, i.e. 2/3.

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
explanation: Common Mendelian disorders include haemophilia, cystic fibrosis, sickle-cell anaemia, colour blindness, phenylketonuria and thalassemia. They follow Mendelian inheritance and can be traced in a family by pedigree analysis.

correct_answer: A single protein that is part of the cascade of proteins involved in blood clotting
explanation: Haemophilia is a sex-linked recessive disease in which a single protein of the clotting cascade is affected. Hence, in an affected individual a simple cut results in non-stop bleeding.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo104.pdf)

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: A haemophilic female must receive the recessive allele from both parents. Her father must be haemophilic (such males are unviable in the later stage of life) and her mother at least a carrier, which makes such females extremely rare.

explanation: The family pedigree of Queen Victoria shows a number of haemophilic descendants, as she was a carrier of the disease.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 7: Genetics and Evolution

explanation: A carrier mother passes the allele to half her sons (affected) and half her daughters (carriers, as the father's X is normal). An affected father passes his X to all daughters, making them carriers, and his Y to all sons, who are normal.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo104.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 7: Genetics and Evolution

explanation: Every daughter receives the father's Xh. From the carrier mother she receives Xh with probability 1/2. So a daughter is XhXh (haemophilic) with probability 1/2.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 7: Genetics and Evolution

explanation: The daughter receives her father's X carrying the allele, so she is a carrier. Each of her sons receives one of her two X chromosomes, so the probability of a colour-blind son is 1/2.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo104.pdf)

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Males have one X, so a single recessive allele produces colour blindness, while females need two. Hence the trait occurs in about 8 per cent of males and only about 0.4 per cent of females.

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
explanation: Colour blindness is a sex-linked recessive disorder due to a defect in either the red or the green cone, resulting in failure to discriminate between red and green colour. Both statements are wrong.

correct_answer: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
explanation: A son receives one of his mother's two X chromosomes, so he has a 50 per cent chance of being colour blind. The carrier mother is not herself colour blind, because the gene is recessive and her other X is normal.

correct_answer: glutamic acid by valine at the sixth position of the beta globin chain
explanation: In sickle-cell anaemia, glutamic acid (Glu) is replaced by valine (Val) at the sixth position of the beta globin chain of haemoglobin.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo104.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 7: Genetics and Evolution

explanation: A single base substitution at the sixth codon of the beta globin gene from GAG to GUG replaces glutamic acid by valine.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo104.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 7: Genetics and Evolution

explanation: Sickle-cell anaemia is autosome-linked recessive, controlled by HbA and HbS. Only HbS HbS individuals show the disease; HbA HbS are apparently unaffected carriers. The mutant haemoglobin polymerises under low oxygen tension, changing RBC shape.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo104.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 7: Genetics and Evolution

explanation: The gene change (GAG to GUG) causes the amino acid change (Glu to Val) in the beta globin chain. The mutant haemoglobin polymerises under low oxygen tension, which changes RBC shape to a sickle.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo104.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 7: Genetics and Evolution

correct_answer: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
explanation: The carrier parent passes HbS with probability 1/2, so half the children are expected to be HbA HbS. Heterozygotes appear apparently unaffected; only HbS HbS individuals show the disease, so the Reason is false.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo104.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 7: Genetics and Evolution

correct_answer: a reduced rate of synthesis of one of the globin chains of haemoglobin
explanation: In thalassemia, mutation or deletion reduces the rate of synthesis of one of the globin chains (alpha or beta) of haemoglobin. Abnormal haemoglobin molecules are formed, resulting in anaemia. A single amino acid substitution in the beta chain is the basis of sickle-cell anaemia instead.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo104.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 7: Genetics and Evolution

explanation: Alpha thalassemia is controlled by two closely linked genes HBA1 and HBA2 on chromosome 16 of each parent, so four genes in all. Beta thalassemia is controlled by a single gene HBB on chromosome 11. In sickle-cell anaemia, the sixth amino acid of the beta globin chain is substituted.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo104.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 7: Genetics and Evolution

correct_answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
explanation: Thalassemia is a quantitative problem of synthesising too few globin molecules; sickle-cell anaemia is the qualitative problem of an incorrectly functioning globin. Beta thalassemia is controlled by the single gene HBB on chromosome 11 and arises from mutation of one or both genes.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo104.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 7: Genetics and Evolution

explanation: Thalassemia produces abnormal haemoglobin and anaemia. Alpha thalassemia arises from mutation or deletion of one or more of the four alpha globin genes, and more affected genes means fewer alpha globin molecules. In beta thalassemia, the beta globin chain is affected, so statement IV is wrong.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo104.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 7: Genetics and Evolution

correct_answer: the amino acid phenylalanine into tyrosine
explanation: Phenylketonuria is an inborn error of metabolism inherited as an autosomal recessive trait. The affected individual lacks the enzyme that converts phenylalanine into tyrosine, so phenylalanine accumulates.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo104.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 7: Genetics and Evolution

explanation: The missing enzyme means phenylalanine is not converted to tyrosine, so it accumulates. It is converted into phenylpyruvic acid and other derivatives, whose accumulation in the brain results in mental retardation; they are also excreted in urine.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo104.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 7: Genetics and Evolution

explanation: An affected child shows that both parents are heterozygous carriers. A cross of two heterozygotes gives 1/4 homozygous normal, 1/2 heterozygous carriers and 1/4 affected. The probability that the next child is a normal carrier is therefore 1/2.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo104.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 7: Genetics and Evolution

correct_answer: failure of segregation of chromatids during cell division cycle
explanation: Failure of segregation of chromatids during the cell division cycle results in gain or loss of chromosomes, called aneuploidy. Failure of cytokinesis after telophase results in polyploidy.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo104.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 7: Genetics and Evolution

correct_answer: polyploidy, resulting from failure of cytokinesis after telophase
explanation: Failure of cytokinesis after telophase increases a whole set of chromosomes; this is polyploidy and is often seen in plants. Aneuploidy, including trisomy, arises from failure of chromatid segregation.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo104.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 7: Genetics and Evolution

explanation: Down's syndrome, caused by an additional copy of chromosome 21, was first described by Langdon Down in 1866.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo104.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 7: Genetics and Evolution

explanation: An individual with Down's syndrome is short statured with a small round head, a furrowed tongue and partially open mouth, and a broad palm with a characteristic palm crease. Physical, psychomotor and mental development is retarded. Development of breasts (gynaecomastia) is a feature of Klinefelter's syndrome.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo104.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 7: Genetics and Evolution

explanation: Down's syndrome shows furrowed tongue and broad palm with a characteristic crease. Klinefelter's individuals have overall masculine development with gynaecomastia and are sterile. Turner's females are sterile with rudimentary ovaries and lack other secondary sexual characters. In phenylketonuria, phenylpyruvic acid and derivatives accumulate in the brain.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo104.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 7: Genetics and Evolution

correct_answer: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
explanation: Turner's syndrome is caused by the absence of one X chromosome, giving 45 with X0. Such females are sterile because their ovaries are rudimentary, and they lack other secondary sexual characters, so the Assertion is false.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo104.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 7: Genetics and Evolution

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
explanation: Klinefelter's syndrome, with karyotype 47, XXY, gives overall masculine development, although feminine development of breasts (gynaecomastia) is also expressed. Such individuals are sterile. Both statements are incorrect.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 7: Genetics and Evolution

explanation: Down's syndrome has trisomy of autosome 21, giving 47. Klinefelter's syndrome has an extra X, giving 47, XXY. Turner's syndrome lacks one X, giving 45 with X0. A normal male has 46 (44 + XY).
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo104.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 7: Genetics and Evolution

explanation: Cystic fibrosis is a Mendelian disorder determined by a single gene. Down's, Turner's and Klinefelter's syndromes are common examples of chromosomal disorders.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo104.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 7: Genetics and Evolution

correct_answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
explanation: An extra copy of a chromosome is trisomy and lack of one chromosome of a pair is monosomy. Aneuploidy is the gain or loss of a chromosome(s) due to failure of chromatid segregation; an increase in a whole set of chromosomes is polyploidy, due to failure of cytokinesis.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo104.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 7: Genetics and Evolution

explanation: A normal human gamete has 23 chromosomes; the abnormal gamete has 22. Their fusion gives 22 + 23 = 45 chromosomes, which lacks one chromosome of a pair, i.e. monosomy, as in Turner's syndrome (45 with X0).
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo104.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 7: Genetics and Evolution

correct_answer: All sons are colour blind, and all daughters have normal vision but are carriers
explanation: The woman has the recessive allele on both X chromosomes, so every child receives an X carrying it. Sons receive the father's Y and are colour blind. Daughters also receive the father's normal X, so they have normal vision but are carriers.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo104.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 7: Genetics and Evolution

explanation: A colour-blind woman carries the recessive allele on both X chromosomes, one of which came from her father. Since the father has only one X, he must be colour blind. A daughter will not normally be colour blind unless her mother is at least a carrier and her father is colour blind.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo104.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 7: Genetics and Evolution

explanation: The man must be IA i, since his mother could pass only i. The cross IA i x IA IB gives IA IA, IA IB, IA i and IB i in equal proportion: A 1/2, AB 1/4, B 1/4. The child is group B (IB i) with probability 1/4.

explanation: For each gene, the probability of showing the dominant trait is 3/4. With independent assortment, all three dominant = 3/4 x 3/4 x 3/4 = 27/64.

explanation: RR produces only R gametes; Rr produces R and r in equal proportion. The progeny are 1 RR (red) : 1 Rr (pink). No white plants appear, as no offspring can be rr.

explanation: A son receives his mother's X carrying the haemophilia allele with probability 1/2. Independently, any child is HbS HbS with probability 1/4. So a son with both disorders = 1/2 x 1/4 = 1/8.

explanation: The affected man is heterozygous and passes the dominant allele to half his gametes. The unaffected woman is homozygous recessive. Each child has a 1/2 probability of receiving the dominant allele and being affected.

explanation: For seed shape, Rr x rr gives 1/2 wrinkled. For seed colour, Yy x Yy gives 1/4 green. With independent assortment, wrinkled green = 1/2 x 1/4 = 1/8.

correct_answer: they remove nucleotides from the ends of DNA molecules

explanation: In 1963 two enzymes restricting phage growth in E. coli were isolated (one methylating DNA, one cutting it). Five years later Hind II, the first sequence-dependent restriction endonuclease, was characterised. Cohen and Boyer made the first rDNA in 1972. Today more than 900 enzymes from over 230 strains are known.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 9: Biotechnology and Its Applications

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 9: Biotechnology and Its Applications

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 9: Biotechnology and Its Applications

explanation: Each restriction enzyme inspects DNA until it finds its specific base sequence, the recognition sequence; it then binds and cuts. For Hind II this is a six base pair sequence.

correct_answer: Ori starts replication and controls copy number; the selectable marker helps identify and eliminate non-transformants
explanation: The ori is the sequence from where replication starts and it controls the copy number of linked DNA. The selectable marker, usually an antibiotic resistance gene, lets transformants grow and eliminates non-transformants.

correct_answer: each of the two strands at specific points in their sugar-phosphate backbones
explanation: A restriction endonuclease cuts each strand of the double helix at specific points in the sugar-phosphate backbone, that is, it breaks phosphodiester linkages, not hydrogen bonds.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo109.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 9: Biotechnology and Its Applications

correct_answer: A sequence of base pairs that reads the same on the two strands when the orientation of reading is kept the same
explanation: In DNA, a palindrome is a base pair sequence that reads the same on both strands when each is read in the same orientation, for example 5' GAATTC 3' on both strands. It is not a single-strand mirror like the word MALAYALAM.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo109.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 9: Biotechnology and Its Applications

explanation: The complementary strand of 5' GGATCC 3' is 3' CCTAGG 5', which read 5' to 3' is GGATCC, identical to the first strand. The other sequences give different complementary sequences when read in the same orientation.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo109.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 9: Biotechnology and Its Applications

correct_answer: a little away from the centre of the palindrome, but between the same two bases on the opposite strands
explanation: The cut is made a little away from the centre of the palindrome but between the same two bases on both strands. This staggered cut leaves single-stranded overhangs, the sticky ends.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo109.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 9: Biotechnology and Its Applications

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: The ends are named sticky because their single-stranded overhangs base pair by hydrogen bonds with complementary cut ends. This stickiness helps DNA ligase to join them.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo109.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 9: Biotechnology and Its Applications

correct_answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 9: Biotechnology and Its Applications

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Joining requires complementary overhangs. Cutting both vector and source DNA with the same enzyme produces matching sticky ends, which pair and are sealed by ligase. The Reason explains the Assertion.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 9: Biotechnology and Its Applications

correct_answer: Both fragments carry a single-stranded overhang reading 5' AATT 3'
explanation: Cutting between G and A on both strands leaves G on one side and AATTC on the other on each strand. Each fragment therefore has a four-base 5' overhang that reads AATT 5' to 3', and these overhangs are complementary to each other.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo109.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 9: Biotechnology and Its Applications

explanation: Cutting DNA at specific locations became possible with the discovery of 'molecular scissors', the restriction enzymes. Ligase joins fragments, while polymerase synthesises DNA.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 9: Biotechnology and Its Applications

correct_answer: anode, because DNA fragments are negatively charged

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 9: Biotechnology and Its Applications

correct_answer: Assertion is false, but Reason is true

correct_answer: bright orange bands under UV light after staining with ethidium bromide

correct_answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 9: Biotechnology and Its Applications

explanation: Agarose is the sea weed polymer that sieves fragments; ethidium bromide stains DNA; UV exposure makes the stained bands glow bright orange; elution is extraction of DNA from the excised bands.

correct_answer: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
explanation: For certain ecological investigations there is no need to know absolute densities; relative densities serve the purpose equally well, for example fish caught per trap. So the assertion is false and the reason is true.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

explanation: Population size, technically called population density (N), need not be measured in numbers only; per cent cover or biomass may be used. Total number is not easily adoptable when the population is huge and counting is impossible or very time-consuming. Population size can be estimated indirectly, without counting or seeing individuals, as in tiger census based on pug marks and fecal pellets.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: food availability, predation pressure and adverse weather
explanation: Population density changes with time depending on food availability, predation pressure and adverse weather, acting through births, deaths, immigration and emigration.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

explanation: Natality adds births, mortality removes deaths, immigration adds individuals of the same species coming from elsewhere, and emigration removes individuals leaving the habitat, each over the period under consideration.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Both are true. Births and deaths dominate under normal conditions, whereas immigration and emigration assume importance only under special conditions such as colonisation of a new habitat. The reason describes the normal case and does not explain the special case.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)

explanation: From Nt+1 = Nt + [(B + I) - (D + E)], if (B + I) equals (D + E) the bracket is zero and density stays the same despite turnover of individuals.

correct_answer: Density rises to 150, and immigration contributed more than births
explanation: Nt+1 = 100 + [(30 + 50) - (20 + 10)] = 150. In a newly colonised habitat immigration (50) contributed more to growth than births (30), as expected under such special conditions.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)

explanation: dN/dt = rN = 0.12 x 1000 = 120 individuals per unit time.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

explanation: r = b - d = 0.05 - 0.03 = 0.02; dN/dt = 0.02 x 5000 = 100 individuals per year.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

explanation: rt = 0.0693 x 10 = 0.693, so Nt = 1000 x e^0.693 = 1000 x 2 = 2000. Exponential growth compounds, unlike simple linear addition.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Both statements are true. r is important because it summarises the net per capita growth, allowing comparison of factors affecting growth. The 1981 Indian value is merely an example of r and does not explain its importance.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
