correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Since resources for most animal populations are finite and become limiting sooner or later, growth slows and levels off at K, as the logistic model describes. The reason explains the assertion.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
explanation: Logistic growth passes through lag, acceleration, deceleration and an asymptote at K. At carrying capacity no further growth is possible, so the reason is false.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

explanation: A population with limited resources shows a lag phase, then acceleration, then deceleration and finally an asymptote when density reaches carrying capacity, producing a sigmoid curve.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

explanation: dN/dt = 0.1 x 200 x (800/1000) = 20 x 0.8 = 16 individuals per unit time.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

explanation: dN/dt is proportional to N(K - N): 200 x 800 = 160000; 500 x 500 = 250000; 800 x 200 = 160000; 950 x 50 = 47500. The rate is greatest at N = 500.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

explanation: A plot of N against time under limited resources is sigmoid; this is Verhulst-Pearl logistic growth, dN/dt = rN((K - N)/K).
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
explanation: When N = K, (K - N)/K = 0, so dN/dt = 0 and growth stops at the asymptote. As N approaches K the term approaches 0, not 1; it is close to 1 only when N is very small.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: It approximates exponential growth, as (K - N)/K is close to 1
explanation: When N is much less than K, (K - N)/K is nearly 1, so dN/dt is nearly rN, the exponential form. Resistance to growth becomes important only as N approaches K.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: competition among individuals, with the fittest surviving and reproducing
explanation: Limited resources lead to competition between individuals; eventually the fittest individual survives and reproduces. Many governments have likewise introduced restraints to limit human population growth.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: Curve a is exponential with unlimited resources; the dashed line is K
explanation: When resources do not limit growth, the plot is exponential (J-shaped, curve a). When resources limit growth, the plot is logistic (sigmoid, curve b) and levels off at the carrying capacity K, shown as the dashed line.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

explanation: In dN/dt = (b - d) x N, b and d are per capita (not total) birth and death rates, and (b - d) = r. Nt = N0 e^rt is the integral form; the logistic equation includes the factor (K - N)/K.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: per capita birth rate minus per capita death rate
explanation: If b and d are per capita birth and death rates, then dN/dt = (b - d) x N; setting (b - d) = r gives dN/dt = rN.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

explanation: Some organisms such as Pacific salmon fish and bamboo breed only once in their lifetime, while most birds and mammals breed many times.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: Darwinian fitness, reflected in a high r value
explanation: Populations evolve to maximise reproductive fitness, also called Darwinian fitness (high r value), in their habitat. Under particular selection pressures, organisms evolve towards the most efficient reproductive strategy.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
explanation: Life history traits have evolved in relation to abiotic and biotic constraints of the habitat. Darwinian fitness corresponds to a high r value, not a low one.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: Oysters: small number of large-sized offspring
explanation: Oysters and pelagic fishes produce a large number of small-sized offspring; birds and mammals produce a small number of large-sized offspring. Pacific salmon fish and bamboo breed once; most birds and mammals breed many times.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
explanation: Oysters, like pelagic fishes, produce a large number of small-sized offspring, so statement I is wrong. Bamboo and Pacific salmon fish breed only once in their lifetime, so statement II is correct.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: needs soil microbes to return inorganic nutrients and animals for pollination
explanation: No natural habitat is inhabited by a single species. A plant needs soil microbes to break down organic matter and return inorganic nutrients for absorption, and usually an animal agent for pollination.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

explanation: Mutualism is (+, +), competition (-, -), commensalism (+, 0) and amensalism (-, 0). Predation and parasitism are both (+, -).
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

explanation: Predation, parasitism and commensalism share a common characteristic: the interacting species live closely together.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

explanation: Amensalism is (-, 0); predation and parasitism are (+, -); commensalism is (+, 0), so the second species is unaffected, not harmed. Interspecific interactions involve populations of two different species.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: Only one species benefits and the interaction harms the other
explanation: In both predation and parasitism only one species benefits (predator or parasite) and the interaction is detrimental to the other (prey or host); both are (+, -).
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: transferring to higher trophic levels the energy fixed by plants
explanation: Predation transfers the energy fixed by plants to higher trophic levels; predators act as conduits for energy transfer across trophic levels.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
explanation: A sparrow eating any seed is no less a predator than a tiger eating a deer. Although herbivores are categorised separately, in a broad ecological context they are not very different from predators. Both statements are incorrect.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

explanation: Pisaster is a predator of the rocky intertidal communities of the American Pacific Coast; prickly pear was introduced into Australia in the early 1920s and controlled by a moth; the Abingdon tortoise of the Galapagos became extinct after goats were introduced; Ophrys is a Mediterranean orchid using sexual deceit.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
explanation: Introduced exotic species often become invasive and spread fast because the invaded land does not have their natural predators, as with prickly pear in Australia. So the assertion is false and the reason is true.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: Predators maintain species diversity by reducing competition among prey species
explanation: After Pisaster was removed, more than 10 invertebrate species became extinct within a year because of interspecific competition. Predators help maintain species diversity in a community by reducing the intensity of competition among competing prey species.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Overexploitation of prey could drive the prey and then the predator itself to extinction. This is the reason why predators in nature are prudent, so the reason explains the assertion.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: during its caterpillar stage by feeding on a poisonous weed
explanation: The Monarch butterfly is distasteful to birds because of a special chemical that it acquires during its caterpillar stage by feeding on a poisonous weed.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
explanation: The Monarch butterfly acquires its chemical during the caterpillar stage by feeding on a poisonous weed, so statement I is wrong. Cryptic colouration in some insects and frogs is a valid anti-predator defence.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

explanation: Nearly 25 per cent of all insects are phytophagous. For plants, herbivores are the predators.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

explanation: Acacia (and Cactus) has thorns; Calotropis produces highly poisonous cardiac glycosides; the Monarch butterfly carries a distasteful chemical acquired from a poisonous weed; some insects and frogs are cryptically coloured.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
explanation: Cattle and goats avoid Calotropis because it produces highly poisonous cardiac glycosides, a chemical defence. Thorns are the defence cited for Acacia and Cactus, so the reason is false.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

explanation: Nicotine, caffeine, quinine, strychnine and opium are produced by plants as defences against grazers and browsers. Penicillin is an antibiotic produced by a fungus, not a plant defence chemical.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Because plants cannot run away from their predators, herbivory is particularly severe for them; therefore plants have evolved an astonishing variety of morphological and chemical defences.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

explanation: Predators transfer energy across trophic levels, keep prey populations under control, form the basis of biological control, and maintain species diversity by reducing (not increasing) competition among prey species.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: the ability of a predator to regulate its prey population
explanation: Biological control methods adopted in agricultural pest control are based on the ability of the predator to regulate the prey population, as seen when a cactus-feeding moth controlled prickly pear in Australia.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

explanation: Flamingoes and fishes are unrelated species competing for zooplankton; the Abingdon tortoise became extinct after goats were introduced; Connell showed Balanus excluding Chathamalus from the intertidal area; MacArthur's five warblers coexisted by resource partitioning.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
explanation: Resources need not be limiting for competition to occur; in interference competition one species reduces the feeding efficiency of the other even when food and space are abundant. So statement I is incorrect and statement II is correct.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: the fitness of one species (its r) is significantly lower in the presence of another
explanation: Since unrelated species can compete and resources need not be limiting, competition is best defined as a process in which the fitness of one species (measured by r, the intrinsic rate of increase) is significantly lower in the presence of another species.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

explanation: Gause gave the competitive exclusion principle; Connell performed field experiments on barnacles in Scotland; MacArthur showed resource partitioning among five warbler species; Darwin was convinced that interspecific competition is a potent force in organic evolution.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
explanation: Connell showed that the larger, competitively superior Balanus dominates the intertidal area and excludes the smaller Chathamalus. The assertion reverses the roles and is false; the reason is true.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
explanation: Herbivores and plants appear more adversely affected by competition than carnivores. Gause's principle may be true if resources are limiting, but not otherwise, so statement II is incorrect.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

explanation: Gause's principle states that the inferior competitor is eventually eliminated, but evidence in nature is not always conclusive. Recent studies show that competing species may evolve co-existence mechanisms, such as resource partitioning through different feeding times or foraging patterns.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: They avoid competition through resource partitioning
explanation: MacArthur showed that five closely related warbler species living on the same tree avoided competition and co-existed due to behavioural differences in foraging, a mechanism called resource partitioning.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Both statements are true: exclusion is relatively easy to demonstrate in the laboratory with limited resources, while evidence from nature is not always conclusive. The second statement contrasts with the first rather than explaining it.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

explanation: Competitive release is evidence for competition in nature: a species restricted by a competitively superior species expands its distributional range dramatically when the competitor is removed.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: co-evolve, each countering the other's mechanisms
explanation: Host-specific parasites and their hosts co-evolve: if the host evolves mechanisms to reject or resist the parasite, the parasite must evolve mechanisms to counteract and neutralise them to succeed with the same host species.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

explanation: Parasites show loss of unnecessary sense organs, adhesive organs or suckers, loss of digestive system and high (not low) reproductive capacity.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

explanation: The human liver fluke (a trematode) depends on two intermediate hosts, a snail and a fish; the malarial parasite needs a mosquito vector; Cuscuta has lost chlorophyll and leaves and parasitises hedge plants; lice are ectoparasites of humans.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
explanation: Endoparasites have complex life cycles owing to extreme specialisation, but their morphological and anatomical features are greatly simplified while their reproductive potential is emphasised. The assertion is false; the reason is true.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
explanation: Ectoparasites feed on the external surface of the host; lice on humans and ticks on dogs are the most familiar examples, and many marine fish carry ectoparasitic copepods. Both statements are correct.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: It is not considered a parasite, although it needs our blood for reproduction
explanation: The female mosquito needs human blood for reproduction but is not considered a parasite; it serves as a vector for the malarial parasite.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

explanation: Ticks on dogs are ectoparasites; the human liver fluke lives inside the host as an endoparasite; the cuckoo (koel) is a brood parasite laying eggs in the crow's nest; the mosquito is the vector of the malarial parasite.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
explanation: The parasitic bird lays its eggs in the host's nest and lets the host incubate them. The eggs resemble the host's eggs in size and colour to reduce the chance of the host detecting and ejecting them, so the reason is false.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

explanation: The majority of parasites harm the host: they may reduce its survival, growth and reproduction, reduce its population density and make it physically weak and more vulnerable to predation. Natural selection has not led to totally harmless parasites.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

explanation: In commensalism one species benefits and the other is neither harmed nor benefited: epiphytic orchid on mango, barnacles on a whale, cattle egret with grazing cattle, and clown fish with sea anemone. The whale and the anemone derive no apparent benefit.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

explanation: Thorns (Acacia, Cactus) are the most common morphological means of defence, not chemical. The other three statements correctly describe prey and plant chemical defences.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

explanation: The epiphytic orchid on mango is commensalism; fig and wasp are mutualists; the cuckoo shows brood parasitism; Balanus and Chathamalus compete, with Balanus excluding Chathamalus.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: the moving cattle stir up and flush out insects from the vegetation
explanation: The cattle, as they move, stir up and flush out insects from vegetation that might otherwise be difficult for egrets to find and catch. Egrets benefit and cattle are unaffected: a classic example of commensalism.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
explanation: The clown fish lives among the stinging tentacles of the sea anemone and gets protection from predators. The anemone does not appear to derive any benefit, so this is commensalism. Both statements are incorrect.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

explanation: Lichens are an intimate mutualistic relationship between a fungus and photosynthesising algae or cyanobacteria. The other three are commensal associations in which one partner benefits and the other is unaffected.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

explanation: Lichens are fungus with algae or cyanobacteria; mycorrhizae are fungi with roots of higher plants; many fig species have a one-to-one relationship with a pollinator wasp; Ophrys is pollinated by a male bee through sexual deceit.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: the fungi help in absorbing nutrients, and the plant supplies carbohydrates
explanation: In mycorrhizae, associations between fungi and roots of higher plants, the fungi help the plant absorb essential nutrients from the soil while the plant provides the fungi with energy-yielding carbohydrates.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Both are true. Plants pay fees to animals: pollen and nectar for pollinators and juicy, nutritious fruits for seed dispersers. The fig wasp feeding its larvae on developing seeds is a separate pollination mutualism and does not explain why fruits reward seed dispersers.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
explanation: Many fig species have a tight one-to-one relationship with their pollinator wasp. The female wasp uses the fruit as an oviposition site and pollinates the inflorescence while searching for egg-laying sites; in return the fig offers some developing seeds as food for wasp larvae.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

explanation: One petal of Ophrys resembles the female bee; the male bee is attracted, pseudocopulates and is dusted with pollen; when it pseudocopulates with another flower it transfers pollen and pollinates that flower.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Ophrys relies on sexual deceit: a petal mimics the female bee. If the female bee's patterns change, the mimicry fails and pollination success falls unless the orchid co-evolves. The reason explains the assertion and shows co-evolution at work.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

explanation: Plants reward pollinators with pollen and nectar and must guard against nectar thieves; many orchid floral patterns attract the right bees and bumblebees. Not all orchids offer rewards: Ophrys uses sexual deceit.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo111.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

explanation: Crop fields and an aquarium are considered man-made ecosystems. Estuary and wetland are natural aquatic ecosystems, and grassland is a natural terrestrial ecosystem.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo112.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: A global ecosystem that is a composite of all local ecosystems on Earth
explanation: The biosphere is regarded as a global ecosystem, a composite of all the local ecosystems on Earth. Because it is too big and complex to study as one unit, it is divided into terrestrial and aquatic categories.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo112.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

explanation: Desert is a terrestrial ecosystem, estuary is an aquatic ecosystem, a crop field is a man-made ecosystem and the biosphere is regarded as the global ecosystem.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo112.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: Vertical distribution of different species occupying different levels
explanation: Vertical distribution of different species occupying different levels is called stratification. Identification and enumeration of species gives species composition, which is a different structural feature.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo112.pdf)
source_page: NCERT section: Ecosystem: Structure and Function
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

explanation: In a forest, trees occupy the top vertical stratum, shrubs the second, and herbs and grasses occupy the bottom layers.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo112.pdf)
source_page: NCERT section: Ecosystem: Structure and Function
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
explanation: Species composition and stratification are the two main structural features of an ecosystem. Identification and enumeration of species gives species composition; stratification is the vertical distribution of species at different levels.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo112.pdf)
source_page: NCERT section: Ecosystem: Structure and Function
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

explanation: Productivity, decomposition, energy flow and nutrient cycling are the functional aspects of an ecosystem. Stratification is a structural feature, along with species composition.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo112.pdf)
source_page: NCERT section: Ecosystem: Structure and Function
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: A pond is a shallow water body in which all four basic components of an ecosystem, the abiotic components, producers, consumers and decomposers, are well exhibited. This makes it a simple, self-sustainable and convenient example for understanding ecosystem structure and function.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo112.pdf)
source_page: NCERT section: Ecosystem: Structure and Function
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

explanation: In a pond, the abiotic component is water with dissolved inorganic and organic substances and the rich soil deposit at the bottom. Autotrophs are phytoplankton, some algae and floating, submerged and marginal plants. Consumers are zooplankton and free swimming and bottom dwelling forms. Decomposers are fungi, bacteria and flagellates.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo112.pdf)
source_page: NCERT section: Ecosystem: Structure and Function
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

explanation: Fungi, bacteria and flagellates, the decomposers of a pond, are especially abundant in the bottom of the pond, where dead organic matter settles along with the soil deposit.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo112.pdf)
source_page: NCERT section: Ecosystem: Structure and Function
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

explanation: The solar input, the cycle of temperature, day-length and other climatic conditions regulate the rate of function of the entire pond. Zooplankton are biotic consumers, not a physical climatic factor.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo112.pdf)
source_page: NCERT section: Ecosystem: Structure and Function
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

explanation: A pond converts inorganic into organic material using solar energy, heterotrophs consume autotrophs, and dead organic matter is decomposed and mineralised for reuse by autotrophs. Energy moves unidirectionally towards higher trophic levels and is dissipated as heat; it does not return to autotrophs.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo112.pdf)
source_page: NCERT section: Ecosystem: Structure and Function
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: Inorganic nutrients from dead organic matter
explanation: Decomposition and mineralisation of dead organic matter release inorganic nutrients that are reused by autotrophs. Energy, in contrast, flows in one direction and is lost as heat, so it is not reused.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo112.pdf)
source_page: NCERT section: Ecosystem: Structure and Function
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: Species composition concerns which species are present and how many, whereas stratification concerns their vertical distribution
explanation: Identification and enumeration of plant and animal species gives species composition. Vertical distribution of species occupying different levels is stratification, for example trees, shrubs, and herbs and grasses in a forest.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo112.pdf)
source_page: NCERT section: Ecosystem: Structure and Function
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

explanation: An ecosystem comprises abiotic and biotic components. Abiotic components are inorganic materials such as air, water and soil, whereas biotic components are producers, consumers and decomposers.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo112.pdf)
source_page: NCERT section: Ecosystem: Structure and Function
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: Amount of biomass produced per unit area over a time period by plants during photosynthesis
explanation: Primary production is the amount of biomass or organic matter produced per unit area over a time period by plants during photosynthesis. It is expressed as weight (g m^-2) or energy (kcal m^-2).
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo112.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: g m^-2 yr^-1 or kcal m^-2 yr^-1
explanation: Productivity is the rate of biomass production and is expressed as g m^-2 yr^-1 or kcal m^-2 yr^-1 so that ecosystems can be compared. Production itself, without the time rate, is expressed as g m^-2 or kcal m^-2.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo112.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo112.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

explanation: If respiration is 40 per cent of GPP, NPP is 60 per cent of GPP. So GPP = 1200 / 0.6 = 2000 g m^-2 yr^-1. Respiration is 800 and 2000 - 800 = 1200.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo112.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

explanation: GPP minus respiration losses is NPP, and NPP is the biomass available for consumption by heterotrophs, that is, herbivores and decomposers.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo112.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: Formation of new organic matter by consumers
explanation: Secondary productivity is the rate of formation of new organic matter by consumers, that is, the rate of assimilation of food energy by consumers. Production of organic matter by plants is primary productivity.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo112.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: 170 billion tons dry weight of organic matter
explanation: The annual NPP of the whole biosphere is approximately 170 billion tons (dry weight) of organic matter, of which the oceans contribute only 55 billion tons; the rest is on land.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo112.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

explanation: Biosphere annual NPP is about 170 billion tons and oceans contribute about 55 billion tons. Land therefore contributes about 170 - 55 = 115 billion tons dry weight.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo112.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: About 32 per cent of NPP from about 70 per cent of the surface
explanation: Oceans produce about 55 of the 170 billion tons of annual NPP, which is about 32 per cent, although they cover about 70 per cent of the surface. Ocean productivity per unit area is therefore low.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo112.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Primary productivity depends on the plant species, a variety of environmental factors, nutrient availability and the photosynthetic capacity of plants; therefore it varies among ecosystems. The reason explains the assertion.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo112.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: Assertion is true, but Reason is false
explanation: NPP is the biomass available to heterotrophs, so the assertion is true. NPP is GPP minus respiration losses, so it excludes the organic matter used in plant respiration; the reason is false.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo112.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
explanation: Primary production, an amount produced per unit area over a time period, is expressed as weight (g m^-2) or energy (kcal m^-2). The rate of biomass production is productivity, expressed per year.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo112.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

explanation: GPP is the rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis; NPP is GPP minus respiration losses; secondary productivity is the rate of formation of new organic matter by consumers; primary production is the amount of biomass produced per unit area over a time period by plants.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo112.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

explanation: Productivity is a rate per unit area, and NPP = GPP - R. Secondary productivity refers to consumers, not producers. Oceans contribute only about 55 of the 170 billion tons of annual NPP, so most NPP is on land.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo112.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: Organic matter produced by producers per square metre per year
explanation: Productivity is the rate of biomass production, expressed as g m^-2 yr^-1 or kcal m^-2 yr^-1, which allows ecosystems of different sizes to be compared. Biomass present at one time is the standing crop, not productivity.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo112.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: Their primary productivity may still differ
explanation: Standing crop is the mass of living material at a particular time, while productivity is a rate of production per unit area per unit time. Equal standing crops can arise from different rates of production and loss, so productivity may differ.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo112.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
explanation: Gross primary productivity is the rate of production of biomass, or organic matter, during photosynthesis; the biomass remaining after respiration losses is net primary productivity. Secondary productivity is the rate of formation of new organic matter by consumers. Only Statement II is correct.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo112.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

explanation: Trees occupy the top vertical stratum of a forest, shrubs the second, and herbs and grasses occupy the bottom layers.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo112.pdf)
source_page: NCERT section: Ecosystem: Structure and Function
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: Relatively little biomass is available to herbivores and decomposers
explanation: NPP = GPP - R. A large respiratory loss leaves a small NPP, and NPP is the biomass available to herbivores and decomposers. NPP can never exceed GPP.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo112.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: Assertion is false, but Reason is true
explanation: An aquarium, like a crop field, may be considered a man-made ecosystem, because organisms in it interact with each other and with the physical environment. The assertion is false and the reason is true.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo112.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

explanation: Pond, lake, wetland, river and estuary are aquatic ecosystems, whereas forest, grassland and desert are terrestrial ecosystems.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo112.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: Detritivore that breaks detritus into smaller particles
explanation: Detritivores such as the earthworm break down detritus into smaller particles, a process called fragmentation. Enzymatic degradation of detritus is catabolism, carried out by bacteria and fungi.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo112.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

explanation: Decomposers break down complex organic matter into inorganic substances like carbon dioxide, water and nutrients; this process is decomposition.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo112.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

explanation: Fragmentation is by detritivores; leaching carries water-soluble inorganic nutrients down into the soil horizon where they precipitate as unavailable salts; catabolism is enzymatic degradation by bacteria and fungi; mineralisation releases inorganic nutrients from humus.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo112.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Humus is a dark coloured, amorphous substance. Being colloidal in nature, it serves as a reservoir of nutrients, so the reason explains the assertion.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo112.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
explanation: Humification leads to accumulation of a dark coloured amorphous substance, humus, which is highly resistant to microbial action and decomposes extremely slowly. It is not light coloured or crystalline and is not formed by leaching.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo112.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: Soluble nutrients going down the soil and precipitating as unavailable salts
explanation: By leaching, water-soluble inorganic nutrients go down into the soil horizon and get precipitated as unavailable salts.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo112.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: The steps can operate simultaneously on the detritus
explanation: Fragmentation, leaching and catabolism all operate simultaneously on the detritus, while humification and mineralisation occur during decomposition in the soil. They are not strictly sequential stages.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo112.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

explanation: In a particular climatic condition, decomposition is slower if detritus is rich in lignin and chitin, and quicker if it is rich in nitrogen and water-soluble substances like sugars.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo112.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: Leaf litter rich in nitrogen and sugars
explanation: When climatic conditions are the same, the rate of decomposition depends on the chemical composition of detritus. Detritus rich in nitrogen and water-soluble substances like sugars decomposes quickly, whereas lignin and chitin slow it.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo112.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation: Warm and moist conditions favour decomposition because temperature and soil moisture affect the activities of soil microbes. Lignin and chitin slowing decomposition is a true statement about chemical composition, a separate factor, so it does not explain the assertion.
source_document: NCERT Biology Textbook for Class XII, Revised Edition November 2022, Reprint 2026-27 (lebo112.pdf)
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Biology syllabus, Unit 10: Ecology and Environment

correct_answer: Assertion is false, but Reason is true

explanation: Sacred groves are tracts of forest set aside where all trees and wildlife are venerated and given total protection. Since organisms are protected in their natural habitat, this is in situ, not ex situ, conservation.

explanation: Ex situ approaches include zoological parks, botanical gardens and wildlife safari parks, cryopreservation of gametes with in vitro fertilisation, tissue culture propagation and seed banks. Biosphere reserves protect species in their natural habitat, which is in situ.
